articles.title: Dinagat Islands residents protest Tubajon mining plan
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO, AGUSAN DEL SUR, Philippines — Residents of Barangay Navarro in Tubajon, Dinagat Islands, protested against a proposed mining project in their village, calling for greater protection of…

blocks.text: SAN FRANCISCO, AGUSAN DEL SUR, Philippines — Residents of Barangay Navarro in Tubajon, Dinagat Islands, protested against a proposed mining project in their village, calling for greater protection of local watersheds as the province grapples with a prolonged water crisis.

The protest was held outside the Navarro Barangay Hall on Aug. 27, where a meeting initiated by the Tubajon People’s Council was expected to bring together five barangay leaders, representatives of the proponent company and other officials to discuss how to manage the impact of the planned extractive operation.

Residents said they feared the plan could be endorsed without affected communities first being given enough opportunity to examine its contents. They raised concerns over the possible effects of mining on the Navarro and Imelda watersheds, nearby farms, coastal waters and fishing communities.
The meeting eventually did not push through.

Residents said their concerns had become more urgent because Dinagat Islands was already under a state of calamity due to a severe water shortage brought about by a prolonged dry spell. Around 18,000 people have been affected or placed at risk, while some communities have reportedly endured water shortages for about three months now.
They called for public consultations in all affected barangays, disclosure of the IMP and related documents, and protection of the remaining watersheds in Navarro and Imelda.

The Tubajon protest came as Dinagat Islands Rep. Kaka Bag-ao and Association of Philippine Electric Cooperatives party-list Rep. Sergio Dagooc, a Dinagat Islands resident, separately raised mining concerns involving Gibusong Island in the neighboring municipality of Loreto during a House budget hearing involving the Department of Environment and Natural Resources.

Both lawmakers urged the Mines and Geosciences Bureau to permanently trash the disputed mining applications in Loreto instead of merely suspending them, saying suspension could leave open the possibility that the applications may later be revived.
Bag-ao said the call for banning mining in the town was especially important because the province was already facing a severe water crisis affecting thousands of residents.

DENR officials committed to strengthen monitoring of mining activities in Dinagat Islands, visit Gibusong Island and meet affected communities, prevent mining in the Bonsai Forest in Mt. Redondo, and assign personnel to closely monitor mining areas.
The DENR also said Gibusong Island, which covers Barangays Helen, Liberty and Magsaysay in Loreto, could eventually be declared a “no-mining” area following proper assessment.
Residents in Navarro, meanwhile, vowed to continue monitoring developments and pressing government officials for transparency before any mining-related endorsement is made. /cb

articles.title: Ex-vice mayor Mangubat concedes Dasmariñas congressional race
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Former Dasmariñas Vice Mayor Raul Rex Rosario Mangubat on Saturday night conceded defeat to incumbent Mayor Jennifer “Jenny” Barzaga in the special congressional race for…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Former Dasmariñas Vice Mayor Raul Rex Rosario Mangubat on Saturday night conceded defeat to incumbent Mayor Jennifer “Jenny” Barzaga in the special congressional race for Cavite’s 4th District.

Mangubat conceded as partial and unofficial votes as of 8:30 p.m. showed Barzaga leading the congressional race at 185,668 votes—reflecting ballots from 41.50 percent of registered voters in the city.
The former vice mayor placed second, albeit by a significant margin, garnering only 23,208 votes so far.

“Tapos na ang halalan, at malinaw na ang naging pasya ng ating mga kababayan. Buong puso kong binabati si Jenny Barzaga. Ipinagkatiwala sa iyo ng mga Dasmarineño ang kanilang boto, pag-asa, at kinabukasan,” said Mangubat in a statement.

(The election is over, and the decision of our countrymen is clear. I wholeheartedly congratulate Jenny Barzaga. The people of Dasmarineños have entrusted you with their votes, their hopes, and their future.)
“Ang demokrasya ay hindi lamang tungkol sa ating karapatang pumili. Ito rin ay tungkol sa kababaang-loob na tanggapin at igalang ang pasya ng nakararami,” he added.
(Democracy is not just about our right to choose. It is also about the humility to accept and respect the decision of the majority.)
Mangubat then thanked his supporters, assuring them that their efforts were not wasted as they were able to prove that it was possible to lead an electoral campaign cleanly and honorably.

“Ngayong tapos na ang halalan, panahon na upang isantabi ang kulay at pagkakaiba. lisa lamang ang lungsod na ating mahal at iisa ang tagumpay na dapat nating hangarin ang pag-unlad ng bawat Dasmarineño,” he further said.
(Now that the elections are over, it’s time to put aside color and differences. There is only one city we love and one success we should strive for: the development of every Dasmarineño.)
Dasmariñas makes up the entire 4th District of Cavite, having 447,387 registered voters from 75 barangays.

Should Barzaga bag the Congressional seat, she will replace her son, Francisco “Kiko” Barzaga, who was expelled from his post by the House of Representatives last June 2 for “disruptive” and “disorderly” behavior.

This also effectively means the Barzagas’ hold on Dasmariñas as a political dynasty will continue, extending their political dominance in the city to nearly three decades since Elpidio “Pidi” Barzaga Jr. first became mayor in 1998. /cb

articles.title: Public warned vs fake news as AFP bares foreign influence in VP trial
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The House prosecution team has warned Filipinos against falling for fake news surrounding the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, amid an Armed Forces of the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The House prosecution team has warned Filipinos against falling for fake news surrounding the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, amid an Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) disclosure that foreign malign influence operations are increasingly riding on local controversies, including the impeachment and flood-control issues.

Prosecution team adviser and spokesperson Robert Ace Barbers urged the public to scrutinize information circulating online and, whenever possible, go directly to the evidence being presented before the Senate impeachment court.

“Every day may fake news,” Barbers said, describing the steady stream of online narratives targeting members of Congress who endorsed the impeachment. He said that when critics cannot answer issues on substance, they resort to personally attacking those raising the questions.

His warning came after retired Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad, AFP spokesperson on the West Philippine Sea, said malign information operations have increasingly shifted from traditional pro-Davao and pro-China narratives to domestic controversies.
“Ngayon, mas mahirap ma-detect sapagkat impeachment sumasabay d’yan, Sanjia sumasabay d’yan, and other local issues; flood control sumasabay d’yan,” Trinidad said.
Trinidad said the pattern involves taking advantage of local issues and twisting narratives to favor China while attacking government officials who stand up on these issues.
He said such influence operations seek to shape public perception without the use of conventional military force.

AFP spokesperson Col. Francel Padilla said the military is monitoring developments in the information space and coordinating with other government agencies to determine the facts behind issues being circulated online.
Greatest weapon
“Our greatest weapon is the truth,” Padilla said, explaining that AFP intelligence and cyber units work together to establish facts and provide the public with information anchored on empirical data.

The two military officials also said the West Philippine Sea should unite Filipinos across political, regional, and religious lines as foreign malign influence operations expand from maritime disputes into domestic issues and social-media feeds.
For Barbers, the revelation makes it even more important for Filipinos to personally follow the impeachment proceedings and distinguish evidence from online narratives.

“Ang panawagan namin palagi sa ating mga kababayan, Kung maaari, subaybayan ninyo. Pakinggan ninyo at dinggin ninyo ’yung ebidensyang inilalatag. Nang sa ganu’n, ay maiwasan natin ’yung maniwala tayo sa fake news,” he said.
Barbers said the prosecution’s message is not to dismiss criticism or opposing views, but to ensure that the public has access to the facts and evidence needed to make its own judgment.
“Ebidensya ang dapat maging pakinggan,” Barbers said, stressing that the impeachment should not be reduced to a contest between personalities or political camps.
Barbers said the impeachment process is ultimately about accountability under the Constitution, not personalities or political camps.
“At the end of the day, ang mahalaga ho dito ay ang ating konstitusyon, ang ating saligang batas. Meron pong tinatawag na accountability mekanismo,” he said. /cb

articles.title: MILF candidate to seek SC relief after Comelec cancels candidacy
articles.summary: COTABATO CITY, BARMM, Philippines — The camp of Anwar Alamada, a candidate for district representative of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) in Maguindanao del Sur’s fifth parliamentary…

blocks.text: COTABATO CITY, BARMM, Philippines — The camp of Anwar Alamada, a candidate for district representative of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) in Maguindanao del Sur’s fifth parliamentary district, disqualified by the Commission on Elections (Comelec), is bringing his case to the Supreme Court.

Lawyer Badrodin Mangindra, Alamada’s lawyer, said they followed the process, filing an appeal before the Comelec en banc after its Second Division cancelled his candidacy in the Sept. 14 Bangsamoro parliamentary elections.
But the Comelec en banc affirmed the second division’s cancellation.
Alamada is an official candidate of the MILF’s United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP) and served in the erstwhile rebel group’s ceasefire panel mediating warring families and field commanders.
In a resolution promulgated on Thursday, Aug. 27, the Comelec en banc said Alamada failed to prove that he is a resident of Barangay Kudal, Pagalungan, Maguindanao del Sur.
Rafsanjani Ali, a candidate for the same seat under the rival Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), challenged Alamada’s candidacy, claiming he misrepresented his residency.
Ali said in his complaint that Alamada falsely declared that he is a resident of Barangay Kudal for the past 49 years.
On July 7, Alamada filed a motion to overturn the ruling, but the division denied Alamada’s attempt to introduce new evidence in his motion.
Despite the ruling disqualifying him in next month’s balloting, Alamada continued his campaign sortie along with the UBJP candidates in Buluan, Maguindanao del Sur on Friday, Aug. 28.
With Alamada’s candidacy cancelled, the lone seat in Maguindanao Sur’s 5th parliamentary district will be contested by Ali and Nasser Guialal Dalgan of Bangsamoro Party (BAPA).

Maguindanao del Sur 5th parliamentary district is composed of the towns of Datu Montawal, Gen. Salipada K. Pendatun, Pagalungan, Rajah Buayan, Sultan sa Barongis and Paglat, with 114,737 registered voters.

The poll body also cancelled the registration and accreditation of Moro Ako Party as a Regional Parliamentary Political Party (RPPP) after finding out it made untruthful representations about having established chapters throughout the region, which were required for accreditation.
A certain Aladin Abdul filed the petition to cancel Moro Ako Party’s registration with the poll body.
In a statement, a member of Moro Ako Party shared with local media that it would bring the matter to the Supreme Court and that it continues its campaign activities. /cb

articles.title: Beyond the beaches: The story Panglao tells through Hudyaka Festival 2026
articles.summary: PANGLAO, BOHOL, Philippines — The streets of this tourist town came alive on Friday, Aug. 28, as 10 barangays showcased their culture, traditions and faith through the Hudyaka sa Panglao Festival…

blocks.text: PANGLAO, BOHOL, Philippines — The streets of this tourist town came alive on Friday, Aug. 28, as 10 barangays showcased their culture, traditions and faith through the Hudyaka sa Panglao Festival 2026.

Known as a major tourism destination in Bohol, Panglao is famous for its white-sand beaches, clear waters and dive sites. But during the annual festival, residents showed that the town’s attractions go beyond its natural wonders.
The festival’s main events—the street dancing and ritual showdown—featured performances inspired by the history, livelihood, food and communities of Panglao.
The contingents highlighted stories from their respective barangays, including fishing, tuba gathering, local products and tourist destinations.

Barangay Poblacion paid tribute to pan pati, a popular local bread, through its performance. The presentation honored the people who started making the bread and the generations that kept the tradition alive.

Barangay Danao, meanwhile, presented a story of perseverance through a working student who finished his studies, found a job and eventually fulfilled his dream of providing a home for his father, with faith in St. Augustine playing an important role in his journey.
The performances drew residents, tourists and expatriates who lined the streets to watch the colorful costumes, elaborate props and synchronized dances accompanied by drums and native gongs.
Danao won the street dancing competition, followed by Bil-isan in second place and Poblacion in third.

Poblacion won the ritual showdown, with Bil-isan placing second and Danao third. Poblacion also received Best in Choreography and Best in Costumes. Tangnan won Best in Andas (processional carriage), while Danao received Best in Musicality.

blocks.caption: Performers bring energy, color, and rhythm to the Hudyaka sa Panglao 2026 Street Dancing Competition on Friday, August 28, in Panglao town, Bohol.

blocks.text: For 17-year-old Poblacion performer Gwenn Balbiran, the weeks of nightly rehearsals were worth the effort.
“We offer our dance to Saint Augustine, and for our love of Panglao,” she said.
Kyla Tiempo, 20, another Poblacion dancer, said their performance was an expression of their faith.
“This is our devotion to God and our patron Saint Augustine,” she said.
Rooted in faith
Hudyaka sa Panglao, which means merrymaking in Cebuano, was first held in 1987 as part of the town’s annual fiesta in honor of St. Augustine of Hippo. It is the oldest festival in the province.
According to co-founder Rosario Estoquia, the festival has continued to grow each year, becoming bigger and more colorful while maintaining its connection to the community.
The celebration was held online in 2020 and 2021 because of the COVID-19 pandemic. It returned to the streets in 2022.
Panglao’s contingent has also competed in the Sinulog Festival in Cebu, where it won a competition.
Mayor Edgardo Arcay said Hudyaka helps strengthen unity among residents while promoting Panglao as a tourist destination.
“This festival is about celebrating who we are as Panglaonons—our culture, our heritage, our devotion, and our gratitude to our patron Saint Augustine,” Arcay said.
He said the festival also reminds residents to protect Panglao’s natural and cultural treasures for future generations.
Panglao has experienced rapid growth as a tourism destination. Once a fourth-class municipality, it became a first-class municipality in 2022, largely due to the expansion of tourism.

blocks.caption: Saint Augustine of Hippo, patron saint of Panglao, Bohol

blocks.text: The Bohol-Panglao International Airport has helped make the town a major gateway to the province.
Panglao recorded around a million tourists in 2024 and more than 500,000 visitors during the first half of 2026, according to the local government.
The growth, however, has brought environmental challenges, including coral vandalism and the impact of mass tourism on the island’s natural resources.
Apart from its beaches, Panglao also has important cultural heritage sites.

The Panglao Parish Church of Saint Augustine, completed in 1924 under Bishop Juan Gorordo, is one of the town’s major landmarks. The church features Corinthian columns, ceiling paintings and machuca tile flooring.
The church was declared an Important Cultural Property in 2011 and sustained minimal damage during the 2013 Bohol earthquake.
Five cultural property markers were installed at the church complex by the National Museum of the Philippines in 2023.

Panglao’s tourism attractions also include Balicasag Island, known for its coral walls and marine life; Virgin Island, popular among snorkelers; and South Farm in Barangay Bolod, which features organic farming and tourism activities.
Through Hudyaka, Panglao continues to promote not only its beaches and tourism industry but also the faith, traditions, and stories that form part of its identity. /cb

articles.title: Nepal flood death toll rises to 675
articles.summary: KATHMANDU – Devastating floods near the border with China this week have killed at least 675 people in Nepal, the Himalayan nation’s disaster authority said on Saturday. Chinese state…

image.caption: A woman points at damaged houses across the Trishuli river in the aftermath of flash floods at Devighat in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 29, 2026. (AFP)

blocks.text: KATHMANDU – Devastating floods near the border with China this week have killed at least 675 people in Nepal, the Himalayan nation’s disaster authority said on Saturday.
Chinese state media earlier confirmed seven dead in Tibet following Wednesday’s disaster, taking the total killed to 682.
The number of missing in Nepal remained constant at 2,426, after a sharp hike in numbers on Saturday morning.

That missing list includes 517 foreigners, as well as 933 workers on hydropower projects on the river where the torrent smashed down, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.
The number of missing also includes 45 Nepali Army soldiers, 40 police officers, and 19 immigration and customs officers.
In India, authorities said they had recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims. However, they are not included in the toll.

articles.title: Zimbabwe crash involving church minibus kills 27
articles.summary: Dozens of people were killed when a minibus carrying churchgoers collided head-on with a truck in central Zimbabwe. The crash near the town of Chivhu is the latest deadly road accident in the African…

image.caption: The accident occurred on Friday about 87 miles south of the capital Harare [FILE: April 20, 2020]Image: Zinyange Auntony/AFP

blocks.text: At least 27 people were killed in a minibus crash in central Zimbabwe after the vehicle carrying churchgoers collided head-on with a truck, police said Saturday. Seven people were injured.

Police spokesperson Paul Nyathi said members of a popular Indigenous African Christian denomination, known for wearing white robes, were traveling to a conference on Friday when their minibus collided with a truck on a major highway near the town of Chivhu, about 140 kilometers (87 miles) south of the capital, Harare.
The foreign-registered haulage truck was overtaking another vehicle when it collided with the minibus. Both vehicles were carrying an "unspecified" number of passengers, Nyathi said in a statement.
Footage shared on social media by public broadcaster ZBC showed the mangled minibus charred to a shell.
Zimbabwe faces road safety crisis

Authorities say 94% of road accidents occur due to human error. Many Zimbabweans rely on privately operated minibus taxis, known locally as kombis, for everyday transportation. The vehicles are often criticized for carrying more passengers than allowed.
Zimbabwe’s roads are also riddled with potholes after years of underfunding and neglect, while driving standards can be poor.

In April, at least 18 people were killed when a minibus burst into flames on a highway in southern Zimbabwe. Earlier that month, a woman and her five children were killed when their vehicle collided with a haulage truck on another highway linking Zimbabwe and South Africa.

blocks.caption: Rescue personnel work at the site of a bus accident on a major highway near Harare [FILE: January 18, 2015]Image: Xinhua/imago images

blocks.text: Road crashes kill about 300,000 people across Africa each year, accounting for roughly a quarter of the global road death toll, according to the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa. The continent has the world’s highest road fatality rate, the commission says.
This is despite Africa’s 1.5 billion people accounting for only about 3% of the world’s vehicle fleet.

articles.title: Barbers: There should be no double standard in enforcing sub judice rule
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – No one should get special treatment under the sub judice rule governing Vice President Sara Z. Duterte’s impeachment trial, House impeachment team adviser and spokesperson…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – No one should get special treatment under the sub judice rule governing Vice President Sara Z. Duterte’s impeachment trial, House impeachment team adviser and spokesperson robert Ace Barbers said Saturday.

“Kung talagang ipapatupad itong Rule 18, iyong sub judice rule ng impeachment court na ito, this must apply to everybody,” Barbers said during the Saturday News Forum at Dapo Restaurant in Quezon City.
“Hindi lamang sa mga public and private prosecutors, hindi lamang sa counsel for the defense, hindi lamang sa ating respondent, kasama dito iyong senator-judges,” he added.

Barbers made the remark when asked about Senate impeachment court Presiding Officer Sen. Francis Escudero’s reminder for senator-judges to observe impartiality and judicial decorum under the sub judice ruling.
The question specifically raised public statements by Sen. Robin Padilla, but Barbers did not name or single out the senator in his response.
Instead, Barbers stressed that the restrictions should be enforced uniformly on everyone covered by the rule.
“Kaya nga if they are lenient doon sa iba, teka muna, bakit ganoon? Hindi dapat ganoon. This should be applied equally to all the parties in this trial,” he said.
Barbers said senator-judges who go beyond the restrictions should receive the same scrutiny as prosecutors, defense lawyers and other parties in the proceedings.
“So kung meron mang senator-judges na nag-o-overboard, dapat equal ang attention. May mga pamantayan, may mga panuntunan naman,” he said.
Barbers noted that the ruling provides remedies for possible violations, including internal Senate mechanisms involving the Committee on Ethics for senator-judges.
Escudero’s ruling reminded senator-judges to maintain impartiality and judicial decorum and pointed to remedies under Senate rules for possible violations by its members.
Barbers said the bottom line is that no one covered by the rule should be exempt from following it.
“So ito ay isang, kumbaga, parang rule na hindi dapat lalabagin ng kahit sinuman,” he said.
At the same time, Barbers reiterated his personal appeal for some leeway in enforcing the rule to allow the public to receive accurate information about the impeachment proceedings.
“Sabi nga, itong impeachment ay sui generis. Baka sakaling pwedeng medyo luwag-luwagan natin dahil ang pinaka-objective sana ay ma-inform ang publiko kung ano iyong totoong nangyayari,” he said.

articles.title: Right-wing commentator Milo Yiannopoulos deported from US to UK
articles.summary: The self-styled provocateur had been detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

blocks.text: British right-wing political commentator Milo Yiannopoulos has been deported from the United States after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
Yiannopoulos, 41, a former editor of Breitbart News and onetime political aide to rapper Kanye West, was deported on Friday, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
Yiannopoulos, "an illegal alien from the United Kingdom" had been sent "back to his home country", a DHS spokesperson said in a statement given to the BBC.
The self-styled provocateur has called himself the "most fabulous supervillain on the internet" and advocated for stricter US immigration controls. His critics call him a purveyor of hate speech.
Yiannopoulos, who grew up in Kent in the south of England, was arrested on 27 August after arriving at Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport.
He flew into the US in May 2019 and "chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation's laws", the DHS said.
He has previously cheered on ICE raids, last year calling for "total legal immunity for ICE agents when they're on duty".
He wrote on social media in 2025: "We have got to deport millions and millions of people. Without that, nothing else matters."
Yiannopoulos also advocated "on the spot deportation for anyone who can't prove they are in the US legally" on social media.
Yiannopoulos was an early supporter of Donald Trump during the 2016 election, headlining an event that year called Gays for Trump during the Republican National Convention.

The commentator has since become a critic of the US president, but still voices support for his agenda. He wrote on X in March this year that Trump had "lost his way, bought off by foreign interests".

Yiannopoulos has courted controversy with his comments on transgender people, Muslims, Black Lives Matter, feminists and gay people, even though he himself identified as gay. He now calls himself an "ex-gay".

In 2020, he assisted West in the rapper's unsuccessful bid to become president. He also worked for Marjorie Taylor Greene, a former Republican congresswoman who fell out with Trump and became a fierce critic before resigning from office.

Laura Loomer, a far-right commentator and Trump ally who has feuded with Yiannopoulos, took credit for his arrest by ICE, claiming on X on Friday night that his flight back to the UK had already departed.
"This subversive foreign agent is already out of the United States and DHS tells me he's NEVER allowed to come back to the United States ever again," she wrote.

In 2017, he was disinvited from speaking at CPAC, a US conservative conference that also hosted Trump, after footage emerged of Yiannopoulos appearing to condone paedophilia. He also later apologised and resigned from Breitbart.
He denied the allegations and said he had been speaking about his own experiences as a child.

Yiannopoulos was once regularly linked with the alt-right, a disparate group that is outspoken against political correctness and feminism, and which includes neo-Nazis and white supremacists among its ranks.
He has said he does not consider himself part of the alt-right, although he has called it "energising and exciting".

articles.title: 'We didn’t want them:' Hamilton rallies against Dominion Society, as group holds event in Burlington, Ont.
articles.summary: More than 100 people gathered outside of Hamilton city hall around midday Saturday to denounce the fact that a self-proclaimed nationalist group that wants to deport millions of people from Canada…
articles.byline: Paul Forsyth, Eva Salinas, Lauren Kuivenhoven

image.caption: The parking lot at The Atrium in Burlington was full on Saturday. People with Dominion Society lanyards were seen in the parking lot. (Jaskaran Singh/CBC)

blocks.text: More than 100 people gathered outside of Hamilton city hall Saturday to denounce the fact that a self-proclaimed nationalist group that wants to deport millions of people from Canada planned to host a day-long conference in the city the same day.
The Hope Not Hate rally said it was a gathering to “stand up against racism and bigotry,” in light of the Dominion Society’s organizing.
In the end, the anti-immigration group, which had previously announced its DomCon event would take place in Hamilton on Saturday, held it down the highway in Burlington, Ont.

CBC Hamilton observed several men in suits wearing Dominion Society lanyards in the parking lot of The Atrium Banquet and Conference Centre. One of them, Max Genest, identified himself as a member of the group. The parking lot was nearly full. Around 30 masked protesters were also on site, as were several members of the Halton Regional Police Service.
Protesters outside the Atrium centre said they were not part of an organized group but declined to speak on the record, citing fear of being targeted by Dominion Society supporters.
They told CBC they were protesting what they called "fascist and racist" beliefs.
The venue said it had no knowledge of the group when it accepted its reservation.

"Atrium was not aware of the Dominion Society of Canada's background upon booking and is not aware of any client's social political views, nor is it a contractual requirement for any … client to disclose that information," Alexandre R. Figueiredo, who identified himself as owner and CEO of Atrium, said in an email to CBC News.
"Atrium respects the rights of all citizens, including the right to protest."
The Canadian Anti-Hate Network first reported the venue to CBC News earlier on Saturday.
"Hamilton beat Dominion Society," Evan Balgord, executive director of the Canadian Anti-Hate Network, told CBC Hamilton in response to the conference being held in Burlington.
Efforts from groups in Hamilton to spread awareness about the Dominion Society and have bookings cancelled were ultimately successful, Balgord said.

"The day's not over yet but I’m relieved that this time, they did not successfully host their racist and anti-immigrant event in Hamilton," Lyndon George, executive director of the Hamilton Anti-Racism Resource Centre (HARRC), told CBC Saturday. "Full credit goes to a coordinated effort to keep hate out of Hamilton."

Dominion Society did not confirm the location to CBC directly. "Despite the best efforts of angry anti-Canadians activists and their sympathizers in the Hamilton police, they were not able to cancel DOMCON26," group founder Daniel Tyrie wrote in an email Saturday.

When CBC shared its observations with the City of Burlington, the city said in an email it was previously not aware of the conference taking place there but that the "event is not taking place at a city-owned or city-operated facility.

"Burlington is proud to be a diverse and inclusive community. We reject hatred, discrimination and intolerance in all forms. Hate has no place in Burlington, and we remain committed to creating a city where everyone feels welcome, valued, respected and safe," the email statement said.
At least 2 Hamilton venues cancelled booking

In the lead up to Saturday, groups like HARRC, followed by Hamilton Mayor Andrea Horwarth, some Niagara municipalities and Hamilton police said venues should be aware of who is making a booking before accepting it.
On Saturday, people gathered at Hamilton city hall said the group was not welcome.

“It’s very important to us to make sure that we stand up, that we speak out, that we contact politicians, and we don’t just sit in discomfort when we hear about a rise in white supremacy,” said Karen Goodfellow, who came to Hamilton from Toronto to show support.

"As working class people we decided we needed to get together in this city and say we’re all in this together," Hamilton labour organizer Ritch Whyman told CBC Hamilton. "We didn’t want them... to bring their racist politics into our city.”
Hamilton is a "welcoming" place, added Vivyan Salih, who works at the Immigrants Working Centre.

The Dominion Society did not reveal the venue in the lead up to the event. Then came word from Hamilton police that two different venues in Hamilton had pulled the plug on hosting the conference, one just days before.
Police joined call-out to venues before event
Police had joined the call for venues to “consider the impact” of hosting the event in the days leading up to it.
"The messaging associated with DomCon is divisive and exclusionary and can negatively impact the sense of safety and belonging within our community," police said in a news release Thursday.
Dominion Society in turn accused the police of an “abuse of power.”

items: What is Dominion Society of Canada and why are people of different political backgrounds worried?

blocks.text: Dominion Society said it was planning to have Canadian and international speakers at DomCon, such as far-right Austrian extremist Martin Sellner. But Sellner, who is permanently banned in the UK, posted on social media that the Canadian government blocked him from travelling here by not replying to his visa application in time.
Richard Robertson, B’nai Brith Canada’s director of research and advocacy, commended the blocking of Sellner.
“Extremists such as Sellner have no business coming to Canada to attack our multicultural society and incite hate and intolerance,” he said.
Protesters rally at Hamilton City Hall against anti-immigration group

A livestream of the conference on Saturday showed co-founder Ken Jones giving opening remarks, followed by a speaker singing the national anthem in front of a Canadian Red Ensign flag held up by two men.
Later, attendees were heard chanting "remigration now". following a pre-recorded video address by Sellner.
Balgord, of the Canadian Anti-Hate Network, previously said Dominion Society likely has thousands of members — mostly young white men and boys.
On its website, Dominion Society describes itself as "promoting Canadian nationalism and immigration reform."
However, "when they're talking just to their supporters, they're talking about how they need to deport people from Canada who are not the right kind of white and European," Balgord told CBC Hamilton.

Dominion Society's website outlines a plan for "remigration," or the mass deportation of five to nine million people, including temporary foreign workers, permanent residents and people born in Canada to non-Canadian citizens.
It also promotes the great replacement conspiracy theory, which suggests white people are being replaced by racialized people.
'We are equally free to condemn them'
On Aug. 4, several Hamilton groups, including HARRC and Hamilton Centre for Civic Inclusion, signed an open letter urging businesses and institutions not to rent space to Dominion Society.

They called on elected officials to denounce the group, and asked leaders to commit that their policies and statements "will not contribute to the scapegoating of immigrants and racialized communities that is on the rise in Hamilton."
Horwath wrote letters to local businesses, asking them to be wary of an anti-immigration group advertising a conference.

"While people are free to express their views, our community must also be clear about the values we stand for and are proud of: inclusion, respect and ensuring that everyone feels they belong in Hamilton," she said.

items: Hamilton police join call for venues to 'consider the impact' of hosting anti-immigration group Saturday

blocks.text: Hamilton Centre MP Aslam Rana issued a statement on Aug. 18 condemning the planned conference, saying it and Dominion Society "represent a racist and extremist ideology masquerading as a nationalist movement."
He said Hamilton has already seen a significant increase in hate crimes. "Organizations and events like these only work to divide Canadians and seek to pit neighbour against neighbour," he said.
Fear that DomCon could be move neighbouring Niagara Region also spilled over into that region this week.

Saleh Waziruddin, with the Niagara Region Anti-Racism Association, wrote to municipal chief administrative officers across Niagara warning that Dominion Society could be planning to move its "hate" conference there.

The Township of West Lincoln, nestled against the border with Hamilton, made it clear it wasn't interested in having DomCon in the township and urged private facilities to not allow "hate-based" events.

"We are working hard to unite our community and build a strong sense of safety, civic pride and belonging," the township statement said on Thursday. "We strongly condemn hate-motivated groups who would dismantle our efforts, spread hatred or breed division within our community."
St. Catharines Mayor Mat Siscoe told CBC News he hoped no facility in his city would "lower itself" to rent to Dominion or other groups like it.
"They are free to express their views, and we are equally free to condemn them and make clear that those views are not welcome here," he said. "That, too, is freedom of speech.”

articles.title: Israeli settlers attack home in occupied West Bank's Qusra: witnesses
articles.summary: Dozens of masked Israeli settler militants attacked homes surrounding the occupied West Bank village of Qusra on Saturday, the first major attack since a siege by settlers in the area earlier this…

image.caption: Palestinians look at the houses that came under settler attack in the Palestinian village of Qusra, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, on Saturday. (Ammar Awad/Reuters)

blocks.text: World

Dozens of masked Israeli settler militants attacked homes surrounding the occupied West Bank village of Qusra on Saturday, the first major attack since a siege by settlers in the area earlier this month drew an international outcry. The settlers surrounded a Palestinian home, throwing stones while seven Palestinians were trapped inside, according to witnesses.
Settlers surrounded the home and threw stones, while seven Palestinians were trapped inside, onlookers say

Dozens of masked Israeli settler militants attacked homes surrounding the occupied West Bank village of Qusra on Saturday, the first major attack since a siege by settlers in the area earlier this month drew an international outcry.
In one case, the settlers surrounded a Palestinian home, throwing stones while seven Palestinians were trapped inside, according to witnesses who spoke to Reuters.

Saddam Oday, one of those trapped, said the Israeli military fired tear gas into the home and detained the residents inside while letting him go. He said the military had not detained any of the settlers and had allowed them to leave.
Palestinian-American pleads for U.S. to help end Israeli settler siege
The owner of the house, Luay Bayrudi, said when the military arrived, soldiers handcuffed, blindfolded and beat those inside before later releasing them.
The Israeli military said in a statement that troops and border police forces had arrived on the scene to remove "rioters" and protect the residents inside the house.
The military did not immediately respond to a request for comment on why they had reportedly fired tear gas at the house and detained and beaten the residents.
In his first public statement on Qusra, Israeli ‌Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he condemned the violence in Qusra and blamed a "handful of rioters."
"I strongly condemn the criminal acts of violence committed in the villages of Qusra and Jalud," Netanyahu said, referring to a separate incident in a neighbouring village.
Residents report frequent encroachments
Bayrudi said that after calling the Israeli military for help, he and six others were trapped inside the home for more than an hour as settlers threw stones.
He showed a Reuters reporter his bandaged arm, which he said had been injured by a stone during the attack.
Oday, a medic, said four of those trapped suffered injuries due to the tear gas, and two sustained injuries from the stones thrown by settlers.

The attack occurred a few hundred metres away from three homes to which settlers laid siege this month, drawing international condemnation and a massive Israeli military deployment that residents say has kept them effectively trapped in their homes.

"They spotted the residents working on their house, which is still under construction, and they started throwing rocks," said Loui Ridi, a Palestinian American whose home was one of the three under siege this month. He said he watched Saturday's attack from his house.
Ridi said he had seen near-daily encroachments of Israeli settlers into the area surrounding his home, despite the heavy Israeli military presence in the area.
Israeli soldiers appear to throw items from balcony of besieged house in West Bank's Qusra
Settler violence rising

Rights groups say the increasing settler presence on the edge of Palestinian villages, like Qusra, is part of a wider effort by settlers to seize more land from Palestinians, further eating into territory where Palestinians aim to establish a state.

Violence by Jewish settlers in the occupied West Bank has been on the rise, with some emboldened by the government of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has overseen a massive settlement expansion in the territory. Netanyahu has not commented on the situation in Qusra.

items: Israeli settler blockades part of escalating violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank

blocks.text: The Israeli military said in its statement that along with the border police it would continue "to operate in the areas of Qusra and (neighbouring) Jalud to prevent further disturbances and restore order in the area."
The United Nations and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law pertaining to military occupations. Israel rejects this, viewing the area as disputed rather than occupied.

articles.title: Elderly Aeta dies in Porac landslide as floods grip Pampanga
articles.summary: CITY OF SAN FERNANDO, Pampanga — A 70-year-old Aeta died in a landslide in Porac, Pampanga, as heavy rains from the enhanced southwest monsoon triggered widespread flooding and forced residents in…

blocks.text: CITY OF SAN FERNANDO, Pampanga — A 70-year-old Aeta died in a landslide in Porac, Pampanga, as heavy rains from the enhanced southwest monsoon triggered widespread flooding and forced residents in high-risk areas to evacuate.
The man was died when a landslide struck Barangay Pidpid on Friday (Aug. 28), according to Pampanga Vice Gov. Dennis Pineda.
The area is about 20 kilometers south of Mount Pinatubo.
Pineda said 30 Aeta families from the area had been evacuated to the Pio evacuation center near the Porac town proper as a precaution.
The evacuation came as rivers and waterways across Pampanga continued to swell following days of heavy rain.

The provincial government on Friday ordered preemptive and forced evacuations in high-risk and vulnerable areas after the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) issued a red rainfall warning for the province.
Pampanga has been under a state of calamity since Aug. 12 because of widespread flooding and the effects of the enhanced southwest monsoon and successive weather disturbances. /gsg

articles.title: Groups press DENR to suspend mangrove earth-balling
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Environmental groups are urging the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) to suspend the earth-balling and relocation of mangroves, warning that the practice…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Environmental groups are urging the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) to suspend the earth-balling and relocation of mangroves, warning that the practice could result in the death of up to 80% of trees removed, as a House resolution calls for an examination of the agency’s policy.

The call was made by the Global Mangrove Alliance Philippines (GMAP), international ocean conservation organization Oceana and mangrove scientist Dr. Jurgenne Primavera of the Zoological Society of London (ZSL), amid a congressional inquiry into the DENR’s guidelines allowing mangrove earth-balling in exceptional circumstances.

The DENR memorandum, dated Oct. 8, 2025, is titled Interim Operational Guidance and Conditions on the Earth-balling and Relocation of Mangroves in Exceptional Circumstances. It provides guidance for processing requests to earth-ball and relocate mangroves pending the completion of a study by the agency’s Ecosystems Research and Development Bureau.

Under the memorandum, mangroves “shall not be removed or disturbed” as a rule. Earth-balling and relocation may be considered only in specified exceptional cases, including when mangrove trees pose a danger or when the activity involves an infrastructure flagship project endorsed by the Department of Economy, Planning, and Development, provided that mitigation measures to avoid impacts on mangroves have been exhausted.
The guidelines also prohibit the DENR from accepting or processing requests for earth-balling and relocation for commercial, recreational or other private purposes.
Survival of transplanted mangroves
The environmental groups, however, said available scientific evidence raises concerns about whether mangroves removed through earth-balling can survive after transplantation.
“Repeal the DENR Guidelines now. Congress must investigate to stop this threat to our remaining mangroves,” Primavera, ZSL’s chief mangroves scientific adviser, said.
The groups cited several studies they said had been presented to the DENR as early as March 2025.

These included a China-based study that recorded only 20% to 25% survival of two mangrove species 10 months after earth-balling; an Australia-based study that found mortality after 2.5 years among mangroves with an average trunk diameter of more than 5 centimeters; and Philippine data showing adult mangroves in five barangays in Ibajay, Aklan, had average trunk diameters of 9 to 16 centimeters.

The House resolution filed by Mamamayang Liberal Party-list Rep. Leila de Lima cites additional research indicating that successful earth-balling is ecologically and physiologically limited to trees with stem widths of less than approximately 8 centimeters.
It also says mangroves in coastal areas typically targeted for infrastructure development in the Philippines have mature stems ranging from 10 to 30 centimeters in diameter or more.
Earth-balling involves digging up a tree together with surrounding soil to form a compact mass, which is then secured and transferred using equipment such as a crane or bladed tree spade.

“[S]tudies have shown that mangrove earth-balling and transplantation establish that the practice fundamentally disrupts the integrated soil-water-vegetation connections upon which mangrove ecosystems depend, resulting in losses of ecosystem function,” the House resolution stated.
DENR guidelines impose safeguards
The DENR memorandum, meanwhile, states that the survival of earth-balled mangroves must be the “paramount consideration” in all cases.

It requires proponents to follow established methodologies for selecting transplanting and replacement sites, preserving the root system and soil ball, timing the operation according to tidal and seasonal conditions, and using appropriate equipment and transport techniques.
Proponents must also submit a Mangrove Rehabilitation and Monitoring Plan before any permit is issued.

The memorandum further requires transplanting and replacement sites to meet ecological standards involving tidal elevation, hydrological conditions, salinity and soil conditions, slope and wave protection, and proximity to existing mangrove stands.

For projects covered by the Philippine Environmental Impact Statement System, proposed earth-balling and relocation activities must also be included in the applicable environmental assessment documents.
Actual earth-balling, transplanting and replacement planting must be conducted under the direct monitoring and supervision of the concerned DENR field office, according to the memorandum.
Pending applications for mangrove earth-balling and relocation, meanwhile, will be evaluated under the safeguards in the memorandum.

“Proponents with incomplete requirements or pending submissions shall be directed to update their applications in compliance with these provisions prior to further evaluation. No permit shall be issued unless full compliance with this Memorandum is observed,” the agency said.
The memorandum also says existing guidelines and requirements for the issuance of cutting or earth-balling permits will remain in effect and will apply alongside the new provisions.

It also provides that unauthorized cutting, earth-balling or relocation of mangroves may be subject to penalties under Presidential Decree No. 705, as amended, the Fisheries Code and other applicable laws.
House questions legal basis of policy
Beyond the scientific concerns, the House resolution questions whether the DENR memorandum is consistent with existing laws and international commitments on mangrove protection.
It cites Section 99 of Republic Act No. 8550, as amended by RA 10654, or the Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998, which prohibits the conversion of mangroves for other purposes.

The resolution also points to Presidential Proclamation No. 2152, which declares the entire province of Palawan and certain other areas as mangrove swamp forest reserves, and the Indigenous Peoples’ Rights Act, or RA 8371, when mangrove areas fall within ancestral domains.

The resolution argues that the DENR’s issuance could conflict with these protections, describing the “unilateral issuance of administrative guidance” as a “grave overreach of executive regulatory authority.”
It also asks House committees to examine the memorandum’s legal validity and determine whether it should be revoked or amended.

Specifically, the resolution calls for the inquiry to “review the legal validity of the administrative issuance in light of existing mangrove protection laws, recommend its immediate revocation or amendment as may be warranted, and call for the conduct of a comprehensive, independent scientific review.”

The proposed inquiry would also look beyond the current memorandum. De Lima’s resolution asks lawmakers to review and consolidate existing legislation and explore a new mangrove conservation and protection law establishing “clear, enforceable standards for mangrove preservation, rehabilitation, and sustainable management.”
Mangrove loss raises stakes for coastal communities

The Philippines is home to at least 50% of the roughly 65 mangrove species found worldwide, but its mangrove cover has declined from about 500,000 hectares in the early 20th century to roughly 285,000 to 311,400 hectares in 2020, according to Oceana.
The House resolution puts the remaining cover at about 284,798 hectares and says the country has lost more than 64% of its mangroves since 1918.

The resolution notes that mangroves help protect coastal communities from storm surges, flooding and erosion while also serving as nurseries for marine species, supporting fisherfolk livelihoods and contributing to climate change mitigation.
For Oceana Vice President Von Hernandez, allowing earth-balling could put those natural defenses at further risk.
“By allowing earth-balling, the DENR is sacrificing proven nature-based solutions for short-term economic gain,” Hernandez said.

“Shouldn’t the DENR be held accountable for reneging on its mandate to protect mangroves and uphold nature-based safeguards especially at a time when every coastal community in the country is under siege from flooding and storm surges?” he added.
Concern over Cancabato Bay

Oceana also pointed to Cancabato Bay in Tacloban City, Leyte — known as “ground zero” of Supertyphoon Yolanda (Haiyan) in 2013, one of the deadliest typhoons in recorded history, which killed at least 6,300 people — as a potential site for further mangrove removal.

The organization said operators of Daniel Z. Romualdez Airport announced on July 29 that “mangroves in the airport’s vicinity will have to be removed to make way for shore protection infrastructure, a new perimeter road, and to prevent bird strikes.”
According to GMAP, many coastal areas with mangroves targeted for cutting were declared no-build zones after Supertyphoon Haiyan.
Stronger mangrove protection
GMAP has called for a halt to earth-balling while Congress examines the policy.
“In the spirit of precaution, all earth-balling of mangroves must stop while Congress examines the scientific, legal, and governance questions surrounding the policy,” the group said.
The groups also cited the 40-hectare Floodway Project in Jaro, Iloilo, as an example of infrastructure being integrated into a natural mangrove environment.
They are urging the passage of the proposed National Coastal Greenbelt Bill, which seeks to strengthen mangrove restoration and nature-based solutions for vulnerable coastal communities.
Oceana said it supports De Lima’s investigation and the proposed legislation.
“With climate impacts intensifying, we appeal to President Marcos Jr. to certify the passage of this bill as urgent,” Hernandez said. /dm

articles.title: Far-right media provocateur Milo Yiannopoulos deported by ICE from US to UK
articles.summary:
Ex-Breitbart editor has vocally supported immediate deportations for anyone who can’t prove US residency

Far-right British media provocateur Milo Yiannopoulos has been deported from the US…

blocks.text: Far-right British media provocateur Milo Yiannopoulos has been deported from the US after being detained on Thursday by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in New Orleans in connection with what the agency said was expired authorization to be in the country and a deportation order.
Yiannopoulos’s deportation occurred on Friday, said a statement on Saturday from a spokesperson for the US Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE.

The DHS spokesperson’s statement did not say where Yiannopoulos had been deported to. But, citing “two senior US sources”, the UK’s Telegraph newspaper reported that Yiannopoulos had been flown back to Britain.

A DHS spokesperson on Friday said that Yiannopoulos, 41, had been arrested by ICE on Thursday at the Louis Armstrong New Orleans international airport. The spokesperson said Yiannopoulos “legally entered the country” in May 2019 through New York City but then “chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws”.
The spokesperson said that Yiannopoulos was issued a final order of removal by an immigration judge on 22 July “after failing to show up for his immigration hearing”.

“He will remain in ICE custody pending removal,” the spokesperson added. “This administration is working diligently to ensure that aliens in our country illegally can no longer fly unless it is out of our country to self-deport.”

Yiannopoulos – who has previously been a vocal supporter of ICE and immediate deportations for anyone who can’t prove US residency – was believed to have been arrested while heading to a concert by rapper Ye, formerly Kanye West.

West performed at New Orleans’s Caesars Superdome on Friday. In 2022, Yiannopoulos worked on West’s short-lived 2024 White House campaign, and his social media account suggests he was working for a company of the rapper.

Yiannopoulos, a former editor of the conservative media outlet Breitbart News, previously served as an intern for the former US congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene. He eventually became locked into a feud with fellow far-right commentator Laura Loomer, a Donald Trump administration ally who claimed on Friday that she had reported Yiannopoulos to ICE over his immigration status.

At the peak of his influence, Yiannopoulos was offered a speaking slot at the Conservative Political Action Conference, or CPAC, in 2017 after he had been supportive of Trump during his run for his first presidency.
He fell out of favor in conservative circles after the publication of a video in which he condoned sexual relations with boys as young as 13.
Yiannopoulos claimed that his experiences as a victim of teenage sexual abuse gave him license to comment on the subject. He soon resigned as a senior editor at Breitbart.

Yiannopoulos was also banned from Twitter, now called X, in 2016 for directing racist and misogynistic tweets against a Black actor in a Ghostbusters remake. His account was reinstated to the platform in 2022 after it was acquired and renamed by multibillionaire Elon Musk.

A little more than a year before his detention by ICE, a social media post from Yiannopoulos called on immigration checkpoints to be set up at California “supermarket entrances, gas stations, strip malls, intersection and government buildings, with on the spot deportation for anyone who can’t prove they are in the US legally”.

He had also sarcastically asked whether it was impolite for one “to masturbate” in public rather than in private “if you are going about your business and find yourself observing an ICE raid” amid the mass deportation campaign that Trump has pursued throughout his second presidency.

articles.title: Daughter traces mother and aunt’s last known location in Nepal through TikTok video
articles.summary:
Tulshi Patel says mother Hemangini Jitendra Patel and aunt Hema Sunil Amin were last seen at Friendship Bridge on Nepal-China border

•

blocks.text: The daughter of a woman missing in Nepal has told how she traced her mother’s location through a TikTok video posted hours before the devastating flash flood hit.
The catastrophic flash floods that hit Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday, thundering down valleys and sweeping away entire villages, have killed at least 675 people, while more than 3,000 remain missing.
Among the missing are 33 British nationals, including a 13-year-old, NHS workers and a priest. A team from the UK will arrive in the Nepali capital, Kathmandu, on Saturday.

Tulshi Patel’s mother, Hemangini Jitendra Patel, and her aunt, Hema Sunil Amin, set off on a pilgrimage in which they had planned to travel into Tibet, but the pair have not been contactable since the flash floods hit.
In an interview with LBC’s Matt Frei, Patel said the two women had been talking about the trip since the start of the year and the journey had been “on their bucket list”.

She said she had last spoken to her mother and aunt on Monday, had received a photo of them on Tuesday, and their last known location had come from a GPS signal from the tour group at a place called Friendship Bridge at the Nepal-China border.

Patel, a pharmacist from Milton Keynes, said: “We did our own deep-dive research and we found a TikTok video that verified and showed my mum and auntie and three other people from the tour at the border waiting to cross, I guess, that the local Nepali tour guide had made.”
Of the video, Patel said: “It was Wednesday morning, just before 6am, Nepal time.
“They were supposed to have crossed the border on Tuesday, but I guess due to weather conditions, or whichever it was, they got delayed and unfortunately crossed over on Wednesday.”
The flood is believed to have occurred after a magnitude 5.2 seismic event near the border between Nepal and China on Wednesday at 8.37am local time, according to the US Geological Survey.
Patel said her mother and aunt had been in good health and had prepared well for the trip. “They’d gone on walks regularly, they were looking forward to it. This is all they wanted,” she said.
“Their positive viewpoints, health, mental health was great and they were very strong and positive about everything.

“This was something that they were both looking forward to. They’d been talking about this from the beginning of the year. It was something that was on their bucket list that they really wanted to do.”

Patel said she had messaged the two women “in the hopes that maybe we’ll see a tick to say they’ve seen it or read it” and had attempted to contact the tour guide. “We’ve messaged the tour guide in case he has a signal because he’ll have a local Sim as well.

“Every day we’re calling via WhatsApp … We’ve not given up, but, from our end, all we can do is research, but we just need kind of eyes and ears there from our side to basically get them out. Get all of them out and safe.”
Patel said the family had considered travelling to Nepal to join search efforts but had decided against this as they did not know how close they could get to the region in order to help.

blocks.caption: Leena Bector. Photograph: Facebook

blocks.text: Some of those missing were visiting Kailash Mansarovar, a high-altitude site in ‌Tibet revered by Hindus and Buddhists. Neetu Goyal Tiwari, 51, was on her “dream” trip to complete a pilgrimage when the flash floods hit.

The family have been desperately phoning contacts in Nepal in an attempt to find her, though they increasingly believe her to still be in China. As many of the family members are based in India, it is difficult for them to obtain visas to search for her. Her brother, Naresh Goyal, said Neetu’s husband and daughter remained in the UK for now.

“We’re not sure what the next second holds and what we should do from our end, because we’re trying to reach everyone we can,” he said. “She was a very fun-loving woman [and] really had a great heart. I really hope she comes back soon.”
Other families of those missing have travelled to the affected region from the UK. Leena Bector, 53, from Slough, was among 27 travellers who are unaccounted for.
Her husband, Bhupesh Bector, told the Times he was booking the next flight to Kathmandu after the Home Office had failed to confirm whether Leena was on its missing persons list.
He said: “Even if they find her today or tomorrow, I need to be there. She must be in trauma.”

articles.title: JuanHand pushes ₱1-trillion lending spree as bank credit slows down
articles.summary: Digital cash lender JuanHand is poised to extend more loans beyond the ₱1.16 trillion it has disbursed to date, with a new product allowing borrowers to take out additional funds within their credit…

blocks.text: Digital cash lender JuanHand is poised to extend more loans beyond the ₱1.16 trillion it has disbursed to date, with a new product allowing borrowers to take out additional funds within their credit limit without first settling their existing loan.

JuanHand has introduced its top-up loan, allowing eligible users to apply for additional funds even while they have an existing loan, with approvals taking as little as five minutes through its operator, WeFund Lending Corp.’s AI-powered tool.
“Through the utilization of WeFund’s proprietary AI, the platform can analyze user data and provide approval in as fast as 5 minutes,” JuanHand said.

JuanHand is the Philippine subsidiary of New York Stock Exchange-listed global financial technology firm FinVolution Group. To date, JuanHand has extended over ₱1.16 trillion in loans to more than 20 million Filipinos.

According to the digital lender, the new top-up loan feature is designed to offer borrowers another option “when they need access to additional financial resources, provided that the new loan remains within their available credit limit and applicable eligibility requirements.”
Under its current terms, borrowers can apply for loans of up to ₱50,000, with daily interest rates set as low as 0.025 percent, “subject to applicable loan terms and eligibility.”

This feature has veered away from conventional digital micro-lending models. “Rather than limiting borrowers to a single borrowing experience, this allows eligible users to borrow again as long as it is within their credit limit,” JuanHand explained.

JuanHand has simplified its requirements, making the application process accessible by requiring “only a registered mobile number and one valid ID” before the AI-driven underwriting evaluates the borrower’s profile.

This development comes alongside Filipinos’ growing reliance on e-wallets, digital lenders, and digital banks. Digital lending has become crucial for expanding financial services beyond traditional banking networks, the firm noted.
“As digital borrowing continues to evolve, JuanHand remains focused on serving underserved yet creditworthy Filipinos” while responding to the changing needs of local consumers.
Credit products such as JuanHand’s could offer some thrust the overall financial system needs, as it has seen moderating lending activity in June.

Lending by big banks in the Philippines grew by 9.8 percent in June, its slowest pace in four months, as borrowers turned more cautious, dampening demand for loans. It slumped from the peak of 12.1 percent in May.
Outstanding loans stood at ₱17.33 trillion as of end-June, according to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP). (Derco Rosal)

articles.title: Pinatubo, Taal lahar flow warning issued as monsoon rains persist
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) on Saturday warned of possible lahar flows in Pinatubo and Taal volcanoes amid continuous rains. Phivolcs…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) on Saturday warned of possible lahar flows in Pinatubo and Taal volcanoes amid continuous rains.

Phivolcs warned that prolonged heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or “habagat” may generate lahar, or volcanic sediment flows, and muddy streamflow in rivers and drainage areas near the volcanoes.

“Prolonged and intense rainfall may generate non-eruption lahars on major rivers draining western Pinatubo Volcano where significant deposits of the 1991 PDCs remain on the watershed,” Phivolcs said in an advisory.
It added that the lahar from Pinatubo may occur on the upper to middle reaches of Sto. Tomas-Marella and Bucao river systems.
These are among the river systems covered by a government dredging project that has been ongoing for about six years.
Meanwhile, the muddy stream flows may affect the lower reaches and communities of Zambales, including San Marcelino, San Narciso, San Felipe, and Botolan.
The volcanic sediments may affect the O’Donnell and Pasig-Potrero River systems and downstream communities in Tarlac and Pampanga provinces.
Heavy rainfall may also cause muddy streamflow and even volcanic debris around Taal volcano, primarily on the west and north slopes of the lake.
These can affect parts of Batangas provinces, particularly Agoncillo, Laurel and Talisay.
Phivolcs advised the affected communities to continuously monitor weather conditions and to take precautionary measures when necessary. (with a report from Joanna Rose Aglibot / INQUIRER Luzon) /gsg

articles.title: Old soup factory takes on new high-tech life as quantum computing firm gets $195M federal boost
articles.summary: In the echoey void of a gutted Campbell's Soup factory in Toronto’s west end, Canada's minister of artificial intelligence and digital innovation announced the federal government’s biggest bet to…

image.caption: A former Campbell's Soup plant in Toronto, shown here in 2018, will become a site for advanced manufacturing for Xanadu Quantum Technologies' quantum computers. (CBC)

blocks.text: Business

In the echoey void of a gutted Campbell's Soup factory in Toronto’s west end, Canada's minister of artificial intelligence and digital innovation announced the federal government’s biggest bet to date on homegrown technology that could revolutionize artificial intelligence, medical science and a host of other key sectors of the economy.
Former Campbell's Soup facility to become manufacturing site for Xanadu Quantum Technologies

In the echoey void of a gutted Campbell Soup factory in Toronto's west end, Canada's minister of artificial intelligence and digital innovation announced the federal government's biggest bet to date on homegrown technology that could revolutionize artificial intelligence, medical science and a host of other key sectors of the economy.

Against the backdrop of the Canada-U.S. trade war, and U.S. President Donald Trump's frequent threats to Canada's sovereignty, Evan Solomon leaned heavily into patriotism as he announced $195 million in repayable federal funding for Toronto-based Xanadu Quantum Technologies.
"This is absolutely a great day for Canada, for Xanadu, and I think for science around the world," he said on Friday. "It shows what Canadians do best: We build."
Solomon said Canada is going to take "big swings" in that endeavour.
"We are going to not just make a bet on solving the biggest problems in the world, and being the best in the world.... We're going to do it big, fearlessly."

Founded in 2016, Xanadu builds software and quantum computers powered by light instead of electricity. Unlike traditional computers that generate heat as electricity moves through metal wires, Xanadu's chips guide particles of light without electrical friction.
While other quantum computers require aggressive, power-hungry cooling to work, Xanadu's units largely operate at room temperature.
Last June, the company unveiled a breakthrough chip capable of generating error-resistant photonic qubits, the basic unit of information for quantum computers.
"The countries that will have built what's called a fault-tolerant quantum computer would have the capacity to break cybersecurity," Solomon said.

"This is why China, the United States, Europe, everyone's racing. And the best companies are right here in Canada, and the IP is in Canada. So, from a sovereign national security point of view, this technology is absolutely critical."
'Like riding a rocket'

Xanadu held the announcement inside a former Campbell's Soup factory in Toronto, where the company plans to set up advanced manufacturing for its fault-tolerant utility-scale photonic quantum computers. The 158,000-square-foot facility is expected to cost $893 million and employ 275 workers.
"If digital computing is like galloping on a horse, quantum computing is like riding a rocket," Solomon said. "It's that much quicker."

In 2023, the federal government launched its $360-million National Quantum Strategy. Friday's $195-million repayable financing pledge to Xanadu represents its largest single financial commitment to manufacturing quantum technology.

Friday's announcement ranks among the government's top single-company investments in Canada's tech sector. One of the largest was in 2024, when the government provided a $2.14-billion loan to Ottawa-based satellite operator Telesat.

In March, Xanadu announced negotiations with the federal government and the province of Ontario for as much as $390 million in combined financial support to establish advanced semiconductor and photonic manufacturing capabilities in Canada.
Xanadu CEO Christian Weedbrook said on Friday that up to $195 million in funding is "still being discussed" with Ontario's government, describing the talks as "final negotiations and discussions."

The company said Friday's announcement represents Ottawa's full share. Unlike a traditional loan, there's no fixed date for repayment. The money will come from Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada's Strategic Response Fund, which provided $40 million to Xanadu in 2023.
'Obligations to keep the jobs here'
Weedbrook, who is originally from Australia, says the money will bolster his company's presence in Canada.
"A building that once fed Canadians will now help the technology of the next generation," he said. "Where we are today will allow us to do most of this work here in Canada, in Toronto."
In May, the U.S. government agreed to invest about $2 billion US in nine quantum companies.

Xanadu is growing its footprint south of the border. In 2025, it secured partnerships with the U.S. Department of War and the U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory. The company also works with big-name U.S. firms like Lockheed Martin and chipmaker AMD.

items: University of Calgary to house quantum defence hub to develop tech for armed forces
Xanadu CEO on Canada's quantum future

blocks.text: "I think there's obligations to keep the jobs here for some time," said Amy Karam, a business consultant and fellow at the Canadian Global Affairs Institute.

"By having the government have a seat at the table in terms of business decision-making, I think that is one way that we as a country can really be more involved, or more part of encouraging companies to stay. Just funding and doing research and creating talent, it's not enough anymore."

In March, Xanadu dual-listed its shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange and the tech-heavy Nasdaq. The latter raises the company's profile among U.S. investors, as its stock trades next to household names like Apple, Microsoft and Nvidia.
"It's a big challenge to get companies to stay here," said Karam.
"If you look at the Global Innovation Index, we are slipping drastically," she said.
"We need to do some serious catch-up. We need to take our global technology leadership back, and I have the confidence that this government knows this, sees this and is executing accordingly."

Matthew da Mota is a senior policy researcher at the Canadian SHIELD Institute. The Toronto-based think-tank was launched by BlackBerry co-founder Jim Balsillie to modernize public policy on tech and national security and safeguard Canadian intellectual property.
From developing new pharmaceutical drugs to cybersecurity, da Mota said Xanadu's work could actually be dangerous in the wrong hands.

"It allows for really, really fast processing, really, really fast computation and doing multiple things at once in a way that we weren't able to do with traditional computing. It allows for the potential to break existing encryption," he said.
"That's very dangerous for Canada, and for allies, but it's also something that can be an extremely powerful tool for cyber security long-term."
Why Google's Willow chip could be a quantum computing game changer
Speaking to reporters, Solomon downplayed the potential risk of the government making a concentrated bet on a single company pioneering an emerging technology.
"Unless we are at the frontier with Canadian companies on quantum computing, we will be vulnerable in the future," he said.
"It is vital for this country from a security point of view, from a science point of view, from an economic point of view, to make sure that the best companies in the world are here in Canada."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Jeff Lagerquist is a senior writer with CBC News based in Toronto. Originally from Erin, Ont., he studied journalism at Toronto Metropolitan University. Jeff previously worked as a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance Canada. He was also a reporter and digital producer for CTV National News, BNN Bloomberg and The Financial Post. He was also a Columbia University energy journalism fellow for 2025.
