articles.title: Ombudsman questions bail for convicted officials
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla has questioned the courts’ decision to grant bail to individuals while their convictions are under appeal, saying convicted government officials should start…

blocks.text: Building of the Office of the Ombudsman.
Ombudsman office via FB

MANILA, Philippines — Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla has questioned the courts’ decision to grant bail to individuals while their convictions are under appeal, saying convicted government officials should start serving their sentences immediately.
Remulla criticized how the Sandiganbayan has convicted and imposed sentences on erring government officials but only a few were imprisoned.

“Once convicted by the Sandiganbayan or a lower court for graft, you go to jail. But the courts are being too kind. Instead, they grant bail,” Remulla said during his radio show Executive Session on dzRH.
He also criticized the low amount of bail usually set by the court, proposing that it should be equivalent to “the cost of damage” committed by the convicted official.
Remulla said his office will look at the list of officials who have been convicted by the Sandiganbayan to check whether they are in prison or not.
The ombudsman also pointed out how some cases take a long time to be resolved, with some spanning for 15 years, particularly in resolving appeals.
He said there should be stricter requirements and a deadline for resolving appeals so that the convicted individual is not set free indefinitely.
“The problem is once a motion for reconsideration is filed, a bail is granted with no deadline. Will they sit on that forever?” Remulla pointed out.
He urged the Supreme Court to police the judiciary and called on the public to keep watch on the duties of both the ombudsman and the judiciary.
“I urge members of the judiciary to do their jobs,” he said.

articles.title: Lacson claims proof of illegally reclaimed Taguig land
articles.summary: Sen. Panfilo Lacson said he has identified four parcels of illegally reclaimed land in Taguig using “fraudulently” issued land titles, while at least four other parcels have allegedly no…

blocks.text: Sen. Panfilo Lacson on February 10, 2026.
STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Panfilo Lacson said he has identified four parcels of illegally reclaimed land in Taguig using “fraudulently” issued land titles, while at least four other parcels have allegedly no plotted title lots in the digital file of the Land Registration Authority (LRA).
Lacson tweeted the details of the alleged fraudulent land titles in Taguig’s lakeshore development to dispel Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano’s dismissal of the allegations as false.

“Since Sen. Cayetano keeps publicly asking for evidence, I’ll give it to him, in the spirit of public interest,” Lacson posted on X. He was reacting to Cayetano’s Facebook Live on Thursday, where the Minority Leader said he is “hurt” for the 1.3 million residents of Taguig because Lacson is spreading “fake news” about the city.

Lacson said the details of the four “fraudulently” titled parcels involve one covered by an Administrative Patent, involving 9,204 square meters under an Original Certificate of Title; one covered through Judicial/Ordinary Land Registration Processing covering an area of 5,000 square meters under an OCT; one covered by a Homestead Patent involving 181,077 square meters under a Transfer Certificate of Title and one involving 193,027 square meters under a TCT.
Lacson withheld details like the names of those to whom the titles were issued, as well as the OCT and TCT numbers, with the investigation still ongoing.
These will be turned over to the ombudsman as part of its fact-finding probe on Taguig’s allegedly anomalous lakeshore development and reclamation in the guise of flood control and slope protection.
Lacson earlier said the LRA is digging up details on land titles covering some 38.83 hectares of illegally reclaimed areas on the Taguig side of Laguna Lake.
The uncovered land titles were based on the materials provided by the Philippine Reclamation Authority to Lacson’s office.

articles.title: Cardinal laments flooding despite billions already spent
articles.summary: The country is facing an absurd situation where some of the most heavily flooded communities are also places where billions have supposedly been spent for controversial flood control projects,…

blocks.text: Bishop Pablo Virgilio David of Kalookan, president of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of the Philippines.
Interaksyon / CBCP News

MANILA, Philippines — The country is facing an absurd situation where some of the most heavily flooded communities are also places where billions have supposedly been spent for controversial flood control projects, Kalookan Bishop Pablo Virgilio Cardinal David said yesterday.

“Now imagine having to spend billions more – not to build new infrastructure, but to demolish or correct flood control structures that should never have been built that way in the first place,” David said on Facebook.
He made the statement amid the flooding experienced in many areas in the country.

“Citizens of this country, let us unite. We have nothing to lose but our misery. Go to bisto.ph and join the citizens’ ground validation of government infrastructure projects. Register as a volunteer,” David said.

“Take photographs. Document what you see. If possible, bring engineers, architects, environmental planners or other knowledgeable citizens who can help assess the work. Submit your findings to the Bisto Proyekto advocacy initiative,” he added.
He said “let the evidence lead to investigation, prosecution and accountability.”
David added that the country cannot solve an ecological problem merely by pouring more concrete.

“We have to restore watersheds, protect rivers and wetlands, manage our waste, plan our cities intelligently, prepare for rising seas and a changing climate – and make every infrastructure project part of a coherent, science-based master plan,” he said.
Meanwhile, Antipolo Bishop Ruperto Cruz Santos prayed for protection and peace amid rains brought by the southwest monsoon.

“Livelihoods have been washed away, families displaced, homes destroyed and entire neighborhoods submerged. Lord, look with mercy upon Your people. We beg You: stretch out Your mighty hand and calm the rains. Hold back the floods. Strengthen the land. Protect our communities. Guard every family, every child, every worker, every rescuer and every soul caught in danger,” Santos prayed.

articles.title: Over P5 billion needed to rebuild storm-hit classrooms
articles.summary: At least P5.072 billion is needed for the reconstruction of 476 schools damaged by the southwest monsoon and recent tropical cyclones, the Department of Education said yesterday in a situation report.

blocks.text: Meanwhile, at least P1.013 billion is needed to fund the major repair of 624 schools, the DepEd Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Service said.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — At least P5.072 billion is needed for the reconstruction of 476 schools damaged by the southwest monsoon and recent tropical cyclones, the Department of Education (DepEd) said yesterday in a situation report.
No less than P277.34 million will also be needed for the minor repair of 1,444 schools and another P46.983 million for the cleanup and clearing operations of another 1,627.
The DepEd said that 1,145 classrooms in 307 schools are still being used as evacuation centers for at least 9,798 families.

These include 172 evacuation centers in Central Luzon; 57 evacuation centers in Calabarzon; 37 evacuation centers in Ilocos Region; 15 evacuation centers in Metro Manila; 11 evacuation centers in Eastern Visayas; eight evacuation centers in Mimaropa and seven evacuation centers in the Cordillera Administrative Region.

“The Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Service maintains close coordination with field offices to track emerging impacts, validate class suspension data through the ‘Walang Pasok’ monitor and support timely clearing and repair of affected schools,” DepEd said.

DepEd advised field offices and school disaster risk reduction and management teams to sustain monitoring and operational readiness as weather conditions remain capable of triggering localized flooding, landslides and further disruptions.

articles.title: Sara lawyer doubts Madriaga will be presented as witness
articles.summary: A lawyer for Vice President Sara Duterte said the prosecution will not present alleged bagman Ramil Madriaga as witness in the ongoing impeachment trial.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A lawyer for Vice President Sara Duterte said the prosecution will not present alleged bagman Ramil Madriaga as witness in the ongoing impeachment trial.
In an interview with Bilyonaryo News Channel, Paolo Panelo – counsel of Duterte in the perjury complaint filed against Madriaga before the Taguig Prosecutor’s Office – cited his credibility.
“To me, the prosecution will not present (Madriaga as witness). On the part of the defense, I would not know,” Panelo said.
Duterte filed two perjury cases against Madriaga.
The second perjury complaint was based on Madriaga’s supplemental affidavit, where he claimed to have served as the Vice President’s “bagman.”

Duterte’s first perjury complaint against Madriaga stemmed from the latter’s claim that drug lords and Chinese-sponsored Philippine offshore gaming operators bankrolled her campaign for vice president.
“This is a confession that even the prosecution doesn’t believe in Madriaga anymore,” Panelo added.
He said once the prosecution presents Madriaga during the impeachment trial, the defense would prove that he is lying during the cross-examination.
“So, either way, for me, using Ramil Madriaga here in the impeachment trial would benefit VP Sara and would not benefit those who are criticizing her,” Panelo said.
Panelo described Madriaga as a Trojan Horse.
“That’s why we’re holding interviews, media engagements so I can share the contents of our perjury complaint to show that this witness has no credibility,” he said.
‘Not part of’ defense team

“The truth of the matter is Mr. Madriaga is listed as a witness in the prosecution according to their pre-trial brief. He’s also listed as our witness in our pre-trial brief. But see, Atty. Panelo is not part of the defense team,” defense spokesman Michael Poa said.

Poa issued the reaction after Panelo said Madriaga could be a Trojan Horse for the defense even if he lied when he read his sworn supplemental affidavit during the hearing of the House committee on justice on April 14, claiming that Duterte’s P125-million confidential funds were spent in less than 24 hours and not 11 days as previously reported.

articles.title: ‘China exploiting impeachment, flood control’
articles.summary: China is exploiting the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte and the flood control scandal to disrupt the government and advance its expansionist goal, the Armed Forces of the Philippines…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — China is exploiting the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte and the flood control scandal to disrupt the government and advance its expansionist goal, the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) spokesman for the West Philippine Sea said yesterday.
At the Saturday News Forum in Quezon City, Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad said their social media monitoring and analytics showed foreign malign influence at work on the two issues.

While centering on the West Philippine Sea issue, China’s online activities have also been noted in other issues including the raid on Sanjia Steel Corp. plant in Tagoloan, Misamis Oriental last May 15 where around 69 Chinese workers were rounded up.
“They are taking advantage of this because number one, the pattern is clear. Number two, the issues being raised are false and being twisted to their favor,” Trinidad said.
The Chinese embassy has been waging a word war with Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro for his defense of the Sanjia Steel plant raid.

Trinidad said China has been demonizing government officials on social media platforms, particularly Philippine Coast Guard spokesman for the WPS Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela for his strong denunciation of Chinese aggression in Philippine waters.

“This is part of the approach of the Chinese Communist Party, using information because their doctrine is the acme of skill or ‘yung pinakamagaling na manlalaban ay ‘yung hindi mo na kailangan gumamit ng puwersa (the best fighting skill is one without using force),” he said.

At the same forum, AFP spokesperson Col. Francel Margareth Padilla said they are coordinating with agencies in charge of cybersecurity to thwart China’s attacks against the Philippines on social media platforms.
The officials believe China’s attacks will continue as the national and local elections in 2028 approach. “We urge the public to be mindful of the information they get online,” Padilla said.
Appeal to youth

On Friday at a forum organized by the Rotary Club of Chinatown Circle in partnership with the Philippine Navy, Teodoro called on Filipinos to do their part in actively defending the country’s sovereign rights.
Launched during the forum was the Bantay Dagat Youth Ambassadors-West Philippine Sea (WPS) Edition Caravan.
“As populations expand in the world, as resources grow more scarce, as needs grow more scarce, there is a temptation to expand and that we cannot allow for your sake in the future,” he said.
“You cannot stop the growth of human beings, the growth of society... But what you can stop is somebody else taking what should be yours to support yourself and giving it to somebody else.”

“Because all the resources, whether in the West Philippine Sea, in the internal waters, in the Pacific Ocean side of the Philippines, are sources of potential sustenance, energy for future generations,” Teodoro stressed.

“The Philippines is demographically and geographically unique, being 20 percent land and 80 percent water. So much so that we have 2.4 million square kilometers of maritime domain versus a much, much smaller area of land domain,” he said.
Teodoro reaffirmed the Philippines’ commitment to upholding international law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and the 2016 Arbitral Award.

He also highlighted ongoing efforts to strengthen the country’s defense posture through military modernization, strategic infrastructure development and expanded defense partnerships with like-minded nations.
Teodoro explained that the new Status of Visiting Forces Agreements (SOVFA) with Canada and New Zealand have already entered into force, while that with France is awaiting Senate concurrence.

“You can see that these alliances are for shared interests. And what are these interests? That is to secure the maritime domain for the supply chains of like-minded countries who feel threatened by expansionism in their own borders. We need to push back and we need to fight for a proper interpretation of international law,” he said.
“Be convinced that what you’re doing is important,” he said, addressing the youth. — Michael Punongbayan

articles.title: Bishop to parents: Don’t outsource raising of kids
articles.summary: Parents should not hand over the task of raising their children to others, accord ing to Military Ordinariate of the Philip pines Bishop Oscar Jaime Florencio.

blocks.text: Military Ordinariate of the Philip pines Bishop Oscar Jaime Florencio
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — Parents should not hand over the task of raising their children to others, accord ing to Military Ordinariate of the Philip pines Bishop Oscar Jaime Florencio.
Lessons learned at home, Florencio added, can last a lifetime and parents must remain their children’s first teachers, especially on faith and values.
“Do not give to other people the task of forming the children. What comes first will always be remembered,” Florencio said over the Church-run Radyo Veritas.

He made the appeal after presiding over a mass wedding at Santuario de San Vicente de Paul Parish in Quezon City on Thursday for 17 couples from the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology-National Capital Region.
Florencio said parents have a sacred responsibility to shape their children’s character from the beginning, when basic values and attitudes are first formed.
According to Florencio, families need support because they are the foundation of society and problems at home can eventually affect communities.
He urged parents to teach good values at home, saying proper formation can help children develop good character and may prevent youth violence in schools.
Florencio urged the newly married couples to build strong families and guide their children by teaching them to pray and honor God.
“We have a mission to build a family, a stronger family, and to form children, especially in the faith,” Florencio said.
Florencio assured families facing difficulties that the Church remains ready to accompany and support them, urging couples not to hesitate to seek help.

articles.title: Backflood, high tide inundate 71 Bulacan villages
articles.summary: Heavy rains dumped by the southwest monsoon inundated 71 villages in Bulacan yesterday.

blocks.text: Residents of Barangay San Juan and Palapat in Hagonoy, Bulacan, wade through floodwaters on August 22, 2026.
Michael Varcas / The Philippine STAR
MANILA, Philippines — Heavy rains dumped by the southwest monsoon inundated 71 villages in Bulacan yesterday.
The provincial disaster risk reduction management office (PDRRMO) said the deepest floods were monitored in Barangays Meysulao and Gugo in Calumpit town, with floodwaters reaching up to five feet.
Calumpit had the highest number of flooded barangays, followed by Guiguinto, Paombong, Hagonoy, Balagtas and Plaridel.
A total of 1,589 families or 5,511 people are currently seeking shelter in 47 evacuation centers, the PDRRMO said.
Classes have been suspended in all levels in both private and public schools in Balagtas, Baliwag, Malolos, Marilao, Norzagaray, Obando, Plaridel, Pulilan, San Jose del Monte, Santa Maria and Pandi.
In Pampanga, Gov. Lilia Pinedaon ordered the forced evacuation of residents in high-risk areas in the province as heavy rains continue. Some 3,400 families are now in 203 evacuation centers.
Pineda has also directed emergency responders to be on high alert status.
In Olongapo, a Chinese national and two Filipinos were buried in a landslide inside the Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority yesterday.
SBMA vice president Armie Llamas said they were already retrieved and taken to James Gordon Hospital.
Meanwhile, a portion of the Ninoy Aquino Bridge in Barangay San Isidro, Tarlac collapsed Friday night following heavy rains.
An initial assessment from the Department of Public Works and Highways said the bridge’s foundation was damaged due to strong current from the Tarlac River. Nobody was hurt in the incident.
Motorists were advised to take alternative routes such as the Agana Bridge as the DPWH and the city government are managing traffic in the area. — Emmanuel Tupas, Ric Sapnu

articles.title: Counsel: VP to try to comply with sub judice rule
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte “will try to comply” with the sub judice rule issued by impeachment court presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero, according to her counsel.

blocks.text: In this photo uploaded on Facebook on March 2, 2026, Vice President Sara Duterte personally visits residents affected by Typhoon Basyang at Iligan City Public Plaza.
Vice President Sara Duterte via Facebook
MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte “will try to comply” with the sub judice rule issued by impeachment court presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero, according to her counsel.

Paolo Panelo, counsel of Duterte in her perjury complaint against alleged bagman Ramil Madriaga, issued the reaction after Escudero reminded the Vice President that she is covered by the impeachment court’s two-strike policy on sub judice.
“I think she will try to comply with the ruling of the Senate impeachment court because that’s the criticisms against her, that she didn’t face the impeachment,” Panelo said.

“She faced it, her lawyers are there, she’s answering the question, her legal team is participating. Since she participated, I think she will try to comply with the directive of the Senate impeachment court,” Panelo said.

Escudero has ruled that the sub judice rule will be strictly enforced during the impeachment trial as he warned of public reprimand and admonition on the first offense and a P30,000 fine on the second.

In his lengthy ruling read in open court, Escudero warned the prosecution – both the public and private panels – and the defense teams that they could face contempt of court if they violated the sub judice rule.
“This rule is archaic, especially for public interest cases like this, impeachment. The counsels on both sides should really engage the media to explain to the people what happened,” Panelo added.
While letting go of past lapses, Escudero warned that lawyers found breaking the rule may be referred to the Supreme Court or the Integrated Bar of the Philippines for disciplinary action.

“Our opponent here is the unseen hand behind the shadows, the one trying to influence the outcome of the case. The antidote is going to the media and telling the people the merits of your case. That’s what both sides should be doing,” Panelo added.

Escudero said referrals will be based on the violations and breaches of the Code of Professional Responsibility and Accountability (CPRA) standards of courtesy, civility, fairness, candor or dignified language.
Senators back ruling
Sens. Erwin Tulfo and Juan Miguel Zubiri backed the strict enforcement of the sub judice rule imposing fines on the prosecution and defense and an ethics complaint on senators.

“The merits of this case must be fought and decided before the impeachment court, based on the evidence presented before us, not through sound bites, press conferences or competing narratives in the court of public opinion,” Zubiri said.
Zubiri also welcomed the court’s ruling to forgive the parties who had violated the sub judice rule and for the ruling to be applied prospectively or on succeeding offenses with a fine of P30,000.
Speaking to radio dwIZ, Tulfo said even senators should temper their language and be careful with their public statements about the trial.

Tulfo said judges should also listen to the sentiment of netizens after his brother Sen. Raffy Tulfo called hostile witness former Office of the Vice President disbursing officer Gina Acosta “stupid in the name of blind loyalty.”
Tulfo renewed his call for Col. Raymond Lachica to testify so that the senator judges can make a fair ruling and hear Lachica’s reason.
“We want to hear from the horse’s mouth,” Tulfo said.
Meanwhile, the House prosecution panel has appealed for leniency in the imposition of the sub judice rule.

Prosecution panel adviser and spokesman Ace Barbers said some flexibility in the rule could help the public understand the proceedings while respecting the boundaries set by the court. — Marc Jayson Cayabyab, Daphne Galvez

articles.title: Barbers offers compromise, seeks leniency on sub judice ruling
articles.summary: Fully aware of what's at stake, House impeachment adviser Robert Ace Barbers has sought leniency from the Senate impeachment court as far as the sub judice rule in Vice President Sara Duterte's trial…

blocks.text: Fully aware of what's at stake, House impeachment adviser Robert Ace Barbers has sought leniency from the Senate impeachment court as far as the sub judice rule in Vice President Sara Duterte's trial is concerned.
According to Barbers, the court must observe flexibility in order to help the public understand the high-stake proceedings.

“Personally ako, ang aking apela ay magkaroon ng leniency. Payagan ang ating ibang mga prosecutors as long as hindi sila magdi-discuss ng merito na makakapag-influence sa desisyon na maaaring gawin ng ating mga senator-judges,” he said on Aug. 29 during the the Saturday News Forum in Quezon City.
(Personally, my appeal is for leniency. Let our other prosecutors speak as long as they do not discuss the merits in a way that could influence the decision that our senator-judges may make.)
Presiding officer Senator Francis "Chiz" Escudero recently made a ruling that essentially prohibited parties from discussing merits of the trial outside the court.
With this, lawyers from the prosecution and defense panels could no longer or join press conferences.

Escudero's ruling prohibits public comments on disputed facts, witness credibility, the weight or sufficiency of evidence, the legal viability of a charge or defense, and the possible outcome of the trial.

But Barbers sees a possible compromise: he said prosecutors could, for instance, relay statements already made by witnesses in open court without commenting on their credibility or the weight of their testimony.
Barbers said some latitude could be considered given the sui generis, or unique, nature of impeachment proceedings and the public interest in understanding the trial.
“Sabi nga, itong impeachment ay sui generis. Baka sakaling pwedeng medyo luwag-luwagan natin dahil ang pinaka-objective sana ay ma-inform ang publiko kung ano iyong totoong nangyayari,” he said.
(As they say, this impeachment is sui generis. Perhaps we can be a little more lenient because the main objective should be to inform the public about what is really happening.)
He stressed the importance of helping Filipinos understand the impeachment process and what transpires during the trial.
Barbers said designated spokespersons for both the prosecution and defense could provide accurate information while helping counter misinformation.

“Itong pag-a-appoint ng mga designated spokespersons sa bawat panig, iyong defense at iyong prosecution, ay para magkaroon ng tama, accurate, at hindi fake news na mga impormasyon sa labas ng ating korte,” he said.

(The appointment of designated spokespersons for each side, the defense and the prosecution, is intended to ensure that the public receives correct, accurate, and non-fake-news information outside our court.)
His appeal notwithstanding, the former House quad-committee (quad-comm) overall chairman stressed that the prosecution team would comply with the court’s ruling.
Barbers also maintained that the sub judice restrictions should be applied uniformly to everyone covered by the ruling, including senator-judges.

articles.title: Iceland votes on whether to start EU membership talks in shadow of Trump's Greenland threats
articles.summary: About 265,000 Icelanders are eligible to vote in a referendum on whether to trigger European Union membership talks. Supporters say membership could offer stability and protection against possible…

image.caption: A person stands in a voting booth in Iceland's capital, Reykjavik, on Saturday. The yes-or-no national referendum asks: Should Iceland resume accession negotiations with the European Union? (Leonhard Foeger/Reuters)

blocks.text: World

About 265,000 Icelanders are eligible to vote in a referendum on whether to trigger European Union membership talks. Supporters say membership could offer stability and protection against possible threats from U.S. President Donald Trump, while opponents say it's unnecessary and could endanger rich fishing stocks.
About 265,000 Icelanders are eligible to vote in referendum

Voters in Iceland went to the polls on Saturday to decide whether the country should resume long-stalled negotiations to become a member of the European Union, in the shadow of U.S. President Donald Trump's threats to control nearby Greenland.
The yes-or-no referendum question is simple enough for the roughly 265,000 eligible voters: Should Iceland resume accession negotiations with the European Union?

A yes vote would trigger negotiations with the EU's executive branch, the European Commission, covering 35 areas — from the economy to human rights. Some supporters believe the EU could offer protections if Trump ever made similar threats against Iceland. They also see economic stability in joining the bloc.

If voters reject the proposal, that's it, for a generation at least. Opponents have rallied around the threat EU membership would pose to Iceland's rich fishing stocks and the fact that Iceland already reaps benefits from being in the EU's frictionless single market and the Schengen area free-travel zone.
Experts expect a close vote. More than 20 per cent of voters cast early ballots in advance of referendum day, Iceland's national broadcaster RÚV said.
Trump's Greenland threats

When Trump talked about U.S. control of Greenland, particularly at the start of this year, he shifted the mood in Iceland, just 290 kilometres from the self-governing territory of Denmark, a longtime U.S. ally.
Some Icelanders were particularly alarmed when he mistakenly named their country four times while speaking about his designs on Greenland.
Although Trump has indicated he won't use force to seize Greenland, his interest doesn't appear to have cooled.

items: Iceland referendum to restart EU membership talks will be held in 'coming months', PM says

blocks.text: The underlying worry among many in Iceland is clear: If Greenland is seized, is Iceland next? The ensuing question is clear, too: If yes, does EU membership provide a bulwark against any new Trump ambition in the North Atlantic?
Iceland's left-leaning coalition government, elected in 2024, certainly thinks so, and that's largely why it moved forward with the EU referendum that it had planned for next year.
"We can't really trust the U.S. anymore," said Hildur Knútsdóttir, a horror fiction writer who plans to vote in favour of EU membership.
Why Trump wants Greenland
Years of debate over possible EU membership
EU talk is nothing new in Iceland, which formally ended its previous effort to join the bloc in 2015, largely over concerns of what membership would mean for its rich fish resources.

The hefty cod and haddock catches from the chilled Arctic waters around Iceland are central to the national identity, too. Descendants of Vikings who settled in Iceland have lived off the sea for centuries.
With much of the country's economy geared toward its lucrative and well-managed fishing industry, fishing rights have been a talking point in the run-up to the referendum.

items: Trump's Iceland ambassador pick made a '52nd state' joke. Icelanders aren't laughing

blocks.text: Joining the 27-nation EU would require Iceland to be part of the bloc's common fisheries policy that would allow Spanish, Dutch and other trawlers into its waters. The government has indicated it would seek a special arrangement, potentially a full opt-out from the policy.

In the final days ahead of the vote, Iceland's prime minister, Kristrún Frostadóttir, has sought to remind voters that the referendum is not the end of the matter and that there will be another referendum if and when Iceland reaches a membership agreement with the EU.
"This is not an election about membership and not about adaptation, as there will be another referendum on an accession agreement if the result is yes," Frostadóttir told a rally.
Fish part of national identity
For many, Iceland's national identity and ultimately its culture are on the ballot.

Iceland, which gained independence from Denmark in 1944, has a proud history of refusing to be pushed around by bigger and richer European nations. It even fought — and won — the so-called Cod Wars with Britain in the 1970s over its fishing grounds.

Backers of EU membership say it's best for Iceland to get closer to its European neighbours to combat issues that don't respect borders, such as climate change. They also say the euro would bring more stability than Iceland's volatile króna currency.

Opponents say the current setup is just right and that Iceland already enjoys all of the benefits of European integration without the sovereignty compromises that inevitably come with full membership. They cite trade deals, such as one with China, that are more favourable.
"I think Iceland is better off outside of the EU, within the close collaboration with the EU," former prime minister Katrín Jakobsdóttir told The Associated Press.

articles.title: At least 37 dead and hundreds evacuated after strike on Kyiv weapons depot
articles.summary: An investigation has begun into the storage of weapons for Ukraine's military near a residential area.

blocks.text: Thirty-seven people have died and almost 400 have been evacuated after a Russian drone strike hit a depot storing weapons for Ukraine's military near a residential area on the outskirts of Kyiv.

The strike caused shells, mines and drones to detonate late on Friday, triggering a blast that damaged nearby properties including a care home for the elderly and disabled, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.
He said the storage site "definitely shouldn't have been there" and that an investigation had been launched into "terrible negligence on the part of those who stored explosive right next to people".
The attack is the second to hit a munitions depot near Kyiv in recent months, prompting renewed anger.
Four children are among the 42 people injured in Friday night's explosion, according to regional head Tymur Tkachenko, with a rescue operation ongoing at the site, in the Bucha district, on Saturday.

Russia's Ministry of Defence said in a statement that its forces had targeted "an ammunition depot" in Myla, a village to the west of the Ukrainian capital, holding "components and launch boosters for FP-1/FP-2 long-range unmanned aerial vehicles".
"Everything is completely damaged," local resident Liubov Pavlenko, 45, told the BBC after inspecting her home.
"There are cracks all around the entire perimeter, and cracks around the windows. Basically, the structural integrity has been compromised."
Zelensky said the decision to store explosives in the village was "absolutely unacceptable", adding: "Criminal proceedings have been opened on charges of official negligence."
The office of Ukraine's prosecutor general earlier said it was reviewing the "legality of the placement and storage of explosive objects and materials" near residential buildings in Myla.
It said the "actions of officials who made the relevant decisions" would also be investigated.
However, Zelensky earlier stated that "there are regulations in place - ammunition cannot be stored near homes or other residential areas", adding "appropriate conclusions will certainly be drawn".
He referenced the strike on an ammunition warehouse in Vyshneve in July, which caused a secondary detonation that killed nine, injured dozens more and damaged more than 280 homes.
Friday night's explosion has raised fresh questions about why munitions were being stored so close to people's homes, especially given the regularity of Russian aerial attacks.
"The authorities, the Ministry of Defence - why was this allowed at the depots, in a place where there used to be food?" Borys Daniyluk, 61, said.
"Why were ammunition and weapons stored there, next to a populated village? There are no words, just emotions."
Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky expressed regret that a "lesson" had not been learned following the explosion in Vyshneve.
The investigation into that incident revealed serious failings on the part of a state-owned company that had not complied with regulations regarding storage of explosives near residential buildings.
Zelensky indicated that the Myla depot had been operated by Ukraine's armed forces.
"In the fifth year of the full-scale invasion, making the same mistakes over and over is criminal negligence," Koretsky said on Telegram.
"Everyone responsible, without exception, must face severe punishment so that such situations never happen again."

Meanwhile, Tkachenko said a 14-year-old was killed in a separate attack in the Boryspil district, while Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said a two-year-old had died after a Russian drone crashed in Obolonskyi.

He added that five people, including an 18-year-old girl, were injured in fresh strikes on the capital on Saturday morning. Five people have been killed across the country over the past day, according to local officials.
Zelensky reported further overnight strikes in Odesa, Dnipropetrovsk, Sumy and Zaporizhzhia, as the Ukrainian army said it had shot down 233 Russian drones.
Russia and Ukraine have been intensifying their aerial attacks in recent months, with Kyiv focusing its operations on Russian economic targets.

Ukraine has for weeks struck sites belonging to Wildberries, the country's biggest online retailer, describing the firm as a legitimate target because it supplied components to the military, which Moscow denies.

articles.title: Michigan Senate candidate Mike Rogers says he saw Bin Laden’s body with his ‘own eyes’. He did not
articles.summary:
Ex-House intel committee chair, now running against Abdul El-Sayed, instead saw photo of Osama bin Laden’s body

In a recent fundraising email, the Republican candidate for

blocks.text: In a recent fundraising email, the Republican candidate for Michigan’s open US Senate seat, former congressman Mike Rogers, appeared to mislead supporters about his past by suggesting that he had played an active role in the killing of Osama bin Laden, the leader of al-Qaida who was shot and killed in an American military raid on his compound in Pakistan in 2011.

“When I served as a US army officer and an FBI special agent, I swore a sacred oath to defend the United States against all enemies, foreign and domestic,” Rogers wrote, according to a screenshot of the email shared online by Azi Paybarah, a former Washington Post reporter now with Straight Arrow News. “I dedicated my life to keeping our families safe – working in the shadows, hunting down terrorists, and standing on the frontlines of our national security.”
He then added, in a section of the email highlighted in bold type: “I saw the dead body of Osama bin Laden with my own eyes, knowing that together, we had delivered justice for America.”

Rogers, however, was not in Abbottabad, Pakistan, on 1 May 2011, when Bin Laden was shot and killed – nor was he in the White House Situation Room, where then president Barack Obama and senior administration officials at the time, including Joe Biden and Hillary Clinton, followed the raid in real time.

Instead, as Rogers told reporters the next day, and recounts in a campaign video, he was at home in Washington DC – where, as the chair of the House intelligence committee at the time, he was informed about the raid in a phone call from Obama’s CIA director, Leon Panetta.

While the Rogers campaign did not respond to requests to explain what the former congressman meant by his claim, Paybarah, who first reported the fundraising email sent by Rogers on Sunday, suggested that Rogers must have been referring to the fact that he was one of a select few US officials to have seen a photograph of Bin Laden’s dead body.
Rogers said – days after the raid – that the photograph he’d seen made it clear that Bin Laden was dead. But he said he supported Obama’s decision to not make the graphic images of the raid public.

“The risks of release outweigh the benefits,” Rogers said in a statement at the time. “Conspiracy theorists around the world will just claim the photos are doctored anyway, and there is a real risk that releasing the photos will only serve to inflame public opinion in the Middle East.”
In the years since, though, Rogers has frequently referred to his role as a congressman who helped provide funds for US intelligence agencies in vague terms that seemed to exaggerate his role.

Since Abdul El-Sayed, a Muslim doctor and former public health official, became his opponent in the Senate race, Rogers has repeatedly cited his own role in the US war on Islamist terrorism in his campaign statements.

“Abdul doesn’t represent a vision for the future. He’s leading a movement grounded in ideological fanaticism,” Rogers said the night that El-Sayed won the Democratic nomination. “I spent years hunting terrorists and bringing Osama bin Laden to justice. Never in a million years did I think that I would be running against someone who believes America deserved 9/11.”

A New York Times factcheck pointed out that the second part of Rogers’ “incendiary statement” was false: it was not El-Sayed, but one of his supporters, the Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who once said that American deserved 9/11, before retracting and apologizing for that statement seven years before he endorsed El-Sayed.
For his part, El-Sayed has clearly denounced the 9/11 attacks for years. In a recollection of that day written in 2021, El-Sayed wrote:

“I watched terrorists with names like mine attack my country in the name of my faith. Three thousand of my fellow Americans were killed in the craven terrorist attacks in New York, Washington DC and Pennsylvania. The attack devastated me.”

articles.title: Royal Navy spent three days tracking Russian vessels in UK waters
articles.summary:
Three vessels and a helicopter deployed to monitor four ships travelling through the North Sea to the Channel

The Royal Navy spent three days tracking Russian vessels as they passed through…

blocks.text: The Royal Navy spent three days tracking Russian vessels as they passed through UK waters, it has emerged.
The “intense” 72-hour operation took place last week, with radars used to monitor four ships that made their way from the North Sea through to the Channel.
The fleet was surveilled by HMS Duncan, HMS St Albans and HMS Severn, with a Merlin helicopter providing support, officials said.
The Russian destroyer Admiral Levchenko was observed escorting the cargo vessels General Skobelev and Sparta, which are under sanctions, towards Dover.

In response, Russia deployed its own military resources, including the Neustrashimy frigate, to guard the shipment. Gen Gwyn Jenkins, the First Sea Lord, said there was “no room for complacency” as shadow fleet vessels continued to pose “an unacceptable risk” to UK security.

“Alongside our allies, this approach is forcing Moscow to divert Russian warships away from their core purpose,” he said. “That is because Russia knows we stand ready to act again, should it be required.”

The Royal Navy recently warned of increasing Russian activity in UK waters. In July, it spent 21 days monitoring ships from Moscow, an increase of 25% compared with the previous year. Officials say they have repeatedly observed warships in the Dover strait and the North Sea.
In June, the Royal Marines seized the Russian tanker Smyrtos, the first time British troops have directly boarded a shadow fleet vessel, one of more than 500 that have been sanctioned by the UK.

The Kremlin has threatened the UK after Andy Burnham visited Kyiv this week in his first overseas trip as prime minister. During the trip, Burnham said the UK would provide Ukraine with military support, including blueprints for components of long-range Scalp missiles.
after newsletter promotion

Although western officials have tried to play down the prospect of direct conflict between Russia and Nato, the Kremlin has accused the UK and its allies of “playing with fire” in relation to their continued support for Ukraine.

Andrei Fedorov, a former Russian foreign minister, said he could not “100% exclude” the possibility of “semi-military” action against Britain in retaliation, raising the prospect of an attack on British drone factories from “unknown sources”.

articles.title: Number of missing in Nepal and Tibet rises to nearly 3,000 as operations continue
articles.summary: Nepal requests foreign ⁠help in identification and storing of bodies, DNA testing and rescuing people from tunnels

blocks.text: The number of people killed in the floods in Nepal has risen to at least 675, the country’s disaster authority has said.

Seven have also been confirmed dead in Tibet by Chinese state media, taking the total killed when a glacial collapse unleashed a deadly torrent through river systems in the Himalayan mountains to 682.

Seven bodies have also been recovered in India from rivers flowing from Nepal and are believed to be flood victims. The number of people missing in Nepal and Tibet was revised up to nearly 3,000 on Saturday.

blocks.caption: People put up posters of missing family members at a hospital in Kathmandu, Nepal. Photograph: Ahmer Khan/The Guardian

blocks.text: The missing list includes 517 foreigners and 933 workers on hydropower projects on the river where the torrent smashed down, Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said.
A number of rescue workers are also missing, including 45 Nepali army soldiers and 40 police officers.
When a Chinese rescue team reached the all-but-obliterated Gyirong border crossing complex for the first time on Friday, they found “nothing but ruins”.
Surveillance camera footage from the complex showed huge torrents of water and debris on Wednesday engulfing buildings and people trying to flee. Only ⁠on Friday were rescuers able to reach the area.

blocks.caption: The glacier on Mount Langtang Lirung in Nepal, before and after its collapse. Composite: Planet Labs/AFP via Getty

blocks.text: Amid the deepening crisis, Nepal has now said it needs foreign ⁠help in specialised and technical areas, but not in search and rescue. On ⁠Friday, Nepal’s foreign ministry had said that Kathmandu could manage ​the rescue ​efforts on its own for ​now and declined foreign involvement.

The areas in which Nepal is seeking help include opening transport and communication services in places where bridges have been destroyed, identification of dead bodies, DNA testing, rescuing people stuck in tunnels, and storing bodies for longer durations, the foreign minister, Shisir Khanal, said late on Friday.

blocks.caption: People search lists for the names of relatives rescued from cut-off areas after the flash floods in Nepal’s Nuwakot district. Photograph: Dar Yasin/AP

blocks.text: Khanal said ​there was no ​need for assistance in general search and rescue which was being done by Nepali rescuers. “We think there is no need for repetition in this,” he said.
Nepal has requested that its neighbours, India and ​China, provide bailey bridges to reopen transport and communication in an area where about two dozen bridges have been destroyed.
So far, India has sent three flights carrying about 60 tons of relief material to Nepal, including blankets, medicines, food and water purification tablets, ⁠and a specialised tunnel rescue team.

blocks.caption: An aerial photo shows houses along the Trishuli River destroyed by the floods. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty

blocks.text: China has also dispatched five tunnel experts from Tibet to Nepal for flood-related rescue work, Chinese state media reported, as the country called for emergency aid to be sent to disaster-hit areas and for international rescue cooperation.

blocks.caption: Nepali army personnel rescue survivors from a hydropower tunnel in Rasuwa district, Nepal. Photograph: Nepal Army Handout/EPA

blocks.text: Rescuers – including army personnel and police – have been clawing through mud and using drilling equipment to reach more than 100 people trapped inside a hydropower tunnel in Rasuwa. More than 350 people have already been evacuated from the site under “extremely risky” conditions and the office of Nepal’s prime minister said the rescue effort had become “extremely challenging” due to adverse weather.
Search and rescue operations were temporarily halted because of rain and fog but resumed on Saturday afternoon after the weather improved.

Kawan Koirala, a rescue worker from the Nepal Scout Disaster Response Team, said they had been struggling in thick, leg-sucking mud. “People want their family member’s body back, either dead or alive, but we cannot find them … you can see the mud,” he told Agence France-Presse, exhausted after an 18-hour shift.
Nepal is continuing to monitor two barrier lakes upstream of the flood zone, with an official warning that flood risks will persist until both lakes fully drain.
Satellite imagery showed the second lake growing larger with no visible outlet, raising concerns that water pressure could still be building.

blocks.caption: A woman salvages usable materials from her house deluged in sludge after flash floods at Devighat in Nepal’s Nuwakot district. Photograph: AFP/Getty

blocks.text: China’s state-run Xinhua news agency said that the first barrier lake was reducing in size, citing analysis by the water resources ministry. A Chinese government geohazards expert warned, however, that the lake may be ‌unstable and that more than 100 glacial lakes scattered throughout the area could pose a threat.

In Beijing, a politburo meeting chaired by President Xi Jinping called for stronger monitoring of glacier lakes and landslide risks, and for closer international disaster cooperation, Xinhua reported.

China’s Premier Li Qiang, the country’s No 2 official, arrived in the area of Gyirong on Thursday afternoon, Xinhua said. The visit suggested Beijing was treating the disaster as a matter of ​the highest national priority.

In China, strict controls on the flow of information from one of its most sensitive regions are hampering the public’s understanding of events. The BBC and New York Times have reported that videos of the catastrophic floods, widely shared globally, have not appeared on Chinese social media sites.
Tibet, brought under Chinese control in the 1950s, is the most sensitive and tightly controlled region in the country.

blocks.caption: On the ground in Nepal after deadly flash floods – video

blocks.text: The Gyirong border port plays a key role in China’s belt and road network linking the country to south Asia, with logistics zones and vehicle parks built there in the past decade.
Nepal’s finance minister, Swarnim Waglé, estimated the country will ⁠need $4-$5bn (£3-£3.7bn) for rebuilding. “This is just an ​estimate. Loss and ⁠damage is ​being assessed,” he ​said.
More than 90,000 people have been affected by the disaster, the Red Cross estimated.
Some of the bodies being recovered had decomposed beyond recognition and will need to be identified using DNA samples, Nepali officials have said.

articles.title: Trump administration video showing Haitian deportees in chains sparks outrage
articles.summary: A U.S. Department of Homeland Security video shows men, handcuffed and in chains, boarding a deportation flight to Haiti this week. Critics say the Trump administration is "bragging" about sending…

image.caption: Haitians deported from the United States arrive in Cap-Haitien, a coastal city in northern Haiti, on Thursday. In June, the U.S. Supreme Court allowed President Donald Trump's administration to move ahead with plans to cancel temporary protected status for Haitians. (Ketlain Difficile/The Associated

blocks.text: World

A U.S. Department of Homeland Security video shows men, handcuffed and in chains, boarding a deportation flight to Haiti this week. Critics say the Trump administration is "bragging" about sending Haitian immigrants "back to a war-torn country" after rescinding temporary protected status.
Homeland Security video shows men, handcuffed and in chains, boarding flight to Haiti
· CBC News
· Posted: Aug 29, 2026 10:57 AM EDT | Last Updated: 3 hours ago

A U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) video showing men in chains being walked onto an apparent deportation flight to Haiti has sparked outrage, with critics accusing Washington of sowing fear in Haitian communities as it ramps up deportations to the violence-hit country.
The video, shared on social media platform X late on Thursday, shows several Black men being led up a set of stairs onto a plane, their hands and feet bound and tied to a chain around their waists.

"Haiti TPS has been TERMINATED," reads the post, which said the footage was from a "Haiti repatriation flight" on Thursday. "Those with terminated TPS are in our nation Illegally. They have two options: LEAVE IMMEDIATELY or be DEPORTED."

Haiti TPS has been TERMINATED.

Those with terminated TPS are in our nation Illegally. They have two options: LEAVE IMMEDIATELY or be DEPORTED.https://t.co/Pahpi5pL2Z pic.twitter.com/uoPjNzqNM6—DHSgov

TPS refers to temporary protected status, a U.S. designation that allows foreign nationals to live and work in the United States without fear of deportation when conditions in their home countries are deemed too dangerous.

In June, the U.S. Supreme Court allowed President Donald Trump's administration to move ahead with plans to cancel TPS for Haitians despite concerns from lawyers and human rights advocates over deadly gang violence and instability in Haiti.
The move, which impacts more than 300,000 Haitians in the U.S., came into effect in late July.

items: Supreme Court says Trump administration can end legal protections for many U.S. residents from Haiti, Syria

blocks.text: "The Trump administration terminated TPS for Haitian families and is bragging about sending them back to a war-torn country," the Florida Democratic Party wrote on X, condemning the DHS video. "This isn't strength. It's depravity dressed up as policy."
Democratic Rep. Yassamin Ansari also commented on the post, saying amid "an endless barrage of depravity from the Trump regime ... this is among the worst."

Asked about the criticism, White House spokesperson Lauren Bis told CBC News in an email: "The federal courts have ordered the Haitian illegals must leave the U.S. and we have generously made free flights available to the destination of their choice."
What's next for Haitians who lost status in the U.S.
Haiti 'remains completely unsafe'
Aaron Reichlin-Melnick, a senior fellow at the non-profit American Immigration Council, said that "entire communities are living in fear" amid the crackdown on Haitian immigrants.

"Families are being torn apart and others are agonizing about their next steps; basic things [like] how to keep their loved ones safe," Reichlin-Melnick wrote on X, adding that Haiti also "remains completely unsafe."
The Caribbean country experienced a surge in gang violence following the 2021 assassination of then-president Jovenel Moïse, which created a power vacuum and worsened years of insecurity.

items: Haitians in the U.S. brace for deportation as Trump ends their protected status
At least 47 people killed in violent weekend attacks in Haiti, UN says

blocks.text: According to the United Nations, about 1.5 million Haitians are now internally displaced amid gang-related violence. At least 1,408 people were killed and 656 others were wounded across Haiti between April 1 and June 30 alone.
Last Sunday, at least 47 people, including five children, were killed in a gang attack in Kenscoff, a community overlooking the capital, Port-au-Prince. Dozens of people also were kidnapped.

Indrika Ratwatte, the acting UN assistant secretary general for humanitarian affairs, said on Friday that nearly 200,000 people had been forcibly returned to Haiti in the first eight months of 2026, despite "shocking levels of violence and suffering."

That's a 10 per cent increase compared with the same period last year, Ratwatte said during a special UN Security Council meeting on Haiti. "Many arrive without resources, documentation or support networks, and some have especially urgent protection needs."
Communities brace for more deportations
The New York Times reported this week that the U.S. government plans to speed up deportations to Haiti, going from one flight per month to one per week, after the cancellation of TPS.
CBC News asked the Department of Homeland Security for details on the Haiti deportation flight shown in Thursday's social media video and whether it plans to accelerate further removals.
In an email, a spokesperson said the department does not disclose information about such flights "for operational security and the safety of our personnel."

items: Canada urged to welcome Haitians fleeing U.S. deportations as Trump ends protected status

blocks.text: "Temporary Protected Status is exactly that — temporary. For too long, TPS has been allowed to function as a de facto amnesty program despite Congress never intending it to be permanent," the spokesperson said.

The New York Times said about 57 deportees arrived in Cap Haitien, a coastal city in northern Haiti, on Thursday's flight. The Miami Herald said children, including a three-year-old born in the U.S., were among those deported. Separately, the DHS said on Monday that it sent 162 Haitians back to the country on an Aug. 20 flight.

The Haitian Bridge Alliance, a group that supports Haitian immigrants in the U.S., said many aboard that flight had lost TPS. "This is our painful reality and the fear is striking in communities across the country," the group said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Jillian Kestler-D'Amours is a senior writer at CBC based in Montreal. You can reach her at jillian.kestler-d.amours@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Russian strike on ammunition depot near Kyiv kills dozens
articles.summary: Hundreds were also forced to flee after a Russian attack near Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, sparked a huge fire and explosions. The strike was the second to hit an arms depot near Kyiv in less than two…

image.caption: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country 'cannot be left alone in finding solutions to defend against' such drone strikesImage: Ukrainian Emergency Service/AFP

blocks.text: At least 37 people were killed after a Russian drone strike on a ammunition depot near Kyiv late Friday, one of the deadliest attacks in Ukraine this year.
The drone strike was the second attack to hit an arms depot near the Ukrainian capital in less than two months.
"A terrible situation and terrible negligence on the part of those who stored explosives right next to people," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a video address on X.

"Another such crime — after what happened in Vyshneve — is absolutely unacceptable," he added. Zelenskyy was referring to an attack on an ammunition warehouse last month that set off secondary explosions in the small town on Kyiv's western outskirts, killing ten people.

Russia and Ukraine have recently intensified long-range strikes, increasingly hitting civilian infrastructure such as logistics warehouses and oil and port facilities. These attacks have resulted in more civilian casualties.
What else do we know about the Russian drone attack near Kyiv?

The strike sparked a major fire and explosions at the arms depot in the Bucha district, close to the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv, forcing more than 370 people to evacuate the region. Dozens were injured.

Among those killed was Taras Didych, head of the Dmytrivka community, who was one of the first to rush to the scene to rescue people, according to Kyiv region governor Tymur Tkachenko. He also said the attack damaged at least 50 residential buildings.
Zelenskyy earlier said that criminal proceedings had been opened on charges of official negligence.
"There are regulations in place — ammunition cannot be stored near homes or other residential areas," Zelenskyy said.
Kyiv under jet-powered drone attacks
Friday's drone attack followed ​two days of constant air raids aimed at the Ukrainian capital and the surrounding region.

"Kyiv is under virtually nonstop attack from jet-powered drones. Ukraine cannot be left alone in finding solutions to defend against such strikes," said Zelenskyy, adding that Russia also struck nine other regions overnight.
It's been more than four and a half years since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of its neighbor.

articles.title: Ombudsman questions bail grants to graft convicts
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday questioned the granting of bail to some accused in graft cases before the Sandiganbayan, calling for convicted individuals to serve their jail terms more…

blocks.text: Published August 29, 2026 10:34pm

Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday questioned the granting of bail to some accused in graft cases before the Sandiganbayan, calling for convicted individuals to serve their jail terms more swiftly.

“Sabi ko, marami naman ang nasisintensiyahan. Maraming nasisintensiyahan ang Sandiganbayan pero halos kaunti lang ang nakakulong. Paano? Sinasabi, meron daw tayong presumption of innocence at right to bail,” Remulla said on his radio program.
(Many are being sentenced. The Sandiganbayan sentences many, but only a few end up in jail. How is that? They say there is a presumption of innocence and a right to bail.)

“Pero ‘pag ika’y na-convict na sa lower court, convicted na sa Sandiganbayan, na-convict na ng RTC dito sa graft, dapat iyan kulong ka na. Ang problema, medyo sobrang bait ng korte at hindi ginagawa ‘yung trabaho na ipakulong ‘yung dapat ipinakukulong,” he added.

(But once you have been convicted by the lower court, by the Sandiganbayan, or by the RTC in a graft case, you should already be in jail. The problem is that the courts are being too lenient and are not doing their job of jailing those who should be imprisoned.)
Remulla proposed that bail be set at an amount commensurate with the damage caused by the accused.

“Grant sila nang grant ng bail. Ang bababa pa ng piyansa. Dapat kasi diyan, ‘pag na-convict na ‘yung tao at talagang may petition for bail, ang bail should be set, if ever kung iga-grant mo ‘yan, at the cost of damage na ginawa ng tao.”

(They keep granting bail, and the bail amounts are even low. If a person has been convicted and there is a petition for bail, the bail, if granted, should be set based on the cost of the damage caused by the person.)
Remulla added that bail should be paid through a cash bond rather than a bail bond.
The Ombudsman said his office had requested an inventory of individuals convicted by the Sandiganbayan, including whether they had served time in jail.
Remulla also criticized what he described as the apparent leniency of the judiciary when accused individuals file motions for reconsideration involving bail.

“Basta’t nagkaroon ng motion for reconsideration on a grant of bail, parang walang deadline ang judiciary… May rules sila na dapat sinusunod, hihingi sila permiso, ipapa-extend nila. Pero paano ‘yan, uupuan na lang nila forever? Umaabot ng 15 taon ‘yung kaso, nakaupo lang,” he said.

"Once a motion for reconsideration is filed against a grant of bail, it seems as though there is no deadline for the judiciary. They have rules that must be followed, but they ask for permission and seek extensions.
"What happens then? Are they just going to sit on the case forever? Some cases drag on for as long as 15 years without a resolution.)
GMA News Online has sought comment from the Sandiganbayan and will update this story once a response is received.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Sarah Ferguson to return to UK after relocating amid Epstein revelations
articles.summary:
Former Duchess of York moved to Swiss chalet during fallout over her friendship with convicted child sex offender

Sarah Ferguson will return to the UK after relocating to a Swiss chalet amid…

blocks.text: Sarah Ferguson will return to the UK after relocating to a Swiss chalet amid the fallout over the friendship between her and her ex-husband, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, and the convicted child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, according to reports.

The pair were stripped of their royal titles in October over the scandal of their relationship with Epstein. According to the Sun, the former Duchess of York, 66, is renting a six-bedroom gated property in the home counties.
Ferguson used to live with Mountbatten-Windsor at Royal Lodge in Windsor until he was forced to vacate the premises and move to Marsh Farm on King Charles’s Sandringham estate in Norfolk.
She could “imminently” move into a new home, which has three bathrooms and a “granny annexe”, according to the Sun.

It is believed Ferguson has been spending time out of the public eye at a Swiss chalet in Verbier since leaving Royal Lodge, and her belongings were collected from Andrew’s home in Sandringham this week, the newspaper added.

Her expected return comes just days after the Duke and Duchess of Sussex arrived back in the UK with their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet. The family are expected to enjoy an “extended stay” in Britain, with the children enrolled at school and due to start next week.

Ferguson has faced calls to speak to US authorities about Epstein after last year’s release of millions of documents associated with him shed fresh light on their relationship. One email exchange suggested Ferguson had taken her daughters to see Epstein in the US days after he was released from prison for child sex crimes.
A year after his conviction for child sex crimes, Ferguson thanked Epstein for being the “brother” she had “always wished for” in an email.

Last September, the Mail on Sunday published emails from 2011, in which Ferguson privately described Epstein as her “supreme friend” and apologised for “letting him down”, despite having publicly called her association with him “a gigantic error of judgment”.

The messages were sent less than two months after she had insisted she would “never have anything to do with [Epstein] again”, amid pressure over the ties she and Mountbatten-Windsor had maintained with him – including a £15,000 payment Epstein made to help settle Ferguson’s debts.
Epstein has been the downfall of Mountbatten-Windsor, who was stripped of his titles by the King because of “serious lapses of judgment” over his friendship with the late child sex offender.
after newsletter promotion

Ferguson lost her courtesy royal divorcee title and reverted to her original name, and also lost the freedom of the city of York after councillors voted unanimously to remove the honour over her links to Epstein. She and Mountbatten-Windsor were given the honour as a wedding present from York in 1987 during a visit to the city.

The former duchess has published more than 50 books – largely children’s titles – but after the Epstein revelations, thousands of copies of her latest children’s book were withdrawn from sale and “pulped”.

Earlier this year, Ferguson’s international charity, Sarah’s Trust, announced its closure “for the foreseeable future”. Seven charities, including the Teenage Cancer Trust and children’s hospice, have also cut ties and revoked Ferguson’s patronage due to her links with Epstein.

Six companies linked to Ferguson – S Phoenix Events, Fergie’s Farm, La Luna Investments, Solamoon Ltd, Philanthrapreneur Ltd and Planet Partners Productions Ltd – were wound down in February after more damaging revelations came to light with the release of the Epstein files.

articles.title: Death toll from Nepal-Tibet floods rises to over 600
articles.summary: Heavy rain is complicating an already difficult rescue effort, as hundreds remain missing three days after deadly flash floods hit the Nepal-Tibet border region.

image.caption: More than 2,400 people remain missing following the floods in NepalImage: Athit Perawongmetha/REUTERS

blocks.text: The latest death toll from the devastating flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border was reported on Saturday to be over 600, as frantic rescue operations to search for hundreds of missing people entered a fourth day.
Figures from both countries put the number of missing close to 3,000, with 682 bodies recovered and reports of corpses swept as far downstream as India.
According to Nepal's disaster agency, the death toll there now stands at 675, with 2,426 people — including foreigners — still missing.
Across the border in Tibet, China's state news agency, Xinhua, has confirmed seven deaths and reported 554 missing individuals.
A glacial collapse on Wednesday sent rock, ice, mud and debris surging through the Himalayan mountain river systems below.
The flood swept through areas near the Chinese border, ravaging entire towns and damaging hydropower plants.
What is the status of rescue efforts in Nepal?
Rainy weather conditions are hindering aerial rescue operations in Nepal.
Nepal army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet told the media on Saturday that helicopter operations were on hold until the weather improved.
Rescuers are battling thick layers of mud in the affected areas, which is making it difficult for helicopters to land and take off.
Tunnels in the mountainous region are also a challenge, Basnet said.
The army has located people trapped in a tunnel of the Trishuli 3A hydropower project in Nepal's Rasuwa District. Over 100 people are believed to be inside the tunnel filled with mud.

Basnet said that rescuers were struggling to locate the entry points of the tunnel and had made use of baskets and ropes to reach some people. There are also limited places for helicopters to land in the area.

blocks.caption: Members of the Nepal Army load relief material as a helicopter containing relief supplies takes offImage: Athit Perawongmetha/REUTERS

blocks.text: On Friday, Nepal's Army shared visuals of some people being rescued from the tunnel. The survivors were seen stuck in the mud, while officials crawled through the sludge and held out their hands to them.
On Saturday, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal said a specialized tunnel rescue team had arrived from neighboring India and was ready to start work.
Nepalese authorities said the bodies of many flood victims have also been found dozens of kilometers from the disaster zone in Chitwan District in southern Nepal, which borders India.
Meanwhile, Indian authorities said they recovered the bodies of seven people who were swept downstream from Nepal and believe them to be flood victims.
More than 1,000 believed missing after Nepal flash floods
Nepal needs help in technical areas, says foreign minister
Late on Friday, Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the Reuters news agency that his country needed equipment, along with technical knowledge in tunnel rescue operations.

Khanal also told Reuters that Nepal did not need help with search and rescue operations but needed assistance in opening transport and communication lines in places where bridges were destroyed, identification of dead bodies, DNA testing and storage of bodies for a longer timeframe.
"We have already made requests for such ⁠specialized ​services and technical assistance in areas where we don't have enough expertise and technical know-how," ​Reuters quoted Khanal as saying.
Nepal's Foreign Ministry had on Friday declined foreign involvement in search and rescue.
Nepal's post-flood rebuilding estimated at $4-$5 billion
In another Reuters interview, Nepal's Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle said that the Himalayan nation may need $4 billion (€3.5 billion) ⁠to $5 billion ⁠to rebuild after the flood.
The estimate is equivalent ​to nearly a tenth of Nepal's economy.

"The initial estimate is ​between $4-$5 billion. Just an estimate," Wagle told Reuters, adding that the bill would be much less than what was needed in reconstruction after the disastrous 2015 earthquake — Nepal's worst ‌ recorded disaster.
"Loss and damage is being assessed," he said.

blocks.caption: People carry salvaged belongings from damaged houses following the flash floods and mudslideImage: Adnan Abidi/REUTERS

blocks.text: What do we know about rescue operations in Tibet?

In Gyirong, one of the hardest-hit areas in Tibet along the China-Nepal border, Beijing had temporarily halted its rescue efforts due to the risk of renewed flooding before announcing that the threat had waned.
China's Xinhua agency reported on Saturday morning that two villagers had been rescued in the Gyirong area.

blocks.caption: Rescue workers operate excavators and loaders to repair a damaged road leading to Gyirong PortImage: China Daily/REUTERS

blocks.text: The glacial collapse on Wednesday led to the formation of a barrier lake upstream due to debris dams. Experts warned that the lake had started to overflow.
On Saturday, Chinese authorities announced that the lake had begun to shrink.

China's state broadcaster, CCTV, cited the Ministry of Water Resources as saying that satellite imagery of the surface area of the lake in the Tsangpo River basin on Saturday morning showed a reduction of around 21,000 square meters compared to images from Thursday.
Authorities have also identified a larger body of water at the bottom of the glacier collapse.

"We estimate its area to be over 120,000 ⁠square ​meters, but its depth is currently unknown," Reuters quoted Chen Hongqi, a senior engineer at ​the Ministry of Natural Resources' Geological Disaster Technical Guidance Center, as saying.
Reuters also reported an official of Nepal's Disaster ​Management Authority as saying that flood risks will remain until the two lakes have fully drained.

articles.title: Number of missing in Nepal, China floods soars to nearly 3,000
articles.summary: NUWAKOT, Nepal — Rescuers in Nepal and China were still battling Saturday to locate thousands of people missing days after a deadly, tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept through the Himalayan…

blocks.text: NUWAKOT, Nepal — Rescuers in Nepal and China were still battling Saturday to locate thousands of people missing days after a deadly, tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept through the Himalayan region, engulfing villages.

The number of missing soared to nearly 3,000 Saturday, according to the latest figures from both countries, with 633 bodies recovered and reports that some of the dead may have been swept downstream as far away as India.

In an area home to vast energy infrastructure projects, Nepal’s disaster authority added 933 hydropower workers to a missing persons list that already included trekkers and pilgrims to Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash.
Those who made it out say they have lost everything and now face an agonizing wait to discover the fate of missing loved ones and the prospect of rebuilding their lives from nothing.
“All the settlements near the river were swept away. There is nothing left,” survivor Buddhi Ram Dangol told AFP.
Samjhana Thing said she had been waiting three days for news of her missing brother.
“We don’t know anything. Hopefully he is in a safe place,” she said.
‘Enormous’ trauma
The trauma of Wednesday’s catastrophe has been “enormous,” and as many as 93,000 people may have been affected, the Red Cross said, with the death toll expected to rise.
Emergency teams had been racing to retrieve survivors from affected zones, where the widespread devastation meant food and water supplies were running out.
Compounding the search for the missing are fears of further flooding in affected areas.
The deluge of ice and mud caused huge lakes to form, and one of these formations has become a direct threat to emergency workers scouring the region for survivors.
Nepali police urged all rescuers to “immediately move to a safe location,” saying they had received information that “a water dam has burst again on the Tibetan side.”

In Tibet, where Chinese authorities are the only source of information, Beijing suspended its rescue operation in the hardest-hit area of Gyirong over the risk of renewed flooding before saying the threat had eased.
State news agency Xinhua reported early Saturday morning that two villagers had been rescued in the area.
‘All swept away’
On the Nepali side of the border, the military located people trapped in the tunnel of the Trishuli 3A hydropower project, where they were working to find a way in to extract the survivors.
“Two helicopters have been dispatched, but it is challenging because it is tough to even locate the entry points of the tunnel,” army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP.
Some 350 workers and residents have been brought to safety from the site, he added, but efforts were ongoing to rescue more than 100 people trapped in the same area.
Workers rescued from other dam projects along the Trishuli valley described a disaster that unfolded with terrifying speed.
Buddha Tamang told AFP he survived only because he was inside a tunnel at the dam where he worked when the flood struck.
“The senior officers working on the other side, they were all swept away,” Tamang, who was airlifted on Thursday after being marooned for more than 24 hours, told AFP.
Nepal reported a death toll of 626 people on Saturday.
There are 2,426 people, including hundreds of foreigners, who are out of contact in Nepal.
Across the border in Tibet, which is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists, seven people died and 554 remain missing, state news agency Xinhua reported early Saturday.
Authorities also said they had evacuated 555 stranded tourists and 499 Chinese residents from Tibet.
In India, authorities said they had recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims.
Pilgrimage route
Scores of Hindu devotees from across the world are among those missing on the border, as many were on a pilgrimage to Tibet’s Mount Kailash.
Sivaranjani Muthunathan was traveling by bus with 56 others toward the Chinese border when they became stuck in what they thought was a traffic jam.
“Then there was fog, smoke, something that seemed to suddenly engulf us,” Muthunathan, 46, told AFP on Friday, showing a phone video she recorded of a torrent surging toward her.
Around them, vehicles were swept away or buried under mud.
“One by one, we also climbed out through the driver’s side,” then scrambled up a hill, she said. /das
