articles.title: Indonesian claims collegiate men’s singles crown
articles.summary: Gibran Berliangga of Indonesia made the most of his trip to the Philippines, capturing the collegiate men’s singles title of the PTTF Intercollegiate and Interscholastic Challenge on Friday evening…

blocks.text: Gibran Berliangga of Indonesia made the most of his trip to the Philippines, capturing the collegiate men’s singles title of the PTTF Intercollegiate and Interscholastic Challenge on Friday evening at the Home Court at Ayala Malls Manila Bay in Parañaque City.

The rising star from Jawa Barat defeated University of Makati’s EJ Yamson, 11-8, 11-9, 11-8, to claim the title in the tournament backed by the Huaching Foundation, Philippine Sports Commission, PLDT, Topcoms Marketing Inc., Mizuno Philippines, Cara Celine Dormtel, Gold Cross Security Agency, and Best Options Assistance Inc., along with Dino Jalandoni, Bombit Silva, and Eric Ongkauco.

Berliangga was among the more than 409 student-paddlers who took part in the biggest staging of the tournament to date, with participants coming from nearly all over the country, including the University of Mindanao.
Berliangga and Yamson earlier booked their spots in the semifinals with victories over University of Santo Tomas’ Jebb Datahan and De La Salle University’s Morrison Torres, respectively.
The Indonesian denied the Filipino upstart, Datahan, 11-4, 11-5, 11-9, while Yamson, a former DLSU Green Paddler, outlasted his former teammate Torres, 11-8, 11-13, 9-11, 13-11, 11-8.
The other completed events—the high school boys’ singles and boys’ doubles—went to the Philippines, with UST claiming the latter.

Top Filipino junior paddler Emmanuel Paculba Jr. stopped an Indonesian sweep of the men’s singles titles by taking the high school boys’ crown with a 6-11, 12-10, 11-8, 5-11, 11-7 victory over Muhammad Sayyid Sedi.

UST’s Ramon Canalin and Kieji Ridor completed their dream run with an 8-11, 11-6, 14-12, 7-11, 11-9 victory over Philippine Christian University’s top-seeded pair of NJ Marin and Kyle Ruedas in the doubles final.
Canalin and Ridor earned the right to represent the Junior Tiger Paddlers after sweeping Paul Agunod and Carl Sabandal, 11-9, 11-6, 11-9, in the semifinals.
Marin and Ruedas, meanwhile, defeated Indonesians Farel Deni Al Jabbar Nur and Muhammad Sayyid Sedi, 11-7, 11-7, 11-7, to arrange their finals showdown with the eventual champions.
Action in the team events and the playoffs for the collegiate women’s singles, men’s and women’s doubles, and high school girls’ singles and doubles was ongoing as of this writing.
Selected matches will be streamed live on the new and improved CPlay app and the One Sports YouTube channel.

blocks.text: At A Glance

items: CJ Perez said that there wasn't any conscious effort on his part to take over for Gilas Pilipinas in its 82-81 win over Jordan, noting that he only played his game and the breakout performance simply followed.

blocks.text: CJ Perez emerges as Gilas Pilipinas' sparkplug in its narrow win over Jordan. (FIBA)
CJ Perez said there was no conscious effort on his part to take over for Gilas Pilipinas in its 82-81 win over Jordan, noting that he simply played his game, and the breakout performance followed.
The San Miguel Beer star came alive when it mattered most, scoring all but two of his 16 points in the fourth quarter and overtime to emerge as a key spark in the Nationals' hard-fought victory.
“I just did my thing. No one told me to take over but I took it. I took the risk,” said Perez after the game.
“Pag mga ganung sitwasyon di ko na masyado naiisip (to take over) pero syempre sa kumpyansa ng mga teammates ko kasi nakakashoot na nga ako so binigay nila,” he added in a separate interview.

More than the scoring outburst, Perez made his biggest play down the stretch the stretch when Jordan’s defense finally collapsed on him, allowing him to find a wide-open Kevin Quiambao for the go-ahead triple with 11.7 seconds left.
“Ang mga coaches talaga nag trust lang talaga sila. They are telling me to just attack the basket. Pag nagtitouch ako ng paint naoopen yung iba and then nakakatira ako,” recalled Perez.
“Nasu-shoot ko kasi yung layup so nag collapse sila so luckily, nandun si KQ nakita ko siya and he made the shot. Sobrang kumpyansa ni KQ. I'm proud of him,” he added.

articles.title: Partial collapse of Aquino Bridge feared as rains persist in Tarlac City
articles.summary: TARLAC CITY — Authorities are closely monitoring bridges, roads, and other critical infrastructure in Tarlac City amid fears of further damage as continuous rains persist in the area following the…

blocks.text: TARLAC CITY — Authorities are closely monitoring bridges, roads, and other critical infrastructure in Tarlac City amid fears of further damage as continuous rains persist in the area following the partial collapse of Aquino Bridge.
Among these infrastructure is the Aquino Bridge, which was closed to all motorists after a portion of the structure collapsed at around 11:56 p.m. on August 28.

blocks.caption:
INFRASTRUCTURE AT RISK: Authorities continue to monitor bridges and other critical infrastructure in Tarlac City as heavy rains persist, following the partial collapse of Aquino Bridge and the threat of further flooding and damage.
(Photo courtesy of Tarlac City Government via Liezle Inigo)

blocks.text: INFRASTRUCTURE AT RISK: Authorities continue to monitor bridges and other critical infrastructure in Tarlac City as heavy rains persist, following the partial collapse of Aquino Bridge and the threat of further flooding and damage. (Photo courtesy of Tarlac City Government via Liezle Inigo)
The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) is conducting a technical assessment to determine the extent of the damage and the appropriate intervention needed to restore the bridge.
The city government is also closely monitoring Agana Bridge, which could face increased traffic pressure as motorists are being diverted there following the closure of Aquino Bridge.
Traffic management measures and alternative routes are being coordinated with the police, provincial government, and neighboring municipalities, particularly for trucks, buses, and heavy equipment.

blocks.caption:
INFRASTRUCTURE AT RISK: Authorities continue to monitor bridges and other critical infrastructure in Tarlac City as heavy rains persist, following the partial collapse of Aquino Bridge and the threat of further flooding and damage.
(Photo courtesy of Tarlac City Government via Liezle Inigo)

blocks.text: Flood-prone communities are likewise being monitored as the rains continue. The city government has conducted preemptive evacuation of families in Zone 3, San Isidro Tibag, Burot, and San Luis, while pumping stations, sandbagging operations, and other flood-control measures remain in operation.

The disruption caused by the bridge damage has also affected water service in several barangays, with San Isidro, Tibag, Baras-Baras, Dolores, Care, and Sapang Maragul experiencing low water pressure to no water due to damage to the water line crossing the bridge.
The city government has prepared a water truck as an augmentation measure.
Meanwhile, authorities appealed to residents to avoid unnecessary travel, keep children indoors, and rely only on official advisories.
City emergency responders and health centers remain on standby as the local government continues monitoring conditions and providing assistance to affected families.

articles.title: Quezon City orders forced evacuation in flood-prone areas
articles.summary: Quezon City has ordered the forced evacuation of residents in selected areas near slopes and flood-prone communities as rains brought by the southwest monsoon continued to affect the city Saturday,…

blocks.text: QCPD-DMFB personnel conduct a forced evacuation of residents underneath Dario Bridge in Barangay Bahay Toro, Quezon City, on Saturday, Aug. 29, amid heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or Habagat. (Photo courtesy of QCPD-DMFB)

Quezon City has ordered the forced evacuation of residents in selected areas near slopes and flood-prone communities as rains brought by the southwest monsoon continued to affect the city Saturday, Aug. 29.
The order covers parts of 11 barangays across Districts 1, 3, 4, 5, and 6, according to the Quezon City government’s 3:30 p.m. advisory.
In District 1, the affected barangays are Del Monte, Talayan, Ramon Magsaysay, and Bahay Toro, while Bagumbayan is included in District 3.
Kamuning and Obrero are covered in District 4, North Fairview in District 5, and Culiat, Pasong Tamo, and Apolonio Samson in District 6.
Meanwhile, several other barangays conducted preemptive evacuations in preparation for possible flooding brought by the southwest monsoon.
These include Talayan, Damayang Lagi, Pinagkaisahan, Kalusugan, Manresa, and Kristong Hari.

The Quezon City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Department (QCDRRMD) and barangay officials continued to coordinate evacuation and other safety measures for residents affected by the inclement weather.
The city government also urged barangays not included in the forced-evacuation list to conduct preemptive evacuations if they have areas experiencing flooding or facing the threat of landslides.
Residents needing emergency assistance may call the QC Helpline at 122.

articles.title: Skusta Clee faces backlash after canceled Parañaque show
articles.summary: Filipino rapper Skusta Clee faced criticism online after his scheduled performance in Parañaque was canceled amid heavy rain and strong winds, leaving some fans disappointed after waiting at the…

blocks.text: Filipino rapper Skusta Clee faced criticism online after his scheduled performance in Parañaque was canceled amid heavy rain and strong winds, leaving some fans disappointed after waiting at the venue for hours.
Several attendees and netizens expressed their frustration on social media, with some describing the incident as disrespectful and unprofessional.

Some also called for the rapper to be declared persona non grata in Parañaque, while others questioned the lack of a personal appearance onstage to explain the cancellation and apologize to the audience.
Critics also raised concerns about the way the cancellation was handled, with some claiming that the decision appeared to prioritize the safety of equipment rather than the fans at the venue.
The rapper's management, GT Entertainment, later issued a public statement to clarify what happened.

According to them, Skusta Clee and his team arrived at the Parañaque venue and were prepared to proceed with the scheduled performance. However, heavy rain and strong winds caused floodwater to engulf the stage area, eventually reaching instruments and production equipment.

After assessing the condition of the venue, the management decided to cancel the performance, citing safety concerns involving Skusta Clee, the musicians, technicians, and the rest of the production crew.
GT Entertainment also apologized to those who waited for the performance despite the bad weather and acknowledged their frustration over the cancellation.
“We sincerely apologize to everyone who waited and braved the bad weather,” the management said.
They added that the decision was made with the safety of everyone involved in the event as priority.
Some fans suggested that clearer and earlier communication could have helped manage expectations and lessen the disappointment among attendees.
As of writing, there has been no announcement regarding a rescheduled performance.

articles.title: Honda launches the Click125 Street and Click 125 Smart editions
articles.summary: Honda Philippines, Inc. (HPI) adds new variants to the Click125 series with the arrival of the Click125 Street and Click 125 Smart. Click 125 Street The Click125 Street now takes on a stylish visual…

blocks.text: Drive
Combining sporty character, advanced features, and reliable performance
Honda Philippines, Inc. (HPI) adds new variants to the Click125 series with the arrival of the Click125 Street and Click 125 Smart.
Click 125 Street
The Click125 Street now takes on a stylish visual look complemented by a new set of advanced features and technology.

The Click125 Street gets some fresh style and character with new graphics. Adding another layer of character is a set of naked handlebars for fresher look and added customizability. It is equipped with a full digital meter panel, which presents key information at a glance. An all-LED lighting system also gives brighter illumination and improved visibility.

Powering the Click125 Street is a 125cc liquid-cooled, PGM-FI, eSP Engine. It can return as high as 50.3km/L fuel consumption based on WMTC testing. This model rolls on wide tubeless tires that provide enhanced road grip and stability. Adding to the package is the wavy disc brake for responsive stopping performance.

The Click125 Street comes loaded with features like the Smart Key System, while the 18L luggage box offers a generous space for helmets and other essentials to bring along. At traffic lights, the Idling Stop System (ISS) helps in saving fuel by automatically turning the engine off and launching back smoothly with a simple throttle operation. The model also has a built-in USB-C charger that keeps smartphones powered, and a Combined Braking System (CBS) for a stable braking and safe riding experience.

The new Click 125 Street is available in Matte Cyber Grape Metallic, and Pearl Arctic White. The Click125 Street officially joins the Click125 lineup and is available at all Honda 3S Shops and authorized dealers nationwide with a suggested retail price of P90,000.
Click 125 Smart White
Another new variant is the Click 125 Smart Edition White. The new color variant brings a fresh look while still bearing the signature styling and performance of the Click125.

Like the Click125 variants, the Smart Edition White gets an all-LED lighting system that includes the headlight, taillight, position lights, and turn signals. It is also powered by a 125cc, liquid-cooled, PGM-FI, eSP Engine capable of achieving a 50.3km/L fuel consumption figure under WMTC testing, a Smart Key System, full digital meter panel, 18L luggage box, Idling Stop System and USB-C Charger.

As part of the major achievement of Honda’s journey, The Click125 Smart Edition White is set to commemorate the 10-Millionth Unit Production Milestone event. The Click125 Smart Edition Pearl Arctic White will be available for a limited allocation of 20,000 units only and will be available to all Honda Exclusive Shops nationwide.

“The Click125 Street brings a fresh take to the Click125 series with its bold and sporty character combined with advanced features and reliable performance. We believe this new variant gives riders another way to enjoy their everyday journeys while staying true to the quality and performance they expect from Honda. This is what we mean by a Game Changer Upgrade—giving riders an upgraded experience that fits their style and the way they ride today,” said Takeshi Kobayashi, President of Honda Philippines, Inc.

Pasay City Mayor Emi Calixto-Rubiano has ordered the city government’s emergency response units to remain on standby as Metro Manila faced a Red Rainfall Warning.
Rubiano directed the preparation of rescue vehicles and equipment for possible emergency deployment.
She also tasked the traffic and engineering departments with monitoring flooding, road conditions, and other hazards across the city.
The City Health Office, Pasay General Hospital (PasayGen), and health centers were likewise instructed to prepare for possible medical emergencies and ensure the availability of medicines.
Evacuation centers were also checked for adequate supplies of food and other basic necessities in case residents need to be moved to safer areas.
The mayor urged residents to remain vigilant and follow official safety advisories as the city continues to monitor the weather situation.

articles.title: Brgy officials in Tigbauan, Iloilo resign over foul odor, mosquitoes emanating from farm
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY— All nine officials of a barangay (village) in Tigbauan town of Iloilo province are going to resign over a problem with a poultry farm. Barangay Captain of Rene Taño Linobayan led the…

blocks.text: Barangay officials of Linobayan, Tigbauan town, Iloilo province. (Photo from Barangay's Facebook page)
ILOILO CITY— All nine officials of a barangay (village) in Tigbauan town of Iloilo province are going to resign over a problem with a poultry farm.
Barangay Captain of Rene Taño Linobayan led the submission of their mass resignation to Tigbauan Mayor Virgilio Teruel this week.

The resignation of Taño as well as Barangay Kagawads Joesa Mae Mendez, Mary Rose Agapay-Sagala, Leticia Trespecios, Leticia Tasic, Rico Taño, Johnny Vale, and Efren Tayag; and Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) chairperson Ejelyn Claire Casio are set to take effect on September 10.
According to Taño, the mass resignation is a protest over the problem that escalated with a poultry farm in neighboring Barangay Sipitan.
It was last year that Linobayan residents started complaining of the foul odor and the presence of mosquitoes.
Barangay officials led by Taño reported it to the local government unit (LGU), which sent an inspection team that found that the odor was "minimal".
This did not sit well with residents while Taño and other barangay officials are facing a civil damages case filed by the new owner of the poultry farm.
On his part, Teruel urged the barangay officials to reconsider their decision to resign as it would impact the services in Barangay Linobayan.
The Local Government Code stipulates that resignations of barangay officials only can take effect if it's accepted by the municipal mayor.
Teruel also denied that the LGU of Tigbauan under his administration did not properly take action against the problems caused by the poultry farm.

articles.summary: SANTA ANA, Cagayan — The body of a 54-year-old fisherman who went missing after his motor banca was recovered by the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) in Santa Ana, Cagayan on Friday, August 28. The Coast…

blocks.text: SEARCH ENDS IN TRAGEDY: Coast Guard personnel recover the lifeless body of a 54-year-old fisherman who was reported missing after his motor banca was found aground in Barangay Palawig, Santa Ana, Cagayan. (Photo courtesy of Coast Guard via Liezle Inigo)
SANTA ANA, Cagayan — The body of a 54-year-old fisherman who went missing after his motor banca was recovered by the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) in Santa Ana, Cagayan on Friday, August 28.

The Coast Guard District North Eastern Luzon (CGDNELZN), through Coast Guard Station Santa Ana and Coast Guard Sub-Station Palaui, recovered the victim during a search and rescue operation launched after his disappearance was reported.
Authorities said the fisherman was reported missing after his motor banca was found along the shoreline of Barangay Palawig.
Coast Guard personnel immediately coordinated with local authorities and maritime agencies and mobilized search teams.
Nearby Coast Guard units were also directed to conduct search efforts within their respective areas of responsibility.
The search later focused on waters beneath Palawig Bridge, where the SAR team located and recovered the victim’s body.
The remains were positively identified by the victim’s relatives and brought to the Rural Health Unit of Santa Ana for proper disposition and turnover to the family.

articles.title: PNP assisting school security guards to ensure students' safety in Quezon
articles.summary: CAMP NAKAR, Lucena City- The Quezon Provincial Police Office (PPO) is maximizing the deployment of police personnel to assist school security guards, particularly in public schools, and ensure…

blocks.text: Police Col. Romulo Albacea, Quezon police director, interviewed with the media on police assistance to public schools in Quezon. (Danny Estacio)

CAMP NAKAR, Lucena City- The Quezon Provincial Police Office (PPO) is maximizing the deployment of police personnel to assist school security guards, particularly in public schools, and ensure security checks on students coming to the school campuses in Quezon province.

Police Col. Romulo Albacea, Quezon police director, said in an interview with the media here that police chiefs have been directed to assist the security of the school guards in preventing students from bringing unallowed things while attending their classes.
"Police have no authority to intervene in the school's policy; only police primarily duties are to extend assistance," he said.

Albacea encouraged schools’ administration to use their security forces with metal detectors and other instruments for checking bags as fast as possible, most especially those schools with a huge number of students.

He added that the only role of the police is to assist with police visibility within the surroundings of the school to prevent students from unlawfully doing what happened recently, the shooting incidents in Zamboanga and in Tacloban City.
He advised those police personnel who were assigned to the school not to display guns while assisting the school’s security forces.
Albacea added that only they can provide security assistance to public schools, but in the case of private schools, it depends on the request of the school administrators.

articles.title: Dutch health institute issues 'red alert' over Trump-shaped ecstasy pills
articles.summary: The drugs have a delayed effect which "increases the risk of overdose", the health institute says.

blocks.text: A Dutch drug addiction and mental health institute has issued a "red alert" to users about potentially lethal ecstasy pills which resemble US President Donald Trump.
The Utrecht-based Trimbos Institute said several of the pills had been handed in at testing centres in August and were found to contain a "very high" amount of the chemical PMMA.
"Do not use this pill under any circumstance," the institute said in its warning, cautioning that the drug could cause "overheating with potentially fatal consequences".
It issued images of the pills, which feature a depiction of Trump's face on one side and the words "Trump" and "NL" stamped on the other.
PMMA, or para-methoxymethamfetamine, is a substance similar to MDMA – the active ingredient in ecstasy pills.
"However, the effect occurs later, and the stimulating effect is often absent," the health institute advised. "This increases the risk of overdose."
Users are being warned they could experience symptoms such as nausea, an increased heart rate and convulsions hours after ingesting the pills.
Trimbos Institute spokesperson Anniek Groothuis told the Associated Press that it had no reported cases of death or serious illness among possible users.
While producing, selling and using ecstasy is illegal in the Netherlands, a 2024 Dutch government report said the substance was "still quite popular as a party drug".
The report added that, in 2022, a "record 550,000 people" had taken the drug at least once.
This is not the first time Donald Trump's facial features appear to have been used as inspiration for the shape of ecstasy pills.

In 2017, German police confiscated about 5,000 carrot-coloured ecstasy tablets in the shape of the US president's head – which they believed had been promoted on the internet under the slogan "Trump makes partying great again".

blocks.text: Evacuees take shelter at the Palanyag Gymnasium as heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon, or habagat, continue to affect several areas (Photo from Parañaque PIO)

A total of 177 families or 562 individuals have sought shelter in seven evacuation centers in Parañaque City as continuous rains from the southwest monsoon, or habagat, prompted residents in several barangays to evacuate.
Mayor Edwin Olivarez ordered the continued monitoring of flood-prone areas and the readiness of evacuation centers as rains persisted across the city.
Olivarez said 10 evacuation centers in five barangays are currently open to accommodate additional residents who may be forced to leave their homes due to worsening weather and flooding conditions.
In Barangay BF Homes, 43 families or 151 individuals are staying at the Phase 3 Gymnasium, while five families or 13 individuals are at the Phase 1 Gymnasium.
Another 11 families or 36 individuals have taken refuge at the Barangay San Antonio Hall.
In Barangay San Dionisio, 32 families or 103 individuals are staying at the Palanyag Gymnasium.

Barangay San Isidro recorded the highest number of evacuees, with 70 families or 199 individuals at Santos Multipurpose Hall, followed by nine families or 39 individuals at Lopez Village Multipurpose Hall, and seven families or 21 individuals at Silverio Elementary School.
City authorities continue to monitor affected areas and keep the other evacuation centers on standby for possible additional evacuees as the habagat continues to bring rains.

articles.title: Nepal-China flood survivors reach safe areas as families await news of nearly 3,000 missing
articles.summary: NUWAKOT, Nepal (AP) — Most arrive with nothing except the clothes they are wearing. As rescue efforts in communities buried by catastrophic flash floods along the border between Nepal and China…

blocks.text: NUWAKOT, Nepal (AP) — Most arrive with nothing except the clothes they are wearing.

As rescue efforts in communities buried by catastrophic flash floods along the border between Nepal and China entered their fourth day Saturday, authorities continued finding survivors and transporting them to safety. At relief centers, as some arrive, families wait anxiously for news of their loved ones as the death toll and the number of people unaccounted for continued to rise.

After Nepali authorities updated their figures Saturday, the combined toll in Nepal and Tibet rose to 633 dead and nearly 3,000 people missing. Chinese authorities have reported seven deaths and more than 550 missing.
In Nuwakot, one of the Nepali districts devastated by the floods, helicopters resumed operations before noon Saturday after poor weather temporarily hampered aerial rescue activities.
Some helicopters were loaded with boxes and bags of aid, including clothes, instant noodles, crackers and rice. Others returned from the flood-hit areas carrying survivors.

An older man was carefully helped off one helicopter, while a soldier carried an older woman on his back to a medical tent. There, medics checked her blood pressure, breathing and heartbeat, as well as her teeth and gums.
About a dozen people emerged from another helicopter. Soldiers carried several babies who had also been evacuated.
The evacuees had been brought from the nearby community of Trishuli.
Villagers return to devastated homes
As people were still evacuating from Trishuli, some village residents were returning to see what could be salvaged from their decimated homes.

One boy walked out of the village carrying muddy sandals from his house. Another woman, Shoba Shretha, returned to find her dog, Sweetie, who she was forced to leave behind when the floods came. Shretha sat on the ground petting her and feeding her water from a bottle.
At some point, relief coordinators cleared villagers, press and volunteers from the entrance to Trishuli, as excavation equipment drove into the flooded village, continuing to dig.
Families begin to lose hope

In Kathmandu, Nepal's capital, relatives and friends gathered outside the main government hospital from early morning, desperately searching for news of loved ones who remain missing after the incident.
Many shuffled between the help desk and the hospital notice board, clutching photographs and scanning injured patients' lists in the hope of finding them.

Dil Maya Lama stood weeping outside the help desk at the hospital, searching for any information about her missing brother. She travelled from Ramechhap district on Saturday in search of her 26-year-old brother, a driver for a hydropower company in Rasuwa.
"I came here with the hope that I might find him," she said. "There is no information about him."
Nelza Moktan anxiously sought information about her missing cousin, who also worked as a driver in Rasuwa.
"I feel hopeless. It has already been four days," she said.

Families covered hospital walls with posters showing missing relatives, displaying photographs and contact numbers in a desperate appeal for any clue that could bring them home. Nearby, officials had also pasted photographs of bodies yet to be identified in hopes they could be recognized by families or friends.

Gajendra Rawat, a security official at the hospital help desk, said families had so far registered around 1,600 missing persons since the disaster struck. "People are coming from all parts of Nepal," he said.
Back in Nuwakot, military personnel taped sheets of paper listing dozens of missing people to a wall at a relief center, prompting families to crowd around and search for their relatives.
Some scanned the lists, took photos and wiped away tears as they looked through the names.
Rajesh Kumar Ram, who is searching for his son, desperately scanned a list of names.
"I'm hopeful, by chance that my son is somewhere," he said, crying as he spoke. "Maybe they find him stuck somewhere. I'm waiting for that moment only."
Outside, people walked along mud-covered streets past signs of the disaster. On one street, a truck was stuck in the mud with its bed raised in the air.
Rescuers battle to find survivors at disaster-hit areas

Search and rescue efforts continued at several locations in Nepal and China's Tibet, including the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project in Nepal's Rasuwa district and the severely damaged Gyirong border crossing on the Chinese side.

Nepali Army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said rescue efforts would continue at the hydropower construction site, where authorities believe more than 100 people are trapped in a tunnel filled with thick mud.

Basnet said rescuers had used baskets and ropes to reach some people, but the operation remained difficult because of 4 to 5 feet (1.2 to 1.5 meters) of mud and the limited number of places where helicopters could land.
He said rescue teams had also been forced to relocate temporarily when authorities issued warnings about possible further flooding.

Rescuers have been on high alert for more flooding from a new lake that formed high up in the Himalayan mountains after the initial floods Wednesday. Experts warned that the lake, created after a glacier collapse that triggered the floods, was starting to overflow.

Monitoring data from the Chinese Ministry of Water Resources showed late Friday that the lake had dwindled in size. The water level dropped by 10 meters (32 feet) from the high point on Thursday morning, Chinese broadcaster CCTV said.
Aid trucks could be seen traveling from Kathmandu, Nepal's capital, toward the affected areas.
Search continues at devastated China-Nepal border crossing

The broadcaster was showing Saturday images of rescuers getting to Gyirong Port, the hard-hit border crossing with Nepal. Some reached the area by foot and via rafts. Some were dropped down from drones flown to the area. "Anyone, anyone?" rescuers yelled, according to footage by the broadcaster.
It was not immediately known how many people were at the border checkpoint building when the floods hit.

On Saturday, Nepal's disaster agency said the death toll had climbed to 626 with 2,426 people missing in the country. There was little information on survivors on the Chinese side, where the death toll rose to seven Friday as state media showed evacuations of villages and leaders' efforts to direct the relief response.

More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far. China's state media said 554 people were missing on the Chinese side. Hundreds of the missing are foreigners who were in the area to work, trek or make a pilgrimage to a sacred peak.

articles.title: Valenzuela families evacuate as floods rise
articles.summary: Hundreds of families were forced to evacuate in Valenzuela City on Saturday, Aug. 29, as continuous rains caused flooding in several areas. As of 4 p.m., the city government recorded 609 families…

blocks.text: Hundreds of families were forced to evacuate in Valenzuela City on Saturday, Aug. 29, as continuous rains caused flooding in several areas.

Evacuation tents are set up at a designated evacuation center in Valenzuela City on Saturday, Aug. 29, as hundreds of families sought shelter amid flooding caused by continuous rains. (Photo courtesy of Valenzuela LGU)
As of 4 p.m., the city government recorded 609 families staying in 17 evacuation centers across the city amid the Red Rainfall Warning over Metro Manila.

Valenzuela National High School in Barangay Marulas had the highest number of evacuees with 155 families, followed by Luis Francisco Elementary School in Barangay Veinte Reales with 98 families and Lingunan Elementary School with 68 families.
Other affected families sought shelter in evacuation centers in Veinte Reales, Malanday, Punturin, Balangkas, Pasolo, Lawang Bato, Dalandanan, Arkong Bato, Bagbaguin, Parada, Caruhatan, and Maysan.
The city government said hot meals and other assistance were being provided to evacuees with the help of barangay officials.
Residents in flood-prone areas were advised not to wait for floodwaters to rise further before evacuating and to coordinate with their barangays for assistance.
Meanwhile, several roads remained flooded as of 2:55 p.m.
Floodwaters along Monte Carlo Street in Lingunan reached around 43 inches or chest level, while P. Gregorio corner Trinidad Street recorded around 38 inches.
Lingunan Bridge and the Rubber Master area also recorded waist-deep flooding and were not passable to all types of vehicles.
Other impassable areas included Maxxima and Mayers in Lingunan, Wil Oil along Maysan Road, and portions of MacArthur Highway in Marulas.
Several sections of MacArthur Highway in Dalandanan were also not passable to light vehicles due to floodwaters reaching around 13 inches.
The local government said it continues to monitor flood and road conditions and urged residents to remain alert.

articles.title: DOH warns public vs deadly leptospirosis amid ‘habagat’ floods
articles.summary: Amid continued heavy rains and flooding caused by the southwest monsoon, or “habagat,” the Department of Health (DOH) on Saturday, Aug. 29, warned the public against bathing, playing, or wading in…

blocks.text: (MB FILE PHOTO)

Amid continued heavy rains and flooding caused by the southwest monsoon, or “habagat,” the Department of Health (DOH) on Saturday, Aug. 29, warned the public against bathing, playing, or wading in floodwater due to the risk of leptospirosis and other waterborne diseases.
“‘Wag maligo o maglaro sa baha (Do not bathe or play in floodwater),” the DOH said in an advisory.
The health department said floodwater may be contaminated with urine from infected animals, including rats, and may cause leptospirosis.

“Ang tubig-baha ay madumi at posibleng maging sanhi ng impeksyon tulad ng Leptospirosis at iba pang waterborne diseases (Floodwater is dirty and may cause infections such as leptospirosis and other waterborne diseases),” it said.
The DOH warned that complications from leptospirosis may lead to costly medical treatment and death.

“Hindi biro ang mga komplikasyon na dulot ng Leptospirosis, maaari itong mauwi sa malaking gastos ng gamutan at pagkamatay (The complications caused by leptospirosis are serious and may result in costly treatment and death),” it said.

blocks.caption: (MB FILE PHOTO)

blocks.text: The agency advised those who waded in or were exposed to floodwater to immediately consult the nearest health facility, health center, or YAKAP Clinic, regardless of whether they have wounds, to determine if they need doxycycline prophylaxis.

“Kung ikaw ay lumusong o na-expose sa baha, may sugat man o wala, magpakonsulta agad sa pinakamalapit na Health Center o YAKAP Clinic upang malaman kung kailangan mo ng doxycycline prophylaxis (If you waded in or were exposed to floodwater, whether or not you have a wound, immediately consult the nearest health center or YAKAP Clinic to determine whether you need doxycycline prophylaxis),” the DOH said.
Likewise, the DOH cautioned the public against taking doxycycline without a doctor’s prescription.

On Friday, Aug. 28, the DOH reported 5,486 leptospirosis cases nationwide from Jan. 4 to Aug. 26 and warned that infections may continue to rise over the next two weeks following recent rains and flooding.
DOH Undersecretary Gloria Balboa said the figure was 23 percent lower than the 7,163 cases recorded during the same period last year.

articles.title: 'Fake news pala, ha?': Ping gives details of 4 'fraudulently' titled, illegally reclaimed lands in Taguig
articles.summary: Senator Panfilo "Ping" Lacson has dispelled insinuations that his earlier disclosures on the illegal reclamation activities in Taguig City were “fake news". In an X post on Saturday, Aug. 29, Lacson…

blocks.text: Senator Panfilo "Ping" Lacson has dispelled insinuations that his earlier disclosures on the illegal reclamation activities in Taguig City were “fake news".

In an X post on Saturday, Aug. 29, Lacson said the four parcels of illegally reclaimed land in Taguig City have been initially identified as covered by "fraudulently" issued land titles, while at least four other parcels have no plotted title lots in the digital file of the Land Registration Authority (LRA).
"Since Sen. (Alan Peter) Cayetano keeps publicly asking for evidence, I’ll give it to him, in the spirit of public interest," he said, referring to the Senate Minority Leader.
Lacson said the details of the four "fraudulently" titled parcels, which he stressed was "NOT FAKE NEWS," include:
(a) one covered by an Administrative Patent, involving 9,204 square meters under an Original Certificate of Title (OCT);
(b) one covered through Judicial/Ordinary Land Registration Processing covering an area of 5,000 square meters under an OCT;
(c) one covered by a Homestead Patent involving 181,077 square meters under a Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT); and
(d) one involving 193,027 square meters under a TCT.
Some details, including the names of those to whom the titles were issued to, as well as the OCT and TCT numbers, were withheld for the time being as the investigation is still ongoing.
"All of these will likewise be turned over to the Ombudsman fact-finding team for their further appropriate action," he added.

Earlier, Lacson bared that the LRA was checking the origin and history of several newly uncovered land titles covering some 38.83 hectares of illegally reclaimed areas on the Taguig City side of Laguna Lake.
The uncovered land titles were based on the materials provided by the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA) to Lacson's office.

“I requested the LRA to backtrack the history of the issued OCTs (original certificates of title) and other modes of titling, so we will find out how they were manipulated with the end in view of filing criminal charges against those responsible,” Lacson said,
He added that these titles may be declared void ab initio (void from the start) once the PRA initiates forfeiture proceedings in accordance with law.

Earlier, Lacson said several crates of documents from the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) related to anomalous projects in Taguig City were also set to be turned over to the Office of the Ombudsman.

articles.title: US, Ecuador forces strike alleged drug smuggling boat
articles.summary: Tackling drug trafficking in Latin America is a key priority for Washington. In March, Ecuador joined a US-led coalition to combat the drug trade in the region.

image.caption: The US military said the people on board were escorted to Ecuador before the vessel was destroyedImage: U.S. Southern Command/SOUTHCOM

blocks.text: The US military said on Friday it had destroyed an alleged drug trafficking boat in a coordinated operation with Ecuador.
In a post on X, US Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) said that its forces intercepted a vessel "operating as a floating refueling station" in the Eastern Pacific.

According to SOUTHCOM, the vessel was operating "in support of the Los Choneros violent narco-terrorist organization," referring to one of Ecuador's most powerful criminal gangs, which Washington has designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organization.

"Working together with our Ecuadorian partners, our coalition dealt a decisive blow to a narco-terrorist operation responsible for moving significant amounts of drugs through the region," SOUTHCOM said.
US, Ecuador combat drug cartels
In March, Ecuador joined President Donald Trump's "Shield of the Americas" — a US-led coalition focused on combating drug trafficking across the region.
Ecuador's strategic location between Colombia and Peru — the world's two largest producers of cocaine — makes the country a key transit hub for drug-trafficking gangs.
The US military launched Operation Southern Spear in September 2025 as part of a fight against drug trafficking in the region.
The Trump administration, however, has not presented definitive evidence that the vessels targeted in its operations were carrying or transporting illegal drugs.

articles.title: Heart Evangelista gets pushback over 'late is late' comments
articles.summary: Heart Evangelista’s no-excuses stance on tardiness has drawn mixed reactions online, with some agreeing with her call for punctuality while others said her comments overlooked the realities faced by…

blocks.text: Heart Evangelista’s no-excuses stance on tardiness has drawn mixed reactions online, with some agreeing with her call for punctuality while others said her comments overlooked the realities faced by ordinary workers and commuters.
Evangelista recently posted her thoughts on people who arrive late, making it clear that she considers tardiness a matter of respect and professionalism.
“Late is late. There’s no excuse,” she said.
“You want to work? Be there on time. You’re being paid, so respect other people’s time,” she added.
She also addressed traffic, a common reason cited for being late, telling people to leave earlier and adjust their schedules if they know delays are likely.
“But if you’re going to give me a lousy excuse like traffic, then let’s not work together,” Evangelista said.
Some netizens agreed with her position and shared their own experiences of waiting for people who arrived late.
“I love that principle,” one user commented.
Another wrote, “You’re right, Miss Heart. Being punctual and respecting other people’s time is a sign of professionalism and genuine regard for work. I salute you for standing by your principles.”
But others pushed back, particularly at Evangelista’s suggestion that workers should simply leave earlier to avoid traffic-related delays.
One critic wrote, “So dramatic, hahaha. You’re not exactly an ordinary person. Don’t compare yourself to others. You don’t have the same responsibilities in life.”
Another netizen brought up Evangelista’s husband, Sen. Chiz Escudero, saying her comments failed to take into account the daily realities of ordinary Filipino commuters.

“Imagine saying this while your husband is a senator who could make a huge difference in the lives of Filipinos, considering that the majority of us are commuters and don’t have a ton of cars like the class this person comes from,” the user wrote.
The same netizen accused Evangelista of blaming workers for traffic problems that they argued are rooted in car-centric development.

The reactions turned Evangelista’s simple point about punctuality into a broader discussion about privilege, commuting and the very different circumstances faced by workers trying to get to work on time.
Evangelista has not commented further on the reactions.

articles.title: Michael V. to new grads: ‘Make yourselves impossible to replace’
articles.summary: Michael V. may be one of the country’s most recognizable entertainers, but when he returned to his alma mater as a commencement speaker, he had a very 2026 message for the newest batch of graduates:…

blocks.text: Michael V. may be one of the country’s most recognizable entertainers, but when he returned to his alma mater as a commencement speaker, he had a very 2026 message for the newest batch of graduates: Don’t let AI make you obsolete.
The Kapuso Comedy Genius returned to the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) on Aug. 28, not as a student this time, but as one of the speakers for the university’s 58th Commencement Exercises.

Addressing graduates of the College of Education, College of Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences, and College of Science, Michael V. tackled one of the biggest questions facing young professionals today, the growing presence of artificial intelligence in the workplace and everyday life.
His advice was simple: Use AI, but don't try to become AI.
He challenged the Class of 2026 to develop the qualities that technology cannot replicate, including imagination, compassion, problem-solving, leadership and the ability to create meaningful change.

“Yes, AI will probably be here to stay but remember: machines can never live your life for you. Hindi nito kayang mangarap para sa’yo. Hindi nito kayang magmahal para sa’yo. Hindi nito kayang magdesisyon kung anong klaseng tao ang gusto mong maging dahil ikaw lang ang makakagawa noon,” he said.
“Use technology but don’t lose your humanity,” he added.
Then he left them with a parting message that neatly summed up his point:
“Go out there and make yourselves impossible to replace.”

articles.title: Barbie Forteza draws a hard line on cheating
articles.summary: Barbie Forteza knows exactly where she stands when it comes to infidelity and she isn't leaving much room for negotiation. For the actress, cheating isn't something she would simply brush aside in…

blocks.text: Barbie Forteza knows exactly where she stands when it comes to infidelity and she isn't leaving much room for negotiation.
For the actress, cheating isn't something she would simply brush aside in the name of love or second chances. Once trust is broken, she believes a person has every right to walk away.
That was the thinking behind her now-viral “F–k, no” response when she was asked if she would give a cheating partner another chance during a media conference.
Barbie further explained her position during an appearance on “Fast Talk With Boy Abunda,” Friday.
According to Barbie, her answer has less to do with holding a grudge against cheaters and more to do with how she views herself.
“The way I was raised is that you should value yourself,” Barbie said in Filipino. “I support myself. I treat myself out. In a way, that’s how much I love myself.”
For Barbie, being in a relationship means voluntarily giving someone something she considers precious: her time, attention and affection.
“So loving another person who isn’t related to me, who isn’t my family, to whom I don’t have any obligation to, only for that person to cheat on me? Why? Right?” she said.
“I chose you. I have no obligations toward you, and then you cheat on me? My time is valuable. My attention is valuable,” she added.
And that is why, for Barbie, the problem isn't limited to the act of cheating itself.
She said she would also draw the line at anything in a relationship that makes her feel diminished or undervalued.
“I guess it’s not just cheating. It’s anything that would make me feel like I have been treated as less,” she explained.
Trust, once given, is another matter.
“Because I gave myself to you, my time, my love, most importantly. Then you betrayed my trust,” Barbie said.
She was quick to point out, however, that this is her personal standard and not a rule she expects other couples to follow.
“That’s just for me,” she said.

articles.title: Trump gov’t mulls deal to give away part of Yosemite park
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, United States — President Donald Trump’s administration is considering giving away a section of the renowned Yosemite National Park to a private developer. An investigation…

blocks.text: WASHINGTON, United States — President Donald Trump’s administration is considering giving away a section of the renowned Yosemite National Park to a private developer.

An investigation published Friday by NOTUS, a news outlet, said the government has spent over a year quietly working to transfer a roughly quarter-mile strip of the park to a company linked through a web of other entities to Nevada-based Kingsbarn Realty Capital.
It is the latest move by the Trump administration to roll back conservation protections of public lands.
In July, the president slashed two Utah national monuments by more than 90 percent, and this month his administration moved to end a rule barring logging and road-building in national forests.

A Kingsbarn-controlled limited liability company purchased an 83-acre plot just outside the park in 2024, and Kingsbarn CEO Jeff Pori wants to build a road connecting the property to one of Yosemite’s thoroughfares — giving the land “exceptionally rare private access,” NOTUS said, citing people familiar with the discussions.
In exchange, the National Park Service would receive land of equal value in another part of California that has yet to be determined.
In a statement to AFP, the Interior Department appeared to confirm that negotiations had taken place but denied any political pressure to reach a predetermined outcome.

“Any land exchange or access proposal involving National Park Service lands would be subject to all applicable federal laws, regulations and Departmental policies, including required environmental review and public notification processes,” the agency said, adding: “No final decisions have been made.”
“If a proposal advances, the Department will follow established procedures to ensure appropriate coordination, transparency and public involvement consistent with federal law.”

Federal election records show Pori has donated frequently to the Republican National Committee and Trump-aligned fundraising committees. Kingsbarn did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Previously rejected by courts
The National Parks Conservation Association, an advocacy organization, called the move an unlawful “attack.”

“The Trump administration’s attempts to dismantle America’s conservation legacy are now taking aim at Yosemite with this secretive, backroom deal,” said Mark Rose, the group’s senior Sierra Nevada program manager.
The Yosemite NPS Employees Union said it was “appalled” by the ceding of public lands for private interests, calling the proposed trade “antithetical to what we stand for” as stewards of the park.
There was a previous proposal to develop a road through Yosemite when the 83-acre parcel outside the park had a different owner.
That plan was rejected by the administrations of both Republican George W Bush and Democrat Barack Obama. Courts rejected appeals by the then-owner, Lewis Geyser.

First protected in 1864, Yosemite National Park in California’s Sierra Nevada mountains is internationally acclaimed for its spectacular granite cliffs, glaciers, waterfalls, sequoia trees and wildlife.

Rose said the park was already facing an overcrowding crisis from years of lodging expansion in the area and the Trump administration’s decision this year to scrap a vehicle registration system to limit traffic.
Democratic Senator Adam Schiff of California, a fierce critic of Trump, said in a statement: “Yosemite is one of California’s natural wonders, and must be protected from further development.

“The courts struck this project down once, but this administration appears hellbent on moving forward in the face of opposition from the public, Congress and the courts. But the only thing the administration cares about is whether there is money involved. We will fight this again.” /das

articles.title: Ivana Alawi still silent on criticism over floodwater relief effort
articles.summary: Actress and content creator Ivana Alawi has yet to respond to criticism over the manner in which she distributed relief goods and financial assistance to flood-affected families in Pampanga. Alawi…

blocks.text: At A Glance

items: Ivana Alawi's relief effort in flood-hit Pampanga drew criticism from some netizens who questioned why she and her team distributed aid while standing in floodwater despite an apparently nearby dry road.

blocks.text: Actress and content creator Ivana Alawi has yet to respond to criticism over the manner in which she distributed relief goods and financial assistance to flood-affected families in Pampanga.
Alawi visited communities in Apalit and San Simon on August 25, bringing relief packs containing rice, luncheon meat and corned beef, as well as ₱1,000 in cash for residents.
Photos and videos from the relief effort showed Alawi and members of her team handing out the donations while standing in floodwater.
While many residents and followers welcomed the assistance, some netizens questioned the decision to distribute the goods from the flooded area, pointing out that a nearby road appeared to be dry.

The criticism also extended to the videos and photos documenting the effort, with some users asking whether wading through the floodwater was necessary and whether the footage placed too much attention on Alawi.
One netizen questioned whether the relief effort was “a public stunt for good PR,” while also raising concerns about the possible health risks of walking through contaminated floodwater.
Others, however, defended Alawi and said the focus should be on the actual assistance given to families affected by the flooding.
As of writing, Alawi has not publicly addressed the criticism or explained the decision to distribute the relief goods while standing in the floodwater.

articles.title: Palanca award-winning authors, editors, and bookworms share favorite Pinoy-authored books
articles.summary: As Buwan ng Wika draws to a close this August, what better way to celebrate the Filipino language than by revisiting stories written by Filipino authors? For this forum, we asked Palanca…

blocks.text: As Buwan ng Wika draws to a close this August, what better way to celebrate the Filipino language than by revisiting stories written by Filipino authors?

For this forum, we asked Palanca award-winning authors as well as some content creators to share the Filipino books that have stayed with them. From gritty fiction and crime novels to coming-of-age stories and horror books, their picks show the range of Filipino literature and the different ways stories can shape how young readers see themselves, their communities, and the world around them.
‘Mapanglaw ang Mukha ng Buwan’ by Efren R. Abueg

‘I became a writer because of Efren R. Abueg’s short story “Mapanglaw ang Mukha ng Buwan,” which is included in the book ‘Mga Agos sa Disyerto,’ alongside works by Dominador B. Mirasol, Rogelio L. Ordoñez, Edgardo M. Reyes, and Rogelio R. Sikat.

This book has had a profound influence on several generations of Filipino short story writers. It also demonstrated the power of words to give strength and support to the oppressed and the disadvantaged, especially those who have no voice in society.’

blocks.caption: Joe Chua

blocks.text: Joe Chua
‘Andong Agimat’ by Arnold Arre, ‘Libing Isa’ by MPAU, ‘Patay Kung Patay (Death be Damned)’ by Mike Alcazaren, Noel Pascual, and AJ Bernardo, and ‘Trese’ by Budjette Tan and Kajo Baldisimo

‘All of these use horror as a way to explore Philippine society. But more than that, they’re fun to read. It’s a hyperviolent comic book that was the right thing for me to read at the right time and was what got me interested in local comics. I don’t know if I can recommend it now in light of all the school violence, though.’

blocks.caption: Yvette Tan

blocks.text: Yvette Tan
‘Sa mga Kuko ng Liwanag’ by Edgardo M. Reyes

‘I love this book not only because Reyes is a writer I admire, but also because of the novel's effective portrayal of the cruel and dangerous face of the city. It realistically presents major social issues, vividly narrates the true condition of the poor, and depicts the complex struggles of ordinary workers. It also highlights the voicelessness of the poor in the face of oppression. And another thing I value most about this novel is that it is not only the story of Julio and Ligaya, but also the story of many Filipinos struggling to survive.’

blocks.caption: Perry Mangilaya

blocks.text: Perry Mangilaya
‘Macarthur’ by Bob Ong

‘Gritty and unapologetic, Bob Ong’s ‘Macarthur’ is a book I read many years ago yet still think about every now and then. It highlights the strength of laughter as a coping mechanism. It introduces moral conundrums. It enrages. It is hard to believe the book is just 98 pages because it manages to do so much.’

blocks.caption: Firas Abbound

blocks.text: Firas Abbound
‘Dekada ’70’ by Lualhati Bautista

‘If I have to answer only one, I’ll go with “Dekada ‘70” by Lualhati Bautista. This changed the way I read (fiction) books from treating them as pure escapism to realizing they hold powerful reflections of our history and society.’

blocks.caption: Veron Cruz

blocks.text: Veron Cruz
‘Kulang na Silya’ by Ricky Lee

‘There are so many books to choose from, but I’ll keep coming back to “Kulang na Silya” by Ricky Lee. There are also so many Ricky Lee books to choose from, but this one, specifically, really feels like medicine for a creative who is about to give up, or for anyone, really, who is going through a difficult time. Truly, a National Artist for a reason.’

blocks.caption: Paula Michaella

blocks.text: Paula Michaella
‘Janus Silang’ by Edgar Calabia Samar

It is a five-book series that follows Janus, a 14-year-old gamer who plays Tala, an online game inspired by Filipino mythology. Everything changes one game night when all the other players suddenly turn to dust, leaving Janus as the only survivor.

Janus follows the chosen-one trope. The series starts with a horror-esque atmosphere and gradually becomes more fantasy as its universe expands. Along the way, readers are introduced to a wide array of creatures from Filipino mythology and folklore, along with exciting and action-packed fight scenes.

Readers who grew up watching ‘Pedro Penduko,’ ‘Wansapanataym,’ and ‘Kakabakaba Adventures’ will surely find something nostalgic in the series. On the other hand, younger generations are in for a treat as they explore the richness of Filipino culture.

blocks.caption: JP Obias

blocks.text: JP Obias

These choices may come from different genres and generations, but they share one thing: each book left a lasting impression on its reader. And as Buwan ng Wika comes to an end, they offer a reminder that Filipino stories are not simply something to celebrate for one month. They are stories worth returning to, especially for a new generation of readers.

articles.title: Palawan junior tennis brings 3-week showcase to Mindanao
articles.summary: The Palawan Pawnshop nationwide junior tennis circuit shifts to Mindanao next week for a three-tournament swing that will take the country’s premier grassroots talent-search to Davao del Sur, Sultan…

blocks.text: The Palawan Pawnshop nationwide junior tennis circuit shifts to Mindanao next week for a three-tournament swing that will take the country’s premier grassroots talent-search to Davao del Sur, Sultan Kudarat and Cotabato, giving the region’s young players another major platform to compete, gain ranking points and valuable experience and showcase their skills.

Following the successful staging of the Palawan Junior Series last March, which featured stops across the Visayas and Luzon, the long-running circuit continues its nationwide trek with a busy Mindanao schedule designed to sustain the momentum of junior tennis while providing more youngsters from the countryside an opportunity to test themselves against the best players in their age groups.

The Mindanao swing kicks off with the MJFC “Araw ng Digos Junior Age-Group Championships” on Sept. 2-8 at the Digos City courts in Davao del Sur, with another strong field expected to vie for honors in the boys’ and girls’ singles in the 12-, 14-, 16- and 18-and-under categories.
Titles in the boys’ and girls’ 14-and-U and 18-and-U doubles will also be disputed in the tournament being held in honor of Digos City Mayor Josef Fortich Cagas.

The series then moves to Sultan Kudarat for the Bagong Pilipinas age-group tournament on Sept. 10-15, with the Capital Indoor and Outdoor courts in Isulan serving as venue. The Mindanao swing wraps up with the Kidapawan Juniors Championship on Sept. 16-22 at the Kidapawan City courts in Cotabato.

Palawan Pawnshop has remained at the forefront of this grassroots movement, sustaining a year-round, nationwide junior circuit that goes beyond simply staging tournaments. The program serves as an extensive talent-identification and development platform, allowing promising players to gain competition experience and potentially earn consideration for future national pools and teams.

Sanctioned by Philta and Universal Tennis Ranking and supported by Dunlop, ICON Golf & Sports and the Palawan Group of Companies, the nationwide talent-search was initiated by Palawan Pawnshop president and CEO Bobby Castro as part of his continuing effort to raise the standard of junior tennis in the country.
And while Mindanao takes center stage for three consecutive weeks, the nationwide circuit remains in full swing elsewhere.

Siquijor will host another junior tournament, the Governor’s Cup, on Sept. 17-22 at the Capitol tennis courts. The event, sponsored by Gov. Jake Villa, will feature the same age-group divisions, adding another venue for young players to compete and sharpen their skills.

articles.title: Jack Logan: Digital creator to novelist
articles.summary: When did books stop being entertainment? There was a time when people found their escape, their stories and their adventures within the pages of a book. Today, with digital media dominating how we…

blocks.text: When did books stop being entertainment?

There was a time when people found their escape, their stories and their adventures within the pages of a book. Today, with digital media dominating how we consume stories, that tradition can sometimes feel like a thing of the past.
But is it really over for books?
Not quite. There are still people who believe in the magic of the printed page and are willing to bring it back to a generation raised on screens.
Jack Logan is one of them.
Better known as a digital creator, filmmaker and storyteller, Logan is now venturing into a decidedly old-school form of entertainment: the novel.
His first book, “The Pabebe Chronicles: The Flower and the Warrior,” is a 300-page Filipino-language fantasy-comedy that mixes romance, politics, magic, war and humor.
For Logan, however, the book is about more than simply telling a story. It is also a way of encouraging people to read.

“Ako kasi personally mahilig ako magbasa. And this book is my way of encouraging others to do the same. Iba rin ang feeling na hawak mo ang libro, naamoy at nararamdaman mo yung texture ng mga pahina...iba e,” he said.
It is an interesting choice for someone who has made much of his name in digital media.

Logan is a filmmaker, writer and digital creator known for “Jack Logan Realtalks” and “The 12 Days Saga” film trilogy. His documentary “Makabagong San Juan” was also nominated for Best Single Digital Programme/Short Film at the Asian Television Awards.
But writing a novel is a different thing.
There is no camera, no actor and no editing room to hide behind.
There are just words and the reader.
Logan has been carrying “The Pabebe Chronicles” around for a while. He first came up with the story in 2015 and shared it with friends. Like many ideas, however, it sat around for years.
In 2025, he picked it up again.
This time, he decided to finish it.
The result is “The Pabebe Chronicles: The Flower and the Warrior,” the first published book in what Logan plans as a trilogy.
“Basically, it's a fantasy story,” he says. “But it's also a love story. It's political. It's funny.”
The story takes place in Erodas, a fictional realm dealing with the aftermath of the War of Golds. There are kingdoms, royal families, warriors, magic and old grudges.
And then there are the people caught in the middle of all that.
One of them is Bianca, a weaver from Lambak whose royal identity has been erased.
There is also Jack, an amnesiac warrior who has a violent past but cannot remember everything about it.
Then there is Pabie, the Kondesa of Amazon, who Logan says brings a very different energy to the story.
Their lives eventually cross as the political problems of Erodas become complicated by prophecy, deception and magic.
But don't expect Logan to suddenly become very serious just because his characters live in a fantasy kingdom.
That was never the point.

“I wanted it to be Filipino,” he says. “Ito kung paano ninyo nakilala si Jack Logan, ganun din ito. Iisa lang ang boses ko as creator so, kung nagugustuhan ninyo ang mga gawa ko before, tiyak magugustuhan ninyo rin ito.”
That includes the humor.
The book has what Logan describes as a Filipino comedic rhythm, with contemporary language, satire and pop-culture references mixed into the fantasy setting.
“It's fantasy, but the way they talk is Filipino,” he says.
That probably explains the title, too.
“The Pabebe Chronicles” doesn't exactly sound like the name of a grim medieval epic. And Logan isn't pretending otherwise.
He wants to have fun with the genre.
“You can have a very serious scene, then suddenly somebody says something funny,” he says.
That sounds very Filipino.
It also sounds very Jack Logan.
There is one other unusual thing about the book.
“The Flower and the Warrior” is the first “Pabebe Chronicles” novel to be published, but it is actually Book II in the story's chronology.
The saga's timeline goes “The War of Golds,” “The Flower and the Warrior” and then “The Last Baruk.”
Logan knows this may sound slightly confusing.
For now, though, he is happy that readers finally get to enter Erodas, one page at a time.
“The Pabebe Chronicles: The Flower and the Warrior” is published by Central Book Supply, Inc. and is available in hardbound and paperback editions.

articles.title: NASA is launching the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Here are just a few of the wonders it will reveal
articles.summary: If all goes to plan, at 7:26 a.m. Sunday morning, a new space telescope will blast off from Cape Canaveral, Fla., on top of a Falcon Heavy rocket, ready to reveal new wonders about our universe. Here…

image.caption: An illustration is shown of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, which is set to launch on Aug. 30 from Cape Canaveral, Fla. (NASA)

blocks.text: Science

If all goes to plan, at 7:26 a.m. Sunday morning, a new space telescope will blast off from Cape Canaveral, Fla., on top of a Falcon Heavy rocket, ready to reveal new wonders about our universe. Here are some things scientists hope to unravel with this new telescope.
'I can't even imagine what we're going to learn,' says one Canadian researcher
If all goes to plan, at 7:26 a.m. Sunday morning, a new space telescope will blast off from Cape Canaveral, Fla., on top of a Falcon Heavy rocket, ready to reveal new wonders about our universe.

The highly anticipated Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is named after NASA's first chief astronomer, also known as the "mother of the Hubble Space Telescope." Once launched, it will orbit 1.5 million kilometres away, at a point called L2 where gravitational forces balance to keep satellites in a steady orbit. It is a five-year mission, with the possibility of extension.
But why bother adding a new telescope to the arsenal of telescopes already in orbit, like the Hubble Space Telescope or the James Webb Space Telescope?

Because each telescope is equipped with different instruments, and Nancy Grace Roman is no different. While it has a mirror that is roughly 2.4 metres across, similar to Hubble, it also has a coronagraph that can block out starlight to reveal planets orbiting distant stars. It also has its Wide Field Instrument that is just as sensitive as Hubble's but has the ability to image an area 100 times larger. It's like going from looking through a pinhole to something the size of a golf ball.
Its camera will be able to resolve billions of stars, allowing for all different types of sky and stellar surveys.
So, what makes Nancy Grace Roman so special? Let's take a look at just some of the highly anticipated discoveries astronomers are hoping this telescope will make.
The search for other planets
While we don't know of any other planets with life, astronomers are continuing to investigate other stellar systems to find out what makes our solar system so unique. Or perhaps it's not that unique.
To date, more than 6,300 exoplanets have been confirmed, mostly from the Kepler Space Telescope.

There are a few ways to look for exoplanets. The most popular is the transit method, where a telescope looks at a star for an extended period of time. If there's a planet that crosses — or transits — in front of it, the light of the star dips ever-so slightly. And that's what Nancy Grace Roman will do as well. But on a much bigger scale.

"It's just going to be crazy how much more we're going to learn because right now you know we've got Kepler, which I guess we looked at, like, 200,000 stars or something like that, and then with Roman we're going to look at 100 million stars and we're going to go from 10,000 planets to 100,000 transiting exoplanets," said Kelsey Hoffman, a co-investigator on one of the observing programs with the telescope and a researcher at Bishop's University in Sherbrooke, Que.
"So that increase in numbers, it's… I can't even imagine what we're going to learn."
But the telescope will also use another method to search for exoplanets — something called microlensing, which allows astronomers to peer even deeper.

items: NASA will no longer attempt to save its aging Swift space telescope
'The Holy Grail of science': Montreal startup's high-tech camera to help NASA search for exoplanets

blocks.text: "If you have a distant star that you like to call a source of light, and then a star with its planets moves precisely right in front of it, that mass of the star and the mass of the planet act as two lenses, and causes the light that's coming from that distant star to bend a little bit, which we observe as a magnification event," explained Jason Rowe, who is also part of a Nancy Grace Roman observing program and is a professor in the department of physics at Bishop's University.
He's particularly excited because this type of observation will allow scientists to look for more Earth-like planets.

"We've discovered previous planets with microlensing, but we're going to kind of blow the doors open and now discover a very large sample of them," he said. "And microlensing is very sensitive to planets at longer periods, including those that have masses about Earth's size, about Earth masses."
Dark matter and dark energy

What we are able see makes up only five per cent of what exists in the universe. Roughly 27 per cent is dark matter, a sort of invisible glue that holds the galaxies and the stars within them together. The other 68 per cent is dark energy, also invisible, and something that is believed to speed up the expansion of our universe.

Astronomers have been trying for decades to figure out exactly what dark matter is, and Nancy Grace Roman will look for dark matter within galaxies and within beautiful globular clusters, a collection of thousands to millions of stars that are all tightly gravitationally bound.
The mission will measure the locations and amount of dark matter, as well as normal matter, in hundreds of millions of galaxies.

"Normally with surveys, you have this trade-off where you decide, am I going to stare out one little patch for a very long time? Or am I gonna scale across the sky?" said Nicole Drakos, an astrophysicist at the University of Hawaii, Hilo, who is also part of a Nancy Grace Roman observational program. "With Roman, you can stare at one patch on the sky, but you still have an enormous area.
"So you can see these distant galaxies, but also see where they live. You can see their environment. You can map out the dark matter structure around them, the gas around them."
The telescope will also investigate dark energy, which, like dark matter, is invisible. But in this case, dark energy is causing our universe to expand rather than slow down.

"I'm, you know, involved with the deep field stuff, so I'm obviously interested in that. But, you know, in my heart, I am a cosmologist; I really love the cosmology," Drakos said. "Getting a better handle of things like the expansion of the universe, I think, is really cool."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Based in Toronto, Nicole covers all things science for CBC News. As an amateur astronomer, Nicole can be found looking up at the night sky appreciating the marvels of our universe. She is the editor of the Journal of the Royal Astronomical Society of Canada and the author of several books. In 2021, she won the Kavli Science Journalism Award from the American Association for the Advancement of Science for a Quirks and Quarks audio special on the history and future of Black people in science. You can send her story ideas at nicole.mortillaro@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Carney government asks court to strike down climate litigation
articles.summary: The federal government is asking a court to toss out a high-profile environmental lawsuit, arguing it has no business directing Canada's climate policy.

image.caption: Prime Minister Mark Carney makes a statement outside the Office of the Prime Minister and Privy Council in Ottawa on July 21. (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics
The federal government is asking a court to toss out a high-profile environmental lawsuit, arguing it has no business directing Canada's climate policy.
Ottawa argues courts should not direct climate policy
The federal government is asking a court to toss out a high-profile environmental lawsuit, arguing that it's not required to update Canada's climate plan to meet national emissions reduction targets.
The government also says it's not the court's role to make or direct climate policy, and has filed a motion asking the court to strike the case before it goes to full hearings.
In June, three young people and two environmental groups launched a lawsuit asking the Federal Court to order Ottawa to amend its climate plan.

items: Youth, advocacy groups sue Carney government over climate rollbacks

blocks.text: Since the plan was first launched in 2022, the Liberal government has eliminated key measures needed for Canada to achieve the 2030 target.
The lawsuit alleges that not updating the climate plan violates Canada's climate accountability act, formally known as the Canadian Net-Zero Emissions Accountability Act.
In its first major response on Aug. 14, the government pointed out to the court that the act states that "the Minister may amend an emissions target … or an emissions reduction plan."
In a legal document sent to the court, the government states that line alone is grounds to dismiss the lawsuit before the first hearing.
"Read in its ordinary and grammatical sense, the use of the word 'may' clearly does not impose any obligation to amend," the government said in its submission.
Ottawa also said Canada's courts don't make or direct climate policy.
"[The lawsuit] raises broad political and policy issues, these are beyond the Court’s institutional capacity to address," the government's legal submission states.
CBC asked the environment minister's office if this means the federal government will not update its 2030 climate plan.

"The Government of Canada is committed to fighting climate change and reaching net-zero emissions by 2050. As this matter is before the courts, we cannot comment further," said Keean Nembhard, a spokesperson for the minister.
Carney’s taken a ‘wrecking ball’ to Canada’s climate progress plan: Environmental Defence
Although the minister's office didn't say whether it will update its climate plan, the young people who launched the challenge are calling on the court to reject any calls to dismiss it.

"Canadians are living through the devastating reality of not having a meaningful plan to address climate change," said Marie Maltais in a statement. "Yet, at this critical moment, the government is fighting to throw our case out of court, while simultaneously moving ahead with fossil fuel expansion and rolling back key climate protections.”

Kyle Harrietha, who worked for a decade in several roles including as the chief of staff to the energy minister and parliamentary affairs director for the environment minister, believes the government should update its climate plan.
Harrietha helped shepherd the Canadian Net-Zero Emissions Accountability Act through Parliament in 2021, and now runs his own parliamentary consulting firm, DOPA Services.

"I'm not sure the government has unfettered discretion on this," Harrietha said. "I would say as someone who was in the room when this act was developed … that discretion was never intended to create a circumstance where the government would make major changes to its climate policy and then leave the plan unamended."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

David Thurton is a senior reporter in CBC's Parliamentary Bureau. He covers daily politics in the nation’s capital and specializes in environment and energy policy. Born in Canada but raised in Trinidad and Tobago, he’s moved around more times than he can count. He’s worked for CBC in several provinces and territories, including Alberta and the Northwest Territories. He can be reached at david.thurton@cbc.ca
