articles.title: Canada ready to further distance itself from U.S. on military procurement
articles.summary: The flareup in the Canada-U.S. tariff war has not only strengthened Ottawa’s resolve to boost military co-operation with Europe and Asia — it's also hurting prospects of major military purchases from…

image.caption: Stephen Fuhr, head of Canada's Defence Procurement Agency, stands in front of a CF-104D Starfighter, built in 1962, at the KF Centre for Excellence in Kelowna, B.C. (Daniel Leblanc/CBC)

blocks.text: Politics

The flareup in the Canada-U.S. tariff war has not only strengthened Ottawa’s resolve to boost military co-operation with Europe and Asia — it's also hurting prospects of major military purchases from the United States.
Trade war has strengthened resolve to boost military co-operation with Europe, Asia
In an interview, the head of the Defence Investment Agency says the Canadian public would have no appetite for sole-source military contracts to American firms.

"That's just me reading the room," said Stephen Fuhr, secretary of state for defence procurement. "I think that would be a very difficult thing to do, especially after this last week. I think that people would not be happy about that."

items: Canada announces Defence Investment Agency to manage purchase, delivery of military equipment
Ottawa to expand defence buying powers when national, economic security at stake

blocks.text: Canada's retaliatory tariff response announced this week did not directly target the defence sector. However, Fuhr's comments suggest a growing reluctance toward potential acquisitions of U.S. military hardware.
He added that Canada must not act as though relations will simply return to normal after U.S. President Donald Trump leaves office in January 2029.

While Canada has pledged tens of billions of dollars in additional defence spending over the coming years, it wants to put an end to the era during which 70 per cent of those funds flowed south of the border.

"We are in a situation that we didn't provoke, we’re in a position that we don’t deserve," Fuhr said. "We're on the receiving end of this change, and it's our job to look for new opportunities and pivot as fast as we can to meet the moment, and never put ourselves back in this position again."
Canada 'carefully considering' its options

Fuhr still describes the United States as a key defence ally, but insists that Canada has learned the perils of "putting all our eggs in one basket." Above all, he wants Canada to become increasingly self-reliant in terms of military production, or to forge new strategic alliances.

"So working with others who want to work with us and add value to what we're doing, I think we're carefully considering that a lot more. Again, not to diminish the relationship with our traditional partner, but things are different now, and it's been very clear that the relationship that we had will be different moving forward," Fuhr said.
Justin Massie, a military affairs expert at l'Université du Québec à Montréal, said Canada has no choice but to adjust its defence policy to align with the new American reality.

"The United States wants the burden of defending its allies to rest squarely on the shoulders of its allies," Massie said. "They are tired of calling on American taxpayers to fund the defence of Europe and Canada."

Richard Shimooka, a senior fellow at the Macdonald-Laurier Institute, says Canada will still need to find a way to keep working with the United States on continental defence, even as the country’s defence budget is heading to more than two per cent of GDP.
"Canadians don’t understand you can’t do this alone. We could have a 10 per cent defence budget and it wouldn’t be enough," he said.
Fuhr did not single out any specific military project that might be delayed or stalled by the trade dispute.

Nevertheless, major military helicopter procurements currently in the works could be impacted, including a potential sole-source purchase of American-made Black Hawks, which are widely considered the preferred option for Canada’s special forces.

Furthermore, the results of a review of the planned purchase of 88 F-35 fighter jets, manufactured by U.S. defense giant Lockheed Martin, have yet to be disclosed, and Prime Minister Mark Carney has given no indication of his intentions.

Canada has placed a firm order for 16 F-35s and has begun paying for critical equipment for 14 additional aircraft, but there is currently no indication of how many fighters will ultimately be purchased beyond that initial count.

items: Ottawa's mixed fleet of F-35s and Gripens could total more than 100 aircraft, sources say
Saab's surveillance jet deal with Canada faces a U.S. stealth tech hurdle

blocks.text: Meanwhile, Canada remains interested in acquiring a second fleet of Gripen fighter jets, manufactured by Swedish firm Saab.

Ottawa is also in negotiations with Saab to procure GlobalEye radar aircraft, developed in partnership with Canadian manufacturer Bombardier, despite a lobbying campaign in favour of Boeing's E-7 Wedgetail.
'Thrilled' with $2.3B Telesat contract

Fuhr added that he was "thrilled" with the recent $2.3-billion contract awarded to Telesat for Arctic military satellite communications. The project reduces Canada's reliance on Elon Musk’s Starlink network, operated by U.S.-based SpaceX.
Fuhr said the federal government plans to continue doing business with Canadian subsidiaries of foreign contractors.

"We consider those folks in the tent," he said. "They employ hundreds and hundreds of Canadians, they pay taxes in Canada, they have their headquarters in Canada, they do engineering in Canada, they retain IP in Canada — all that really matters."

However, he pointed to growing discussions about the need to move away from strict U.S. controls over key military technology, which fall under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) framework.
"Is there a world in which we can operate with less ITAR restrictions? I think there is," Fuhr said, citing expanded co-operation with partners across Europe, Asia and Oceania.
"Nobody can do it all on their own like the U.S. can. Let's get real about this. But collectively we certainly can, and I think people are trying to move in that direction."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Daniel Leblanc is a reporter with more than 20 years experience in investigative journalism and federal politics. He is a past winner of the Michener Award, the Charles Lynch Award and three National Newspaper Awards.

articles.title: Drinking among Gen Z adults has gone up, busting the sober myth
articles.summary: After years of speculation that Gen Z is the sober generation, new research shows that they are actually starting to drink more — nearly on par with the rest of the adult population.

image.caption: More Gen Z adults are reaching for alcoholic drinks, with the latest research revealing that they drink about as much as the rest of society. (Julio Cortez/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World
After years of speculation that Gen Z is the sober generation, new research shows that they are actually starting to drink more — nearly on par with the rest of the adult population.
New IWSR research shows that the young cohort has steadily increased its drinking habits
After years of being viewed as the "sober generation," Gen Z is changing up the narrative by going out more and sipping on boozy beverages.
Andrea Shipka, 27, is one of them. She says her peers are "for sure" drinking more.
"I've gone out more this year than any other year in my 20s," Shipka said, adding that she typically goes out once or twice a week. Shipka, who is originally from Edmonton, is doing a stint in Paris.

New consumer research from alcohol data and analytics group IWSR shows that young people have indeed steadily increased their drinking habits. At 74 per cent, their drinking rate is nearly on par with the total adult population of 76 per cent. (Just three years ago, Gen Z stood at 66 per cent.)
The latest consumer data included surveys with some 32,000 respondents across 19 markets, including Canada, the U.S. and the U.K., and represented Gen Z, millennials, Gen X and boomers.
Its findings suggest that the youngest cohort is starting to catch up to older generations.
LISTEN | Smoking also making a comeback among Gen Z:
Ottawa Morning6:30Is smoking making a comeback?
Still, this generation has distinct drinking habits.

For example, the study found that Gen Z was more likely to follow public health advice related to alcohol, such as drinking in moderation. They also reported drinking cocktails more than other generations.
Shipka said she exclusively drinks in social contexts — and confirmed she and her friends don't like to overdo it.
"With my friends that drink more, I also tend to see better control with knowing when you're at your limit," she said. "My friends typically won't ... black out or go over their limits."
Gen Z drinking 'starting a little later'

Industry experts say there are likely a few reasons that explain this uptick in drinking for Gen Z adults. For one thing, many Gen Zers came of age during the COVID-19 pandemic when lockdowns were in place, likely delaying their foray into drinking culture.
"There was, needless to say, a difficulty in drinking [at the time]," said Marten Lodewijks, IWSR president and managing director. "You're not going out because you can't."

Canadian data says something similar. According to Statistics Canada, heavy drinking among 18- to 34-year-old regular drinkers has returned to pre-pandemic levels. (Heavy drinking is defined as at least four drinks for women and at least five for men per occasion. Regular drinking, meanwhile, is at least once a month in the last 12 months.)
However, Canadians generally are drinking less, the agency said, and they are seemingly more aware of the health risks associated with alcohol as one of the leading causes of preventable disease.
When it comes to Gen Z, Lodewijks says money may also play a role in their habits.

items: The new science of alcohol: why recent guidance says more than 2 drinks per week is risky

blocks.text: "Everything has become more expensive," Lodewijks said, noting that alcohol is a discretionary expense.
Now that some Gen Z adults are in their late 20s, they likely have more disposable income to spend on going out, he added.
"There was a broad narrative that Gen Z are the lost generation — they don't drink," Lodewijks said. "It turns out that's not true; they're just starting a little later than other generations."
Kirk Zembal, co-founder of Alberta-based brewery Blindman Brewing, told CBC News that he's seeing similar trends, at least anecdotally.
From beer to bourbon, why Calgarians are choosing these alcohol-free options
"We have definitely seen a resurgence in Gen Z drinking," Zembal said.
He said he believes young adults are reacting to being "overly online."

"Folks are really starting to see the value — not that they didn't see the value — of being more intentional about making sure they are socializing out in the real world," he said. "Alcohol provides a social lubricant."
Drinking no longer 'the objective'
It seems like young adults are also frustrated with online dating and are instead opting for in-person introductions at a pub or bar, he said.

"There’s been a bit of a backlash against online dating," Zembal said. "People are feeling discouraged.... They're not having the kind of success and relationships they formed on online dating aren't lasting."
Some young people say they're breaking up with dating apps
But even as Gen Z consumers reach for a pint or cocktail glass more often, Lodewijks said their attitude toward drinking culture is different from past generations.
"Drinking isn't the objective," he said.

That means that unlike millennials who go out specifically for a post-work beer or happy hour wine, Gen Zs are gathering for other reasons, and not necessarily just at bars or pubs. Alcohol may or may not be brought out at social events.

items: Bye bye booze? Alcohol consumption hits 20 year low, as non-alc options soar

blocks.text: It's simply an option, Lodewijks said.
"If you're a producer or brand owner, you need to give them a good reason, a good product, that aligns with what they're doing."
Notably, millennials reported the highest alcoholic beverage consumption at 81 per cent, followed by Gen X at 77 per cent.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Anya Zoledziowski is a Peabody-winning multimedia journalist from Edmonton who's covered social and climate justice, Indigenous affairs, gender, politics and more, and has been recognized by several national and international awards. She’s currently pursuing her PhD in journalism studies.

articles.title: Cambodia claims online scam hubs wiped out after sweeping crackdown
articles.summary: PHNOM PENH, Cambodia — Cambodia, notorious for being a major center for international online scams, claimed Friday it no longer hosts any of the compounds where the lucrative cybercrime was carried…

blocks.text: PHNOM PENH, Cambodia — Cambodia, notorious for being a major center for international online scams, claimed Friday it no longer hosts any of the compounds where the lucrative cybercrime was carried out, although some remain skeptical.

The government’s Ad-Hoc Commission for Combating Online Scams, CCOS, claimed success for its crackdown at a Thursday meeting with about 50 representatives of foreign diplomatic missions and international organizations led by Senior Minister Chhay Sinarith, who heads the anti-scam agency, it said in a statement issued Friday.

“This follows the complete eradication of large-scale online scam operations, strict legal actions against perpetrators, networks and involved officials, alongside the systematic establishment of a cybersecurity legal framework,” it said.

Chhay Sinarith’s claims were met with both skepticism and guarded optimism from independent groups that have tracked the scam compounds, which are infamous not only for bilking billions of dollars from people all over the world, but also for carrying out human trafficking.

Thousands of foreign nationals, who are employed to run “romance” and cryptocurrency scams to swindle victims, are often recruited with false job offers and then forced to work in conditions of near-slavery.
Such scams caused estimated combined losses of $88.3 billion to $114.1 billion in 2025, said a report in July by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime.

“The strong confidence placed in the (Cambodian) government’s assertion that all scamming operations in Cambodia have been eradicated is severely misplaced,” Mark Taylor, an independent international anti-trafficking consultant and former head of an anti-trafficking program in Cambodia, told The Associated Press.
“There are credible indicators that significant scamming operations continue and that recruitment of foreign workers into Cambodia for scamming work continues.”
Blue Dragon Children’s Foundation, a Vietnam-based anti-human trafficking organization, took more of a wait-and-see attitude.

“There is no doubt that some of Cambodia’s criminal compounds used for online scamming have closed,” said Michael Brosowski, the group’s founder and strategic director, citing a drastic decrease in calls from people who have been trafficked, although the calls have not stopped.
“We hope that the Cambodian government will keep its commitment to close down these compounds and give greater protection to victims of this crime.”

Chhay Sinarith said that from July 2025 to Aug. 20, 2026, law enforcement forces investigated 793 suspected scam locations and raided 624 sites, while detaining nearly 30,000 suspects representing 39 nationalities.
Cambodian authorities rescued and deported 58,266 foreign nationals, he said, and 3,477 criminal suspects from 29 nationalities were arrested and placed in pretrial detention.

The crackdown was highlighted by the takedown of two alleged kingpins of the illicit trade, Chen Zhi and Li Xiong, influential Chinese businessmen who had also become Cambodian citizens and were extradited earlier this year after their arrests.

Cambodian lawmakers unanimously adopted a new law in March targeting online scam operations with sentences of up to life in prison, following a government pledge to shut down the centers by the end of April.

articles.title: 5 Lessons Jasmine Curtis wants every girl to know
articles.summary: With an A-list actress for a sister in Anne Curtis, plus beauty, talent, and wit of her own, most people might think Jasmine Curtis simply has it all. But during World Vision’s #GirlsCan campaign…

blocks.text: Lifestyle | Youth
Through World Vision's #GirlsCan campaign, the actress reflects on the lessons she learned from her mother about finding her voice and claiming her space

With an A-list actress for a sister in Anne Curtis, plus beauty, talent, and wit of her own, most people might think Jasmine Curtis simply has it all. But during World Vision’s #GirlsCan campaign event at Gateway 1 Mall in Cubao last Aug. 22, Jasmine opened up about the barriers she faced and the woman who taught her that breaking them can create more possibilities for the next generation.
As a World Vision ambassador, Jasmine shared how her mother’s experiences shaped the way she and her sister learned to recognize their voices, set boundaries, and pursue their own dreams.
Here are five things to learn from Jasmine’s story.
1. Girls often learn expectations before they learn possibilities
Jasmine pointed out that gender bias can begin at home, sometimes through seemingly simple messages about what girls should or should not do.
“Before a girl learns what she wants, she learns what the world expects of her,” she said.
Repeated expectations can eventually become self-doubt, causing girls to believe that certain dreams, careers, or opportunities are meant for someone else.
2. Her mother became her first example of breaking barriers

For her, the first example of a woman breaking barriers was her mother. Coming from a humble background in Bolinao, Pangasinan, her mother, Carmen had to work early after her own mother became sick. She helped pay for her siblings’ education while putting her own dreams on the back burner.
Her mother also did not finish high school. This made education especially important to Jasmine’s family as she and Anne grew up.
“I learned by watching what my mom did when life didn't make things easy for her,” Jasmine said.
3. One woman’s choices can expand another girl’s possibilities
Jasmine said her mother eventually returned to school and work when she was already in her 40s. She later worked as a nurse aide in a hospital and eventually had her own agency.

Watching her mother make those choices changed how Jasmine viewed her own future. “My mother’s choice has expanded mine,” she said, explaining that her mother’s decision to pursue her own path allowed Jasmine and Anne to imagine more possibilities for themselves.
That example also showed her that a person’s journey does not have to end in one chapter.
4. Speaking up is part of claiming your space
Her mother also taught Jasmine that their voices matter. “We can say no and speak up if we are not treated right,” she said.

Jasmine connected this lesson to her own experience, sharing that she spoke up after receiving disrespectful treatment. For her, claiming space means knowing that girls and women can set boundaries and speak when something does not feel right.
5. Telling girls they can is not enough
The World Vision ambassador then emphasized that empowerment should go beyond simply telling girls to be courageous.
“Girls can’t just mean girls, try harder,” she said. “Because courage isn't enough if the doors were closed.”
She called on parents, teachers, employers, media, men, and women to help create environments where girls have access to education, safety, health information, protection, support, and opportunities.
“Our job isn't only to tell a girl that she can. Our job is to help build a world that doesn't keep telling her she can't,” Jasmine said.
Through World Vision’s #GirlsCan campaign, Jasmine hopes to inspire others to help create that kind of world, where girls can dream, choose, lead, and become who they want to be.

articles.title: Lacson bares 'fraudulently' titled parcels of reclaimed land in Taguig
articles.summary: Senator Panfilo Lacson said Saturday four parcels of illegally reclaimed land in Taguig City were initially identified as covered by "fraudulently" issued land titles, while no less than four other…

blocks.text: Published August 29, 2026 3:44pm

Senator Panfilo Lacson said Saturday four parcels of illegally reclaimed land in Taguig City were initially identified as covered by "fraudulently" issued land titles, while no less than four other parcels have no plotted title lots in the digital records of the Land Registration Authority (LRA).
In a post on X, Lacson said the details of the four alleged fraudulently titled parcels include:

items: one covered by an Administrative Patent, involving 9,204 square meters under an Original Certificate of Title (OCT);
one covered through Judicial/Ordinary Land Registration Processing covering an area of 5,000 square meters under an OCT;
one covered by a Homestead Patent involving 181,077 square meters under a Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT); and
one involving 193,027 square meters under a TCT.

blocks.text: He said he released the details to supposedly disprove claims that his earlier disclosures on the illegal reclamation activities in Taguig City were "fake news."
"Since Sen. (Alan Peter) Cayetano keeps publicly asking for evidence, I'll give it to him, in the spirit of public interest," Lacson said.
Lacson said certain details, including the names of those to whom the titles were issued to, and also the OCT and TCT numbers, were withheld for the time being while the investigation continues.
"All of these will likewise be turned over to the Ombudsman fact-finding team for their further appropriate action," Lacson said.
GMA News Online has reached out to the camp of Cayetano for comment but has yet to receive a reply as of posting time.

Previously, Lacson said the LRA is investigating the origin and history of several newly uncovered land titles covering some 38.83 hectares of illegally reclaimed areas on the Taguig City side of Laguna Lake.
The uncovered land titles were based on the materials provided by the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA) to his office.

"I requested the LRA to backtrack the history of the issued OCTs (original certificates of title) and other modes of titling, so we will find out how they were manipulated with the end in view of filing criminal charges against those responsible," the senator said.
Lacson added that the titles may be declared void ab initio (void from the start) once the PRA starts forfeiture proceedings in accordance with law.

He earlier said several crates of documents from the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) related to anomalous projects in Taguig City were also set to be turned over to the Office of the Ombudsman. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: DENR eyes private sector cooperation to curb garbage waste
articles.summary: DENR eyes private sector cooperation to curb garbage waste

blocks.text: Published August 29, 2026 3:41pm
The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) is eyeing private sector cooperation as one of the long-term solutions to address pollution in drainage systems and waterways.
The agency cited the use of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) and the Philippine Ecosystem and Natural Capital Accounting System (PENCAS) in this approach.

Under the Extended Producer Responsibility Act of 2022, large enterprises must take responsibility for the life cycle of their plastic wastes. They are responsible for the recovery of their plastic packaging waste.

“Dati ang solid waste management natin, puro local government lang 'yan, sila ang may mandato diyan. Pero ngayon dito, pinaigting natin 'yung private sector participation. Sila na ngayon ang nag-a-address ng mga plastic waste,” Environment Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna said.

(Before, our solid waste management system, it is all local government, they are the ones with that mandate. But here, we fortify private sector participation. They will now address the plastic waste.)

Meanwhile, the PENCAS creates a framework to account for the true value of natural resources and the ecosystem they serve. This would allow the government to recognize the environmental costs of damage.
The DENR said that it is utilizing 196 trash traps to collect floating waste, while mobilizing 1,500 estero rangers and rover warriors to monitor and clean esteros and rivers in Metro Manila.

“With government, businesses, local governments and the public working together, the Department is working to shift the focus from repeatedly cleaning up garbage to preventing improper waste management from becoming a recurring threat to waterways, communities and the environment,” Cuna said. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Meta sharing FB, IG, WhatsApp info to help PH probe threats
articles.summary: A commitment to the Philippine government to remove harmful artificial intelligence (AI)-generated deepfakes from its platforms and cooperate with investigations on cybercrime and other online…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A commitment to the Philippine government to remove harmful artificial intelligence (AI)-generated deepfakes from its platforms and cooperate with investigations on cybercrime and other online threats has been made by American technology firm Meta Platforms Inc., which owns Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp.

Meta policy officials handling the Asia-Pacific region met with a Philippine delegation on Thursday in Singapore to discuss details of the company’s commitment in the wake of violent incidents that local officials suspect stemmed from social media content.

Secretary Henry Aguda of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) was among those who attended the meeting with Director Melvin Matibag of the National Bureau of Investigation, Laguna Rep. Ann Matibag who chairs the House committee on women, and representatives from the office of Sen. Risa Hontiveros.

“We were able to convince Meta to commit to providing our authorities with subscriber information and traffic data once they identify a threat to the safety of our children, even before an actual attack takes place,” Hontiveros said in a video message on Friday.
Online risks

She said the “parallel development” will further gain traction for Senate Bill No. 2424, or the proposed Child Online Safety and Protection Act, which seeks to regulate children’s access to social media platforms. The bill sets 16 years as the minimum age for social media use.
SB 2424, which was sponsored in plenary on Wednesday, will also obligate social media companies to protect minors from various online risks.

In a Viber message to the Inquirer, Aguda outlined Meta’s commitment, including the establishment of a technical working group with the Philippine government to improve coordination, response times, and action on harmful content; the designation of a point of contact to facilitate faster response time; and the sharing of crucial data when necessary.
‘Good step’
Aguda said Meta also pledged continued cooperation with Philippine investigations, “particularly (on) cases involving imminent harm to children or risk of death or serious physical injury.”
A team from Meta is expected to visit Manila in mid-September to formalize the framework and commitments made.
Senate President Sherwin “Win” Gatchalian welcomed the development as a “good step.”
But it doesn’t mean that the Senate will no longer push for SB 2424, which also proposes that Meta set up a Philippine office, he told the Inquirer in a phone interview.
“So if there’s a problem, we can easily coordinate with them and we can prevent future problems,” he said.

Gatchalian added that a bill will make it easier to penalize social media companies for violations, citing the case in the United States where Meta was slapped with a multistate lawsuit accusing it of intentionally designing addictive social media platforms that harm children’s mental health.
The company entered into a landmark $18-billion settlement this month to resolve the cases.
But because there is no law in the Philippines yet, he said, it would be difficult to make social media companies accountable for harmful content.

“For example, what happened in Zamboanga, the was uploaded and they did not stop it. They could be penalized [if a law exists],” Gatchalian said. The senator was referring to the video of the Ateneo de Zamboanga University shooting earlier this month that was uploaded on Facebook but was not immediately taken down.

The livestream of the deadly incident remained online for about 14 minutes, according to reports. It stayed for five minutes before the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) flagged it and notified Meta, which took approximately four minutes to take it off the platform’s video feed.
Agreeing with Gatchalian, Sen. Erwin Tulfo said “we still have to craft a law for all social media apps—to penalize them. We penalize all of them if they fail to follow their community standards.”

According to the CICC, which was also represented at the Singapore meeting, Meta will “readily provide the credentials and relevant data of users behind online sexual abuse and exploitation of children, child sexual abuse and exploitation material, obscene content and other forms of online abuse.”
Deepfakes

The CICC said the requested data will be provided once the NBI issues a subpoena, subject to legal requirements and applicable laws. This is intended to help investigators identify perpetrators behind online offenses and build up cases against them more quickly.
The CICC noted that one of the critical results of the talks was the establishment of a stronger mechanism for addressing AI-generated content, specifically deepfakes.

“This is an important step forward because it gives us a more preemptive layer of protection. We look forward to working with Meta so that individuals who are targeted by deepfakes can receive assistance before the content causes further damage,” CICC Executive Director Renato Paraiso said.
Under the proposed mechanism, individuals may apply for protection, allowing Meta to identify and remove deepfake content targeting them.
Harmful online content involving minors, including videos of the fatal school shootings in Zamboanga and Tacloban cities, has led to calls to ban Meta in the Philippines.
But with the social media giant now agreeing to cooperate, Paraiso said in a statement, “For now, banning is the last option.”
“We now have concrete areas of cooperation, and we are looking forward to seeing these turn into actual improvements in online safety for Filipinos, especially for our children,” he added.

Meta’s Facebook remains the top social media platform in the country, with 95.8 million users as of late 2025. This represents an 81.9-percent reach of the total population and 97.7 percent of the country’s internet users.

articles.title: Europe’s monarchs, world leaders mourn Norway’s King Harald
articles.summary: OSLO, Norway — European monarchs and world leaders paid tribute Friday to Norway’s King Harald after the royal palace announced his death at age 89. Harald was the continent’s oldest…

blocks.text: OSLO, Norway — European monarchs and world leaders paid tribute Friday to Norway’s King Harald after the royal palace announced his death at age 89.
Harald was the continent’s oldest reigning monarch. His son, Haakon, automatically succeeded him to the throne.
Here are some of the main tributes:
Britain’s King Charles
Britain’s King Charles III hailed his “dear cousin,” who he said had served “with unwavering dedication, guiding Norway through times of great change with warmth and humility.”

“As Norway mourns the loss of so towering a figure, my whole family join in remembering a much-loved kinsman and friend whose kindness, compassion and deep sense of duty echoed from across the sea and across the decades,” the king said in a statement personally signed Charles R.
Danish and Swedish monarchs
The kings of Denmark and Sweden called Harald an “extraordinary” leader and good friend who unified his country.
“Both as head of state and a successful athlete, he was an outstanding representative of his country. He gave ‘All for Norway,'” Sweden’s King Carl XVI Gustaf said, referring to Harald’s royal motto.
Denmark’s King Frederik X said the late monarch was “an extraordinary man” who “joined duty and responsibility with presence and compassion.”
Dutch royal family

The Dutch royal family recalled “unforgettable” journeys with King Harald around Oslo and the rest of Norway. “We cherish the memory of our special friendship with him in our hearts. King Harald served his country with love, pride, and conviction,” the family said in a statement.
Belgian royals
Harald’s “humour, humanity and sincerity made him a truly special man,” Belgium’s King Philippe and Queen Mathilde said.

“Generations of Norwegians grew up with him. For decades, he was a familiar and reassuring presence, a beacon of stability for his country. He fulfilled his role with unwavering dedication, loyalty and dignity,” they said in a statement.
Spain’s royal family
Spain’s royal family hailed King Harald as an “example of responsibility, dignity, simplicity, and tireless dedication to the service” of his country.
“With respect and admiration for him, as well as deep sadness, we offer our condolences” on the king’s death, they wrote on social media.
Jordan’s royal family
Jordan’s Royal Hashemite Court said it mourned the passing of King Harald, “may his soul rest in peace.”
The court “expresses the deepest sympathies of His Majesty and the Jordanian people, as they stand with Norway and its people at this difficult time.”
King Abdullah ordered his court to observe three days of mourning, a statement from the court added.
UN chief
A spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was “deeply saddened” by the king’s death.
“He will be remembered for his engagement for children’s welfare and environmental issues, his support for diversity and calls for generosity,” the statement added.
NATO, EU chiefs
Harald “showed himself to be a dedicated leader,” Mark Rutte, head of the NATO alliance that includes Norway, posted.
“His own military roots made him a champion of the Norwegian military and a long-time friend of NATO,” he wrote online.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said that Harald “served his country with warmth, humility and an unwavering sense of duty.”
French president

Harald “worked tirelessly throughout his reign to strengthen the ties uniting Norway and France,” French President Emmanuel Macron wrote on X, recalling a “warm welcome” on his visit to Oslo in June 2025.
Ukraine’s president
“His Majesty embodied dignity, wisdom, and an unwavering commitment to his country,” said Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in a statement.
“Ukraine will always remember his steadfast support and solidarity with the Ukrainian people during the darkest days of Russia’s aggression.”
Canada’s PM
“Canada mourns with you,” said a statement from Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, offering the condolences of his government.
“I had the privilege of meeting his Majesty last March in Oslo, and he spoke of the ties between our nations with great warmth and affection.”
Italy’s PM

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, in a post on X, called Harald “a monarch who served his nation with equanimity, authority and a deep sense of institutional duty, helping to strengthen the ties between Norway and Italy throughout his long reign.”
Israeli president
Israeli President Isaac Herzog hailed the “loyalty and devotion” of Harald, who early in his reign supported the landmark Oslo Accords between Israel and the Palestinians.
Swiss president
Swiss President Guy Parmelin wrote on X that Harald “will be remembered for his steadfast leadership and devoted service to his country.” /das

articles.title: ‘Tinimbang Ka Ngunit Kulang,’ ‘Sister Stella L’ to lead PFIM 2026 screenings
articles.summary: With the theme “Pelikula: Ginintuang Ikalawa,” this year’s celebration of the Philippine Film Industry Month (PFIM) will feature screenings of digitally restored classics including Lino…

blocks.text: With the theme “Pelikula: Ginintuang Ikalawa,” this year’s celebration of the Philippine Film Industry Month (PFIM) will feature screenings of digitally restored classics including Lino Brocka’s “Tinimbang Ka Ngunit Kulang” and Mike de Leon’s “Sister Stella L,” among others.
The Film Development Council of the Philippines (FDCP) announced PFIM’s monthlong activities that celebrate the 50th anniversary of the Second Golden Age of Philippine Cinema.

The screening of “Tinimbang Ka Ngunit Kulang” will kick off the celebration at the Red Carpet Cinema, Shangri-La Plaza on Sept. 4, along with the announcement of the Philippines’ entry to the 2027 Oscars Best International Feature Film category.

Other digitally restored classics — including de Leon’s “Itim,” Brocka’s “Insiang,” Mario O’Hara’s “Tatlong Taong Walang Diyos,” Lupita Aquino-Kashiwahara’s “Minsa’y Isang Gamu-Gamo,” Eddie Romero’s “Ganito Kami Noon… Paano Kayo Ngayon?” and Ishmael Bernal’s “Nunal sa Tubig” — will be showcased throughout the month at FDCP Cinematheque Centres nationwide.

The audiences will also be taken further back in time with the “SineUna: Cinematic Action Before the War,” which will feature Eduardo de Castro’s “Zamboanga,” Carlos Vander Tolosa’s “Giliw Ko,” Vicente Salumbide’s “Ibong Adarna” and Octavio Silos’ “Tunay na Ina” and “Pakiusap.”

Meanwhile, the newly digitally-restored “Sister Stella L” will have its grand homecoming on Sept. 20 at the Metropolitan Theater as part of the “Mga Hiyas ng Sineng Pilipino,” which is co-presented by the National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA).

Other key PFIM 2026 events include the “Reel to Real: Pelikula at Panayam,” which will spotlight Brocka’s “Jaguar”; the Director’s Series, which will feature Jeffrey Jeturian’s “Tuhog” and “Kubrador”; the world premiere of Mike Alcazaren’s documentary film “Kodomo-tachi: Children of the War” on Sept. 17; the inaugural edition of the PFIM Short Film Competition; Sine Kabataan 2026; and the return of the Film Education Convention (FilmEc).
The PFIM 2026 will conclude with a closing ceremony on Sept. 30. /ra

articles.title: South Korea leans toward military conscription for women
articles.summary: Facing a population decline, fewer potential service members and calls for social equality to be extended to national military service, Korea is inching closer to breaking the taboo on women on the…

image.caption: South Korea's armed forces are experiencing significant personnel shortagesImage: Xinhua/IMAGO

blocks.text: Nearly 60% of South Koreans are now in favor of young women serving mandatory military service alongside their male counterparts, according to a recent survey, representing a significant shift in the long-held taboo against women being obliged to defend the nation.
Thousands of women already serve in the South Korean armed forces on a voluntary basis, but the debate over mandatory service has always been delicate.

Now, for a series of reasons that include a falling birth rate and shrinking number of recruits as well as an insistence that social equality means that women should also serve, the issue has re-emerged ahead of a reform of the national defense plan scheduled to be released this autumn.
Yet, there are still those who insist women should be kept away from the front lines and, instead, that South Korea should invest more in drones and other advanced technologies.
"South Korea's male-centered conscription system has long been closely connected to traditional gender roles," said Hyobin Lee, a professor at Sogang University in Seoul.

"Men were generally expected to protect the country and the family and to fight in wartime, while women were expected to take primary responsibility for childbirth, childcare and the household," she told DW.
A second factor is the intensifying debate about gender equality, a debate in large part driven by young men, she said.
Warfare moves beyond the physical
"South Korean men generally perform their military service in their early 20s, which interrupts their education, employment or early career development," Lee said.
"At the same time, gender equality has become an increasingly important social value, and women's opportunities in education and employment have expanded."

"As a result, some younger men ask a very simple question: If society expects equality in rights and opportunities, why does one of the country's most significant civic obligations — military service — still fall only on men?"
South Korea proposes talks to officially end war with North

Another contributing factor is the change in the nature of the military itself, with a shift away from physically demanding combat roles that were perceived as being more suited to men and the emergence of a national defense more heavily reliant on technology.
This includes unmanned systems, cyber capabilities, information and communications technology and others that do not require physical strength.
What does the study show?

According to the study, carried out by the Reform Institute, the policy research arm of the conservative-leaning Reform Party, and published on August 20, almost 60% of the respondents were in favor of changing the law to require women to undergo national service. Just 34% were opposed to the idea.
Nearly 65% of men were in favor — a figure that rose to 71.7% among men in their 20s and 30s — with 54.5% of women across all age groups similarly supportive.

At present, all able-bodied men are required to complete a minimum of 18 months and up to 21 months of service and can be called back into service in the event of a national emergency, such as war breaking out on the tense Korean Peninsula.
The latest figures highlight, however, personnel shortages that have affected South Korea's armed forces.

According to the Defense Ministry, around 332,000 men were eligible to perform mandatory military service in 2019. That number fell to 257,000 men in 2022 and is forecast to shrink to just 120,000 men in 2043.

While Hyobin Lee is strongly in favor of equality throughout South Korean society, she fears that obliging women to serve the same military terms as men may turn out to be a negative because so many other elements in society still lag.
Women's traditional responsibilities remain unchanged
"Women in South Korea still bear a much greater share of the responsibilities associated with pregnancy, childbirth and childcare," she underlined.

"Having a child can still lead to career interruption or withdrawal from the labor market, and women's responsibilities for caregiving have not declined to the same extent that their participation in education and employment has increased," Lee added.
Korean 'comfort women' memorial angers Japan
"If women were also required to complete military service, the cumulative burden across their life course could become even greater," she pointed out.
"In a country that is already experiencing an extremely low birth rate, it is also possible that this additional compulsory obligation could further delay or discourage marriage and childbirth."
Lee comes from a family with a strong military background, with a grandfather an admiral in the navy and her father serving in the same branch of the military.
But she would have had reservations in completing mandatory service herself.
"If someone chooses a military career, that is completely different from compulsory service," she said.

"Eighteen months in your 20s is a very significant period in a person's life. It is a time when people are studying, beginning their careers, and making important personal choices. Having to put all of that on hold because the state requires it is a substantial burden," she said.
"Personally, I would have found it extremely difficult to give up 18 months of my younger years in that way."

Song Young-Chae, a Seoul-based academic and human rights activist, completed two years in the infantry as a younger man, when periods of service were longer. He is opposed to mandatory service for women.
"The defense of the nation is traditionally the responsibility of men, and I do not believe that there is such an urgent need to conscript women into front-line service," he told DW.
Need to invest in modern technology

"I served along the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) with North Korea, and it was a hard posting," he added. "I believe that we should be investing far more in drones, robots and other advanced military technologies to protect our borders."
How China's rise is shaping Trump's strategy in Asia

The South Korean government set up a task force in 2025 to revise the nation's basic defense plan, with troop modernization and an overhaul of the conscription system — introduced in the 1950s — high on the agenda.

In an interview with the Yonhap News Agency on August 9, Military Manpower Commissioner Hong So-young admitted that the nation faces a "demographic cliff" and that reforms are urgently required. Those include potentially reducing the number of people exempt from service and requiring foreign-born people who have taken South Korean nationality to also serve.
Hong made no comment about mandatory service for Korean women, but said the system needs a "fundamental" overhaul.

articles.title: This extremely successful author polarizes German readers
articles.summary: She's young and she says what she thinks: Caroline Wahl is topping Germany's bestseller lists with her novels. But she has also faced a public backlash.

image.caption: Author Caroline Wahl, shown here at the 2026 German Film Awards, has topped Germany's bestseller listsImage: Sebastian Christoph Gollnow/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Caroline Wahl, 31, has published three novels to date. All three shot to the top of Germany's fiction bestseller lists.

Now, her fourth book is set to be released on August 28: "1999 Meter über dem Meer" (1999 Meters Above Sea) tells the story of a young woman who takes on a false identity to mingle among the high society in St. Moritz, Switzerland.
It is one of the most anticipated new books of the summer in Germany.
So what is the secret to Caroline Wahl's success?
Debut with a bang
Wahl's breakthrough came with her first novel, in 2023: "22 Bahnen" (22 Lengths) sold more than a million copies in German-language editions.
The story of the young student Tilda, who has to navigate everyday life alongside her alcoholic mother and her little sister, was praised by critics for its straightforward, modern writing style.
What's more, the novel managed to fascinate readers across generations, including references to contemporary pop culture as well as to classic literature.

"The many references make the novels both diverse and ambiguous," said Matthias Schaffrick, a research associate at the Collaborative Research Center "Transformations of the Popular" at the University of Siegen, who recently organized a two-day symposium on Wahl's works.

"What stands out most is how she experiments with different narrative styles and questions them, instead of simply telling a story," Shaffrick told DW. "This opens up a literary space with multiple possibilities, enabling different interpretations and certainly contributing to the appeal of her novels for many readers."
Polarizing ambition

The book's success led to media interest in the young author, and quickly showed that Wahl does not care much for conventions. She speaks her mind freely and doesn't mind facing backlash. "I enjoy being polarizing," she told the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper in late August. "I like that there's no gray area, people either hate me, and then they really hate me [...]. Or they like me."

In the podcast "Hotel Matze," she said she wanted to become one of Germany's most famous authors. Her words quickly created a stir, but Wahl didn't mind. "I'm really not up for false modesty. It's not wrong to state your goals ambitiously," she said on the arts and culture TV show "Twist" on the Arte channel. "For young women in particular, it's more extreme than for men — people get irritated when a young woman says, 'I want to be the best.' I want to change that with my attitude."
A passion for fast cars

Part of that is openly speaking about enjoying her newfound wealth. In an interview with SZ-Magazin, Wahl said: "It's not only the writing that is enjoyable, but also being successful. Financial success is also important." She loves fast cars, drives a convertible and bought a camper van she likes to park somewhere with a view of the sea to work.

On social media, Wahl has faced a lot of criticism. She has been accused of making money off the literary depiction of poverty in "22 Bahnen," despite never having lived an impoverished life herself. It's an age-old discussion about whether authors are only allowed to write about things they have experienced themselves. Wahl replied to this criticism on the Deutschlandfunk radio station, explaining that above all, writing to her means "exploring spaces that I don't know and feeling empathy for people who live a different life than mine."

blocks.caption: Wahl is no fan of false modestyImage: Felix Hörhager/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: But even without the debate on her credibility, a young woman who speaks openly about material success still seems to be unsettling for many people in Germany — men and women alike — as the many negative reactions show. To Wahl herself, the debate is misogynist.

On Instagram, she wrote a caption for a photo of her light blue BMW: "I find it weird and don't quite get why it's cool for rappers or other men to show off their AMGs, etc., but when a woman author wants to buy a sports car (and can afford to do so!!!), people advise her not to do it and more importantly, not to show it in public."
Author and influencer

"What happens when something becomes very popular?" asked literary scholar Schaffrick. "The popularity starts being scrutinized, which you can observe in Caroline Wahl's case. And we can see what it means to be a popular author. It's not only her novels that play a role, but also the persona she creates for herself as an author."

By being active on Instagram, where she has even tested energy drinks, Wahl also taps into the role of an influencer, said Schaffrick. "It makes her even more popular and offers new topics for conversation. At the same time, the public debate shifts the focus away from her literature, which is what's actually interesting about the Caroline Wahl phenomenon."

Wahl herself has admitted that the intensity of the backlash and criticism has hurt her. In an interview with the SWR TV channel, she explained that social criticism is not necessarily her intention. "I'm not trying to change anything with my stories. Above all, I want to tell stories."
'22 Lengths' on school curricula

When it comes to bestsellers, opinions always differ among German literary critics: Is this entertaining literature, or serious literature with high artistic aspirations? The arts and feature sections of numerous newspapers have come to different conclusions on whether Wahl's novels can be classified as part of the latter. In an interview with Spiegel, Wahl said she finds "drawing a line between entertaining and serious simply annoying."

So far, Wahl's novels have not been nominated for the German Book Prize, Germany's highest literature award. In 2024, the writer voiced her disappointment in typical fashion on Instagram: "I'm sad and angry that I have not been included on the longlist, even if I somehow knew this would happen. Too successful, says my agent."
Back then, her debut novel could have been included on the list — a book that was quickly added to school curricula and has now been made into a film.

Likewise, Wahl's novel "Die Assistentin" ("The Assistant") has not been included on this year's longlist. A literature critic from Frankfurter Rundschau had this to say about the decision: "Why is good literature always supposed to hurt before it can be deemed 'valuable'? [...] The fact that an author like Wahl has been ignored, simply because her captivating writing fascinates millions of readers, makes me really angry."
Presumably, Wahl's fans will ensure that her new novel becomes another bestseller — even without the German Book Prize.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: Serbia keeps EU, Russia in play ahead of key election
articles.summary: As Serbia heads toward an uncertain election, President Aleksandar Vucic is balancing ties with Russia and EU ambitions. But growing geopolitical tensions and pressure at home are narrowing his room…

image.caption: Aleksandar Vucic is trying to balance Serbia's ties with the EU and RussiaImage: Djordje Kojadinovic/REUTERS

blocks.text: Smoke from the wildfires still hangs over parts of Serbia, but as the flames slowly recede another debate is taking shape in their wake — one that has less to do with firefighting and more with politics.

In early August, wildfires swept across Serbia, burning through more than 3,500 hectares (8,600 acres) in the Deliblato Sands Special Nature Reserve. Firefighters, soldiers and helicopters battled the flames for days.

blocks.caption: Serbia turned to Russia for help in fighting wildfires in the Deliblato Sands Special Nature ReserveImage: Marko Dimic/ZUMA/picture alliance

blocks.text: Then a Russian Ilyushin Il-76 firefighting aircraft arrived in the southern city of Nis. Serbia had turned to Moscow for help, making Russia the first foreign country it asked to provide a firefighting aircraft. Pro-government media greeted its arrival with celebratory coverage, dubbing the aircraft the "Russian beast."

"Considering that there are no firefighting aircraft of this capacity available within the European Union, the arriving Russian aircraft will significantly strengthen our capacities to fight the fires," said Luka Causic, head of the Serbian Interior Ministry's Department for Emergency Situations.
A pragmatic choice between EU, Russia — or a political signal?
The episode, however, was already being viewed through a geopolitical lens, as Serbia had sought Russian assistance before activating the EU's emergency mechanism.

When it did call on the EU, the response was swift. Brussels mobilized four helicopters from its strategic rescEU reserve, based in Czechia, Romania and Slovakia, along with ground firefighting teams from Germany and Romania.

blocks.caption: Emergency services, including German firefighters, were on hand to help Serbia battle wildfiresImage: Feuerwehr Bonn/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: President Aleksandar Vucic rejected the idea that turning to Russia first was a foreign-policy decision or a sign of Serbia's political alignment with Moscow.

"As far as equipment and resources are concerned, we are a European giant. The helicopters we received from Europe to fight the fires are less capable than ours and have a lower carrying capacity than our own," Vucic said during a visit to the Deliblato Sands.
Zelenskyy in Belgrade
The wildfire episode came less than two weeks after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made his first official visit to Serbia.

The two presidents reaffirmed their support for each other's territorial integrity, which is particularly significant for Belgrade because Ukraine does not recognize the independence of Kosovo . Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008, which Belgrade still does not recognize.
But Vucic is also trying to keep the other side on board, said Vuk Vuksanovic, a political scientist and foreign policy lecturer at King's College London.

Vuksanovic argues that Vucic's engagement with Zelenskyy must therefore be portrayed in Moscow not as a fundamental shift in Serbia's relationship with Russia, but as a response to Western pressure and Serbia's own interests.
"Vucic is now trying to make sure that neither the West nor Russia becomes an open opponent during the election campaign," said Vuksanovic.

"Zelenskyy was primarily received so that the ruling coalition could present itself to Europeans as a great friend of Ukraine. In the same way, Vucic is trying to present himself to the Trump administration as a great friend of Israel, primarily to ensure that neither the European Union nor the United States becomes an opponent of the ruling party during the election campaign," he added.
Vucic's room to maneuver is shrinking
The problem is that the room to maintain these relationships may be shrinking.
The deeper the confrontation between Russia and the West becomes, the harder it is for Serbia to remain close to both without facing pressure to choose.

The European Union increasingly expects candidate countries to align their foreign and security policies with those of the bloc. Serbia's refusal to impose sanctions on Russia remains one of the most visible obstacles to closer alignment.

But Moscow, too, has reasons not to take Belgrade's loyalty for granted, Vuksanovic said. He argued that Russia does not fully trust Vucic, even as Moscow continues to support his narrative about "color revolutions" — a reference to anti-government protests, in this case the student-led protests in Serbia that gathered pace in early 2025. Vucic and Russia have both portrayed the protests as Western-backed attempts to destabilize the government.

For Vucic, however, the longer-term question of Serbia's ties with Russia can wait. The more immediate question is whether he will survive the election, tentatively scheduled for October, and remain in a position to preserve that delicate balance himself.

articles.title: Ex-White House teleprompter operator ordered to pay $172,000 for Trump speech bets
articles.summary: The staffer was found to have used his prior knowledge of the president's speeches to place lucrative bets.

blocks.text: A former White House teleprompter operator has been ordered to pay more than $172,000 (£127,000) for using inside information to bet on Donald Trump's speeches.

Gabriel Perez was found to have made trades concerning what the US president would say during addresses between December 2025 and February 2026 on Kalshi - a prediction markets platform where users can bet on real-world events.
Its regulator, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), said Perez would have to surrender profits of $107,539.02 and pay a civil penalty of $65,000.
The White House has not yet commented. In July, then-press secretary Karoline Leavitt said Perez was on unpaid leave and would not return to his post.
Announcing the settlement on Friday, the CFTC said Perez had "misappropriated" his prior knowledge of Trump's speeches to place bets "in breach of his duty of trust and confidence".
It said his civil penalty had been reduced due to his "exemplary co-operation" with the investigation.
Perez has also been banned from trading for three years.
Kalshi's lead lawyer Bobby DeNault welcomed the decision, writing on X: "It doesn't matter who you are: violate our rules or federal law and you will face the consequences."

The company previously told the BBC that its analysts had noticed unusual betting on "mention markets" – contracts through which users predict whether a speaker will use common terms, such as specific countries, campaign slogans or words – in March.
It said it had used account data to find that the user had been a federal employee operating White House teleprompters, and reported the activity to the regulator.
"The words of political leaders like presidents and Fed chairs cause billions of dollars of movement in FX markets, oil futures [and] the stock market," it said in a statement in July.
The same month, the White House Management Office had sent a letter to aides telling them not to place bets on prediction markets, administration officials told the BBC's US media partner CBS News.

articles.title: Sarah Geronimo madbos? Matteo nakadawat og ‘soon-to-be daddy’ greeting
articles.summary: Mga netizens naghunahuna nga mabdos si Sarah Geronimo human ang iyang asawa, ang aktor nga si Matteo Guidicelli, nakadawat og “soon-to-be daddy” congratulatory greeting sa usa ka nagpa-ila nga amigo.…

blocks.text: Mga netizens naghunahuna nga mabdos si Sarah Geronimo human ang iyang asawa, ang aktor nga si Matteo Guidicelli, nakadawat og “soon-to-be daddy” congratulatory greeting sa usa ka nagpa-ila nga amigo.

Usa ka Facebook user, nga amigo ni Guidicelli, ang nag-post og hulagway nila sa aktor nga karon gi-delete na. Matod pa niya, kuha ang maong photo dihang nag-abot sila sa usa ka coffee shop sa Quezon City

“Deep in a meeting with a colleague, totally unaware someone familiar was right there until Gianmatteo Guidecilli walked up and said, ‘ka-ila gyud ko ani!’ (I know this person!)” segon pa sa giingon amigo. “Truly caught me by surprise! So many shared memories with Matt —from shoots, Airborne Proficiency Jumps, and our days at ISAFP. Solid guy — hindi mayabang, sobrang friendly pa.”

(Sa ka focus nako sa usa ka meeting sa akong kauban, wala ko kabantay nga naa koy kaiila nga naa sa [cafe] hangtod nidoul siya ug nag-sulti, ‘Ka-ila man gyod ko ani! […] Tinoud nakuratan ko! Daghan kaayo mig kaagi ni Matt — gikan sa mga shoots, Airborne Proficiency Jumps, ug sa among mga adlaw sa ISAFP. Saligan gyud na nga tawo — di hambugero, ug friendly pa gyod kaayo.)
“P.S. He is soon to be a daddy. Congratulations, bro!” sulti pas user. (Hapit na siya mahimong daddy. Pahalipay, bro!)
Gitubag sab sa maong user ang usa sa mga komento sa iyang post, diin giingon niya nga si Guidicelli mismo ang miingon ug nagkumpirma nga mabdos si Geronimo.
Sarah Geronimo, Matteo Guidicelli hilom pa
Sa pagkaron, si Guidicelli ug Geronimo — nga nagpakasal niadtong 2020 — wala pa mohatag og kumpirmasyon o pag-deny sa mga tsismis bahin sa pagmabdos.
Ang aktres ug singer nagsaulog sa iyang ika-38 nga adlaw nga natawhan pinaagi sa pagpakig-uban pag-usab sa iyang mga ginikanan nga sila Delfin ug Divine Geronimo.

articles.title: Over 1,000 Olongapo City folk forced to evacuate due flooding
articles.summary: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — Over 1,000 Olongapo City residents were forced to seek shelter in safer, higher areas on Saturday as widespread flooding hounded the city amid persistent monsoon rains. Data…

blocks.text: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — Over 1,000 Olongapo City residents were forced to seek shelter in safer, higher areas on Saturday as widespread flooding hounded the city amid persistent monsoon rains.
Data from the Olongapo City Information Center showed that 1,395 individuals from 452 families were staying in evacuation centers as of 9:30 a.m. Saturday.
Some affected residents were forced to stay outside designated evacuation centers, according to city authorities.
Flooding also left residents stranded in several parts of the city on Friday night as water levels in rivers continued to rise and eventually reached spilling levels.
The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said the southwest monsoon or “habagat”, continued to affect Luzon, including Olongapo City.
Pagasa is also monitoring a low-pressure area located 520 kilometers north-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes as of Saturday.
Zambales was among areas forecast to receive 100 to 200 millimeters of rainfall from Saturday to Monday, according to Pagasa.
Photos provided by Olongapo City Mayor Rolen Paulino Jr. showed residents stranded by floodwaters in several parts of the city on Friday night.

articles.title: Trump to mark 9/11 at Pentagon, not New York
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, United States — US President Donald Trump said Friday he would mark the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, attacks at the Pentagon — but angrily denied skipping a memorial in New…

blocks.text: WASHINGTON, United States — US President Donald Trump said Friday he would mark the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, attacks at the Pentagon — but angrily denied skipping a memorial in New York because of a row over a speech.

The New York Times reported that Trump originally intended to commemorate the day with remarks at the site of the Twin Towers but changed his plans because the memorial’s organizers do not allow speeches.
Asked by reporters why he was not going to New York for the anniversary, Trump replied: “Because I’m going to the Pentagon.”
When asked why he could not attend both locations, Trump repeated his answer.
The 9/11 attacks killed nearly 3,000 people.

Hijackers from the Islamist Al-Qaeda network crashed two airliners into the Twin Towers in New York and a third into the Pentagon near Washington, while a fourth plane crashed in a field in Pennsylvania after a revolt by the passengers.
The White House told AFP that Vice President JD Vance was “still traveling” to New York and said that “all three sites will be represented with administration officials in attendance.”

“On the 25th anniversary of this tragic day, the President will remember those who were killed at the hands of evil terrorists, honor their loved ones, and pay tribute to the brave first responders who put their lives on the line to rescue their fellow Americans,” White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said in a statement.
The Pentagon declined to comment.
Trump had earlier issued a lengthy social media post slamming The New York Times report, with a harsh, renewed attack on one of its journalists, Maggie Haberman, whom he called “Maggot Hagerman.”
“This is more Corrupt News, I’ve been to New York many times over the years, and no one ever speaks, it’s a ‘solemn ceremony!'” Trump said on his Truth Social network. /das

“I never even thought of what Maggot made up, and besides, I would love not to speak, because I’m speaking all the time, and this is a day to remember the victims, and their beautiful family members.”

articles.title: US judge throws out confessions of alleged 9/11 mastermind — report
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, United States — A US military judge ruled Friday that confessions made by alleged 9/11 attacks mastermind Khalid Sheikh Mohammed to FBI agents are inadmissible and cannot be used against…

blocks.text: WASHINGTON, United States — A US military judge ruled Friday that confessions made by alleged 9/11 attacks mastermind Khalid Sheikh Mohammed to FBI agents are inadmissible and cannot be used against him at trial, The New York Times reported.
The ruling comes just before the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks that killed nearly 3,000 people in New York, Washington and Pennsylvania.
This week, the trial date for Mohammed and three other alleged plotters was set for June 5, 2028, at the US naval base in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba.
Mohammed, also known as “KSM,” was considered one of Al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden’s top lieutenants before he was captured in March 2003 in Pakistan.

Prosecutors have already excluded statements that Mohammed made after his capture when he was held by the CIA in overseas prisons and subjected to brutal treatment, including waterboarding, before his transfer in 2006 to Guantanamo, the Times reported.
But the trial judge, Lt. Col. Michael Schrama, has concluded that Mohammed’s subsequent interrogations in 2007 at Guantanamo were also inadmissible.

“The prosecution has failed to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that Mr. Mohammed’s statements to the FBI were voluntarily given,” Schrama wrote in his ruling, which was not immediately released to the public. The Times said its unclassified contents were confirmed by several lawyers who had seen it.
A spokesman for the US military court did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment.

Schrama cited an “unbroken continuation of the CIA’s psychological conditioning and severe coercion,” and also found that FBI agents intentionally failed to tell Mohammed that he had a right to remain silent and to consult a lawyer.
Prosecutors can appeal the ruling.

Mohammed’s trial has been repeatedly delayed, and a plea deal that would have seen the death penalty taken off the table was withdrawn last year following protests from the relatives of some victims of the 9/11 attacks.
Much of the legal jousting in the 9/11 defendants’ cases has focused on whether they could be tried fairly after having undergone torture at the hands of the CIA. /das

articles.title: Sabalenka shrugs off recent struggles, seeks 3rd straight US Open title
articles.summary: NEW YORK — Aryna Sabalenka has appeared to be having fun everywhere but the tennis court lately. Her Instagram account is filled with photos where she is fashionably dressed in beautiful settings, or…

blocks.text: Aryna Sabalenka, of Belarus, returns the ball during a mixed doubles match at the U.S. Open tennis championships, Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura)
NEW YORK — Aryna Sabalenka has appeared to be having fun everywhere but the tennis court lately.
Her Instagram account is filled with photos where she is fashionably dressed in beautiful settings, or lounging in a bikini in relaxing ones. Life looks great.
On the court, it’s as bad as it’s been in a while.

The top-ranked women’s player hasn’t even gotten past the fourth round of her last few tournaments, and she hardly looks ready to become the first player to win three straight U.S. Open titles since Serena Williams from 2012-14.
Sabalenka doesn’t sound concerned. She sounds defiant.
Her response to those wondering what’s wrong with her game: “Maybe there’s something wrong with people,” she said.
To those who don’t like the black mesh-covered outfit she’s wearing on the court in New York: “Who cares about people, right? All matters for me is that I love it,” Sabalenka responded.

Sabalenka looked headed for a superb season at the start of the year. She lost in the Australian Open final to Elena Rybakina, but then won back-to-back hard-court titles at Indian Wells and Miami. Even after she was knocked out by Naomi Osaka in the fourth round at Wimbledon, it was assumed Sabalenka would quickly return to form when she came back to North America and the hard courts where her power is so tough to handle.

Then she was upset by Ekaterina Alexandrova in the fourth round in Toronto and blew leads in both sets and was ousted by Sara Bejlek in Cincinnati, appearing frustrated at times with her game the way she used to earlier in her career.
She won’t specify what was wrong, but hinted that everything wasn’t right.
“It wasn’t the best period. I don’t want to defend myself, but obviously I just don’t want to talk about that period. I’ve been dealing with several things,” Sabalenka said.

“But who cares, right? Yeah, I didn’t perform my best. These tough lessons are definitely going to make me way, way stronger and working even harder. I work on my mental side of the game. I was trying to reset my mind and to come back stronger, so it’s only going to make me stronger. It’s only a matter of time for me to come back.”
It wouldn’t be a surprise if it was in New York, where she won the title for the first time in 2024 by beating Jessica Pegula in the final. She defended it last year by topping Amanda Anisimova.
Reaching the top has given the 28-year-old from Belarus plenty of benefits off the court. Endorsement deals and photo shoots. Vacations during the season to Greece with her fiance.
It gives critics who see Sabalenka detail all of that on social media the opportunity to question whether it’s too much fun and not enough work.
“She’s still No. 1 in the world. So I think the results are there,” said Paula Badosa, Sabalenka’s friend on tour who has been pictured in some of those photos with her.

“Of course, everyone is going to expect for her to win every tournament. That’s very, very difficult. And at the moment, that one player is not winning what they expected. Of course, they’re saying that it’s because of the photo shoots or the TikToks and all this stuff, and I’m not going to lie, she’s been doing that since she was maybe out of the top 100. And when she was winning, nobody says anything, you know? And when she loses a couple of matches, it’s because of that. I think it’s none of it.”
The No. 1 ranking is in jeopardy after Sabalenka’s summer swoon. She may need to make a deep run in New York with the likes of Rybakina and Pegula gaining on her.
Sabalenka has done it before. She may be down now but doesn’t sound like she plans to stay there.
“Well, that’s the beauty of the sport,” she said. “Throw tough challenges at me, I will come back only stronger.”
